TL;DR - POSITIONS MENTIONED



BULLISH: Brent Oil (BNO); Japanese Yen (JPY); Healthcare (XLV); Consumer Staples (XLP).



BEARISH: South Korean Semiconductors / SK Hynix (ticker unspecified); South Korea (KOSPI); Russell 2000 (IWM); iShares iBoxx $ High Yield Corporate Bond ETF (HYG); Goldman Sachs (GS); Meta Platforms (META); India (INDA), Indonesia (IDX), Philippines (EPHE), Germany (EWG), France (EWQ); BitMine Immersion Technologies (BMNR); Fundstrat Granny Shots US Large Cap ETF (GRNY; proposed short)



The summary and positions listed here reflect commentary from The Macro Show and may not represent the full scope of Keith McCullough’s current portfolio positioning. Positions listed in order mentioned on the show, not of any strength



CLICK HERE <https://model2.hedgeye.com/click/48134777.8555/aHR0cHM6Ly9hcHAuaGVkZ2V5ZS5jb20vbXUvaGVfdG1zX2ttX2RqXzEwLTI4LTIyNj9lbmNvZGVkX2RhdGE9ZkRvVSwwUytxZkNaSWJlTjhYcnNZR0YydUZTblpUNnM9LA/65561052a51cff3724ccb7dfC892dbd49> to access today's slides.



MAIN SUMMARY



Positioning Changes: Adding Shorts and Defensive Exposure



McCullough reported shorting HYG and Goldman Sachs into the prior close. He described the rally across semiconductors, credit and related stocks as part of the same AI-bubble trade, using rebounds toward lower highs to reload shorts. (12:18)



He bought healthcare and consumer staples on the prior day’s weakness, explicitly describing this as adding “Quad Four exposure on Quad Two days.” He reiterated that the current environment remained Quad 2, rather than advocating an immediate, complete switch into Quad 4 positioning. (16:13) (25:13)



He sold some U.S. dollars and bought Japanese yen. The dollar was overbought and at a cycle high; the yen was beginning to bounce. He still described the dollar’s signal as consistent with stronger oil, inflation and two-year yields. (21:18)



South Korea and Small Caps: Short the Bounce Incrementally



McCullough planned to short South Korean semiconductors that day, citing SK Hynix and the KOSPI. Prices had rebounded toward the upper end of their ranges while remaining below bullish trade and trend thresholds. Despite a roughly 6% rally, he said the KOSPI remained approximately 34% below its cycle peak. If the signal turned bullish on the trade horizon, he would reduce—but retain—the short. (2:44)



He reiterated the Russell 2000 short: after a two-day bounce, it remained approximately 8% below its peak, with roughly another 4% downside to the bottom of its immediate risk range. His instruction was to build hedges incrementally. He preferred large-cap exposure over small caps on the long side. (8:47) (9:21) (9:46)



Oil, Inflation and the Fed



He remained long oil, citing bullish trade and trend signals alongside rising risk-range highs. Brent’s upper range was $119, above the prior $114 cycle high. He identified $122–$123 as a possible subsequent mean-reversion area, referencing early 2022 levels. (4:28)



Higher oil and a stronger dollar supported his shorts in India and Indonesia because of the increased local-currency cost burden. Higher European gas costs supported his Germany and France shorts. (5:23)



He described the two-year Treasury yield as hawkish on both trade and trend, signaling higher-for-longer rates ahead of the Fed meeting. He expected the Fed to acknowledge inflation pressure, either at the meeting or following the next inflation release. He attributed its reluctance to raise rates to election-related political considerations. (5:52) (6:27) (7:30)



Other Equity Shorts and Cryptocurrency Positioning



Meta remained an explicit short based on its signal. He also reaffirmed shorts in India, the Philippines and Indonesia. Japan was approaching the upper end of its range, where he was interested in shorting it; he did not announce an executed Japan trade. (19:56) (20:11)



He confirmed that he had sold all Bitcoin exposure. Bitcoin had held trend support around $79,000, but remained bearish on the trade horizon, with lower highs and only marginally bullish trend support. He expressed interest in eventually shorting it, without confirming a Bitcoin short. (21:41)



He identified BMNR as an existing short and said he would also short GRNY. He mentioned MSTR in the same discussion without clearly specifying a position. (21:52)



Market Structure and Volatility



McCullough warned against treating sharp rebounds as proof of recovery. He cited a $5.5 billion market-on-close buy imbalance in leveraged semiconductor ETF SOXL as an example of investors chasing after a rebound. His approach remained selling or shorting near upper risk-range levels rather than reacting at the lows. (2:10)



He emphasized that thinner liquidity, rapid crowding and machine-driven flows can amplify moves independently of immediate fundamentals. High-beta momentum remained down approximately 15% over the month despite gaining 2.4% the previous day. (10:16) (15:52)



His key VIX levels were 16.76 for bullish trend, 19 for the “chop bucket,” and 20.56 for potential upside. He warned that renewed volatility above 19 would pressure speculative positioning. (18:24)



Earnings Deceleration and the Quad 4 Outlook



Responding to Emma’s question about AI-related investment gains inflating reported earnings, McCullough focused on difficult comparisons in Q1–Q2 2027. He argued that the coming Quad 4 could be more pronounced in earnings than in GDP. (27:01)



Among 302 Russell 2000 companies that had reported, he said aggregate earnings growth had slowed to 12%. He favored shorting individual companies already experiencing their own growth deceleration, as well as countries such as South Korea that he identified as already in Quad 4. (28:41) (29:32)



He described China as facing renewed growth deceleration and a risk of returning to disinflation or Quad 4. He also acknowledged that Brazil—despite what he considered an exceptionally strong macro setup—had produced his largest loss of the year, emphasizing accepting the mistake and reallocating capital. (30:10) (31:00)



Position Sizing and Execution



McCullough clarified that the displayed 4% commodity allocation was a maximum, not a minimum. His stated minimums were 3% for foreign currency and fixed income, 2% for equities and 1% for commodities. Options could begin at 0.25%–0.50%, with a stated maximum of 1%–2%. Positions appearing at different dashboard ranks could still carry the same minimum allocation. (23:32) (24:52)

The best part about risk managing Bear Markets? They bounce.

The raging Bear Market in South Korea bounced bigly overnight. That’s not new. Neither is the CNBC-type “Retail Investor” chasing their own tails in Levered Semis ETFs on the bounce ($5.5 billion MOC Buy Order in SOXL yesterday, Lol).

Brennan explains why this happens in The Fractals of Finance: “The nature of participation has changed dramatically over the past two decades… this evolution matters because the system now responds more quickly than its participants. Liquidity has become thinner and more fragile. Crowding develops in moments instead of days.”

Moments instead of days. That’s the fractal feedback loop operating at The Machine’s accelerating speed. The bounce isn’t a signal. It’s a reflex. The Machine generates it. The Retail Investor chases it. The liquidity evaporates. The crowding collapses.

TL;DR - POSITIONS MENTIONED



BULLISH: Brent Crude Oil (ticker unspecified), U.S. Dollar (USD), Japanese Yen (JPY—new purchase), Healthcare (XLV), Software (IGV), JAKKS Pacific (JAKK), Coca-Cola (KO), Airbnb (ABNB), Shipping (BWET), Exxon Mobil (XOM), Devon Energy (DVN), ConocoPhillips (COP), Lockheed Martin (LMT), Valero Energy (VLO), HF Sinclair (DINO), CVR Energy (CVI).



BEARISH: Meta Platforms (META), Alphabet/Google (GOOGL), France (EWQ), China, India (INDA), Germany (EWG), Indonesia (IDX), South Korea (KOSPI), Silver (SLV), Palladium (PALL)



The summary and positions listed here reflect commentary from The Macro Show and may not represent the full scope of Keith McCullough’s current portfolio positioning. Positions listed in order mentioned on the show, not of any strength



CLICK HERE <https://model2.hedgeye.com/click/48121763.9231/aHR0cHM6Ly9hcHAuaGVkZ2V5ZS5jb20vbXUvdG1zXzEwLTI3LTIwMjY_ZW5jb2RlZF9kYXRhPWZEb1QhVXhqM25RK0hkVGpSTk95VGNIMEs4VHphcnpzPSw/65561052a51cff3724ccb7dfC396f36a2> to access today's slides.



MAIN SUMMARY



Oil Strength and a Flattening Yield Curve



McCullough reiterated the Brent crude long, citing a signal toward $120 after prices tested new cycle highs. He argued that rising energy prices reinforce inflation pressure at the short end of the yield curve, while declining longer-term yields reflect weakening forward growth expectations. (1:12)



The 30-year yield had broken both TRADE and TREND; the 10-year yield had broken TRADE at 5.10% but remained bullish TREND. He described the flattening curve as discounting an economic slowdown several months ahead. (2:12)



China, India, France and Germany were identified as Quad 3 markets. McCullough linked their stagflation pressures to higher energy prices and a strong dollar, reiterating shorts across those markets. He said the dollar could continue working in Quad 4 because of its relative position against other currencies. (3:58)



Bitcoin: Target Cut and Potential Full Exit



He identified approximately $82,000 as the TRADE level and $79,000 as TREND, saying a TREND break would trigger an outright sale. He also raised the possibility of another two-thirds target reduction if he exited and TREND subsequently broke. Ethereum and Solana positions had already been sold at higher prices. (5:42)



Brazil Exit and New Yen Purchase



McCullough confirmed that he exited all Brazil exposure on a stop-loss the previous day. He cited the election outcome, currency weakness and stagflation concerns. A 23% loss on a 2% position cost approximately 46 basis points of portfolio capital; shorts provided offsets in his larger long/short portfolio. (4:41, 16:09)



He bought Japanese yen, describing the dollar as overbought and the yen purchase as signal-driven despite his lack of enthusiasm for the trade. (15:49)



Equity Risk Increasing; Short Bounces



McCullough said he was becoming more bearish as the S&P 500 formed lower highs alongside existing bearish TREND signals in the Nasdaq and Russell 2000. The Russell remained approximately 9.2% below its all-time high. (8:54)



He described a bullish TREND breakout in the VIX, with the bottom of its range rising into the 16s from earlier levels around 10–12. Negative gamma conditions could accelerate moves in either direction; he highlighted the extended absence of a 2% down day and approximately 1.4% upside to the top of the S&P’s range. (9:58, 12:26, 13:39)



He said he was shorting South Korea’s roughly 3% bounce that day and had reloaded the France short through EWQ the previous day. He reiterated shorting European bounces and described recent Indonesian rebounds as shorting opportunities. (9:40, 13:54, 15:16)



Meta remained a short-on-bounces call. Google was described as an outright short, with both companies carrying bearish TREND signals. (8:18, 11:45)



Energy Longs Remain Intact



McCullough maintained longs in oil, refiners and shipping, including BWET, saying there was no signal to exit. Jones noted that exploration and production stocks appeared to price in materially lower oil prices than prevailing levels and the futures curve. (19:26, 21:33)



Previously added longs included Exxon Mobil, Devon Energy and ConocoPhillips. Refining exposure included Valero, HF Sinclair and CVR Energy. McCullough emphasized waiting for signals—including breakdowns in refining stocks—to indicate an energy top. (24:21, 25:42, 27:16)



Gold, silver and corn longs had already been exited; silver and palladium were now shorts. He noted emerging weakness in parts of agriculture rather than across the entire group. (15:16)



Selective Longs and Sector Rotation



Healthcare, software and selected individual stocks remained sources of long-side performance. McCullough specifically discussed JAKKS Pacific, Coca-Cola and Airbnb, while highlighting Lockheed Martin among previously added positions. These were discussed as existing holdings, not new purchases that morning. (10:35, 25:14)



Jonesy noted that the momentum tracker was down to three longs as previously successful trades continued unwinding. Both speakers emphasized rotation toward names such as Exxon Mobil and Lockheed Martin, while McCullough reiterated expectations for more consistent Quad 4 conditions in 2027. (27:35)

reports.quotePt: Quando a queda é tudo o que resta, isso importa.
takeawaysPt: O petróleo continua sendo um sinal macro crucial, com o Brent atingindo novas máximas do ciclo de inflação e a Hedgeye esperando que a inflação de outubro se acelere, reforçando a inflação em #Quad2 nos EUA e a pressão de estagflação em #Quad3 no exterior.

A China e outros mercados globais já estão refletindo condições de #Quad3, com ações chinesas em novas mínimas do ciclo e a Hedgeye mantendo posições vendidas (shorts) em várias exposições a países sensíveis à estagflação.

A Bolha de IA continua enfraquecendo sob a superfície, com META, NVDA, GOOGL e 32 de 35 tickers do tema de IA sinalizando Bearish TREND, enquanto a Hedgeye se prepara para uma configuração mais ampla de #Quad4 em 2027.
reports.bigPicturePt:
O Leão no Inverno foi a peça teatral de Goldman de 1966 sobre Henrique II assistindo seu império, seu casamento e sua dinastia entrarem em colapso simultaneamente. Todo mundo perdendo. A Questão não é se a queda virá, mas se você está preparado para ela.

Quando um #Quad4 ampliado chegar em 2027 e a queda for tudo o que resta (nos rendimentos dos títulos / Bond Yields também!), a única coisa que importa para o seu capital suado é o que você fez antes de isso se tornar óbvio.

No caminho entre cravar o topo do mercado de ações dos EUA em 2007 até o fundo em 2009, eu tinha meus sinais, stops e um processo de gestão de risco. Eu também tinha muito menos do que tenho agora. Minha equipe, modelos e ferramentas estão significativamente melhores do que naquela época.

A coisa mais bullish que posso dizer sobre IA (nós a chamamos de HI: Hedgeye Intelligence) é o que estamos fazendo com ela internamente. É o nosso Cavalo de Troia — acelerando o desmantelamento de longo prazo tanto do "research" de Old Wall quanto de sua mídia repleta de conflitos de interesse.
reports.macroGrindPt:
Medimos e mapeamos de forma fractal TODOS os mercados simultaneamente. Em um sistema fractal, cada componente importa, mas não de maneira igual. Alguns nós carregam um peso desproporcional no ciclo de retroalimentação. Neste momento, dois deles dominam The Signal:

Petróleo

IA

Você pode construir sua própria narrativa sobre ambos. Prefiro não desperdiçar o seu tempo.

Tudo o que precisei esta manhã foi ver o Zuck de couro preto ao lado do Jensen de pele de carneiro para saber tudo o que preciso saber. Um sujeito quer viver em seu metaverso sem pagar impostos. O outro quer "alimentá-lo" com financiamento circular.

Ambos têm um trabalho em comum — vender as ações deles para você.

Vamos nos aprofundar (drill baby drill) no petróleo primeiro:

Permanecemos comprados (long) em Brent Oil (BNO), que está subindo para novas máximas do ciclo de inflação a $116 esta manhã

Continuamos com a projeção mais alta de Wall Street para o CPI de outubro, que continuará a acelerar

Alocações de Ativos de Inflação juntamente com BNO = DBMF, PFIX, CRAK, BWET, UUP, HGER, FTXG.

Implicações nos EUA vs. Globais da inflação do petróleo em #Quad2?

O último #Quad2 MENSAL óbvio dos EUA é o dado de dezembro (que Old Wall vai "enxergar" divulgado em janeiro)

O resto do mundo (ROW) fica com moedas enfraquecendo e estagflação em #Quad3

O maior país com estagflação em #Quad3 no momento = China:

Ações chinesas (Shanghai Comp Index) com queda de -6.1% no último mês, marcando novas mínimas de ciclo de estagflação em #Quad3

Estamos vendidos (short) em várias exposições a países em #Quad3, incluindo Índia, Indonésia, Malásia, França, Alemanha, etc.

De volta à Bolha de IA…

A festa a fantasia de Zuckerberg/Wang está acontecendo porque a NVDA quer "investir" $3 bilhões no que quer que o acordo com a META acabe sendo. Dois dos maiores "líderes" de ações de bolha da história humana apertando as mãos para tornar nossos filhos "seguros"?

Aqui está o que os Deuses Fractais têm a dizer sobre suas ações (e, ao contrário da festa a fantasia, esta parte não tem roteiro):

META = Bearish TRADE and TREND

NVDA = Bearish TRADE and TREND

Dos 35 tickers em nosso produto AI Bubble Big Theme, esses são 2 dos 32 que agora sinalizam Bearish TREND. Assim como o petróleo e a própria Bolha de IA, eles carregam pesos de impacto marginal muito mais pesados do que a maioria dos outros tickers.

E quanto a GOOGL? Oh, meu Deus Fractal. Olhe para aquele gráfico.

Até mesmo um "Moving Chart Monkey" de fator único pode dizer que GOOGL é um desastre agora. O que eles farão para conter o drawdown? O que vai impedir qualquer um desses drawdowns de se tornarem quedas livres (crashes) generalizadas quando o #Quad4 atingir em 2027?

Henrique II também não conseguiu impedir a queda de sua dinastia. Ele apenas não tinha um sinal de Risk Range™ para avisá-lo quando ela começou.
reports.synthesisPt: O cenário macroeconômico atual é dominado pela aceleração da inflação impulsionada pelo petróleo nos EUA em regime de #Quad2, enquanto o restante do mundo enfrenta estagflação em #Quad3, refletida em moedas depreciadas e mínimas acionárias na China e em outros mercados globais. Concomitantemente, a Bolha de IA apresenta forte deterioração estrutural interna, com 32 de 35 tickers temáticos — incluindo gigantes como META, NVDA e GOOGL — confirmando sinalização Bearish TREND. Enquanto executivos tentam sustentar narrativas por meio de acordos circulares, os modelos fractais apontam para o risco crescente de drawdowns se transformarem em quedas severas. A postura estratégica da Hedgeye mantém posições vendidas em exposições a países estagflacionários e alocação comprada em ativos de inflação, preparando o capital para um ambiente mais amplo de #Quad4 projetado para 2027.

BEARISH: High-Yield Credit (HYG), Industrials (XLI), Russell 2000 (IWM), South Korea (EWY), Philippines (EPHE), India (INDA), Indonesia (IDX), Malaysia (EWM), Germany (EWG), France (EWQ), Silver (SLV), Palladium (PALL), Memory Semiconductors (DRAM), CoreWeave (CRWV), Nvidia (NVDA), Nasdaq 100 (QQQ; prospective short).



The summary and positions listed here reflect commentary from The Macro Show and may not represent the full scope of Keith McCullough’s current portfolio positioning. Positions listed in order mentioned on the show, not of any strength



CLICK HERE <https://model2.hedgeye.com/click/48093335.9226/aHR0cHM6Ly9hcHAuaGVkZ2V5ZS5jb20vbXUvdG1zXzEwLTI2LTIwMjY_ZW5jb2RlZF9kYXRhPWZEb2QhNXRjTkFTY2piYjl0eGdjaHVIcDkvTGxadkJJPSE/65561052a51cff3724ccb7dfC1d78ceca> to access today's slides.



MAIN SUMMARY



Rates and Credit: Treasury Shorts Covered, Credit Shorts Maintained



Keith covered all TLT and ZROZ shorts last week after long-duration bonds broke out. Two- and ten-year yields remain bearish TRADE but bullish TREND, while the thirty-year yield is below both TRADE and TREND. He cited approximately 5.10% as ten-year TRADE resistance. (2:36)



He also sold his CLOZ exposure last week, citing widening credit spreads, while maintaining the high-yield short. High-yield option-adjusted spreads stood at approximately 337 basis points. His key warning thresholds remain high-yield spreads above 300 and ten-year BBB spreads above 100, with both rising. (3:20)



Keith expects approximately five monthly Quad 4 readings in early 2027 and further credit-spread widening. He described current conditions as following peaks in credit demand, leverage, and options usage. (4:00)



Brazil: A 2% Position Facing a Potential Exit



Brazil remained a 2% long position, with Keith acknowledging that he had no political edge ahead of the election-related selloff. He emphasized that the minimum position size limited the damage relative to a larger allocation. (4:35)



He would sell Brazil if it broke TREND, but had not announced an exit during the show. He planned to assess the signal during his usual 9:30–11:00 a.m. trading window. (5:17), (19:14)



International Equities: Extensive Asia Shorts and Continued European Shorts



The portfolio remains net short emerging markets, with shorts across South Korea, the Philippines, India, Indonesia, and Malaysia. Keith described his Asia short exposure as among the largest since 2022 and identified the region as a primary area for shorting bounces. Japan had already been exited. (5:37)



He maintained shorts in Germany and France and would short European rallies. Both markets declined approximately 2% or more during the previous week. (15:45)



Technology: Sell Nasdaq Bounces; Nvidia Joins the Short List



QQQ remains bearish TREND despite the morning’s futures rebound. Keith advised using rallies to exit remaining exposure and identified shorting QQQ as the next potential move, rather than announcing an established short. He prefers QQQ to XLK for that trade because Microsoft and Apple retain bullish signals. (6:33)



XLK was sold after breaking TREND, with Nvidia’s breakdown contributing to that decision. Keith reiterated the existing memory-semiconductor short and said the semiconductor cycle was past its peak. (6:17), (7:36)



Microsoft and Apple remain bullish in signal terms, while Google and Nvidia are bearish TREND. CoreWeave was highlighted among Signal Strength shorts. Nvidia would enter the Signal Strength short list that day after Friday’s confirmation. (14:30), (27:07)



Sector Rotation: Consumer Staples Added Alongside Healthcare



Keith bought consumer staples last week, including Friday, as XLP shifted from bearish to bullish. Healthcare remains his strongest sector long, while industrials remain his strongest sector short. He described these as Quad 4 attributes already present in the portfolio. (9:54), (23:18)



Ryan identified Philip Morris, Costco, SharkNinja, and Kroger as long-side stock ideas. Keith used these names to illustrate rotating away from former technology leaders as signals change. (23:34)



Gold miners have come off the long list, industrial names have entered the short list, and financial names have come off the short list. The long list has diversified, supporting the existing RSP position. (22:02)



Equities and Options: Russell Shorts Retained, Some Profits Taken



Keith highlighted approximately 7,600 as the S&P 500’s first significant lower-high Risk Range level. He cited drawdowns of roughly 2.5% for the S&P 500, 6% for QQQ, and 9.5% for IWM. (11:29)



He is short the Russell, not the S&P 500. Russell implied-volatility premiums were approximately 34%, versus 73% for the S&P, making Russell puts relatively cheaper by that measure. He took profits on some Russell puts Friday and would consider buying new short-dated puts if available at better prices. Negative gamma remains a reason to expect sharp moves in both directions. (14:48), (15:27)



Bond Volatility, Commodities, and Crypto



Keith bought PFIX again Friday after waiting for the revised low end of its Risk Range. MOVE remains bullish TREND. He cited persistent inflation, lower-growth expectations for 2027, and his expectation of a December Fed hike. (13:24)



He remains long Brent through BNO and would buy oil dips, citing higher lows and higher highs. Natural gas had already been exited before an approximately 18% decline. (16:24)



He remains out of gold and prefers existing silver and palladium shorts to initiating a gold short. Ethereum, Solana, and Avalanche had been exited after TREND breaks. Bitcoin was bearish TRADE and could become another exit; no sale was announced. (16:41), (18:25)

TXG

Sector:

Healthcare

Sector Head:

Tom Tobin

THESIS SUMMARY:

TXG remains a Long as stronger-than-expected Single Cell demand, accelerating Atera interest, and growing exposure to the AI application layer support a stronger multi-year growth outlook. Atera demand is already running well ahead of the initial 40-system 2026 target, with manufacturing capacity — not customer interest — now the primary constraint, while temporary Spatial softness reflects customers delaying purchases ahead of the new platform rollout. With 2027 estimates already above consensus and management seeing significant pull-through from Atera, the setup points to meaningful upside if adoption continues to outpace expectations.

WEEKEND UPDATE:

TXG has moved from Active Long to Long Bench after losing positive Signal Strength and seeing its Quad Factor Score deteriorate, despite continued strength in spatial genomics adoption and NIH funding.

Moved from Active Long to Long Bench on October 16 after losing positive Signal Strength and seeing its Quad Factor Score weaken, removing two key conditions for maintaining an active position.

FY26 NIH single-cell and spatial awards rose 6.5% to $3.25 billion, outperforming overall NIH funding, which declined 0.2%. Spatial-only awards grew 23.9% to $705 million, supporting the longer-term adoption thesis.

NIH funding growth slowed from 43.0% in June to 6.5%, while September awards declined 24.3%. Hedgeye still expects a Q3 revenue beat, but softer tracking data and weaker market signals warrant patience before reactivating the Long.

DT

Sector:

Software

Sector Head:

Andrew Freedman, CFA

THESIS SUMMARY:

DT is a Long as newly confirmed Signal Strength adds support to an observability name positioned in one of the infrastructure-software segments with the most upside. Its comparable exposure to DDOG gives Dynatrace leverage to rising observability demand as AI workloads and system complexity continue to expand.

WEEKEND UPDATE:

DT remains a Long as accelerating usage trends, durable recurring revenue growth, and expanding AI-related observability demand continue to strengthen the setup.

DT remains a Signal Strength Long on the bench, with the stock holding up well through the recent software drawdown and continuing to show relative strength versus weaker peers.

A shift toward consumption-based billing is driving accelerating usage trends that the desk views as more durable than what it is seeing at MongoDB, while the Arise acquisition is expected to add roughly 200 basis points to annual recurring revenue growth on top of DT’s stable mid-to-high-teens growth rate.

Additional upside optionality comes from observability becoming increasingly important for AI training and self-healing software, while Dynatrace’s history of activist involvement and ongoing M&A speculation provide potential additional catalysts.

MSFT

Sector:

Global Technology

Sector Head:

Felix Wang, CFA

THESIS SUMMARY:

MSFT remains a Long as accelerating Azure demand and strong secular AI spending support durable, economy-independent revenue growth. OpenAI’s July revenue accelerated roughly 20% month-over-month to a $40 billion-plus ARR run rate, reinforcing the improving AI demand trends that previously signaled an Azure inflection. MSFT’s exposure to accelerating Pod 1 revenue growth is particularly attractive in Quad 3, where companies delivering strong organic growth regardless of the macro environment have historically outperformed.

WEEKEND UPDATE:

MSFT remains a Signal Strength Long, supported by its broader AI infrastructure and software positioning, expanding enterprise AI workloads, and continued investment across next-generation compute, networking, and data-center architecture.

Microsoft is reportedly cutting back its internal use of Anthropic's Claude, with additional detail gathered at the OCP conference. The shift is notable as enterprises increasingly determine which large language models, or LLMs, are best suited for specific workloads rather than relying on a single provider.

The global LLM database has expanded to 1,034 models, while upcoming work will focus on October trends in agentic coding, AI systems that can independently perform multi-step software-development tasks. These workloads remain important for Microsoft given its exposure to Azure, GitHub, and the broader enterprise AI ecosystem.

OCP conference takeaways highlighted continued innovation in optics, power, and cooling, including XPO, MPO, and CPO architectures designed to move data more efficiently inside AI data centers. MSFT remains Signal Strength Long, although it is currently not on the position monitor.

CRWD remains a Long with Signal Strength as enterprise cybersecurity spending accelerates and AI expands the number of attack surfaces companies must protect. Broader security demand should support accelerating Pod 1 revenue and backlog growth into earnings. CRWD also reached the low end of its risk range, creating an attractive entry point as software continues to outperform semiconductors.

WST is a Signal Strength Long, added September 18, and recently moved to the Long Bench as easing GLP-1-related headwinds support an improving healthcare outlook. Increased early-stage patient monitoring and medical visits as Medicare patients begin using GLP-1 drugs could provide an additional demand catalyst. With the stock trading near the low end of its risk range, further weakness could present an attractive buying opportunity, supported by the desk’s broader bullish view on healthcare and biotechnology.

WEEKEND UPDATE:

WST remains a Long Bias despite losing Signal Strength on October 8, as its Bullish TREND, attractive entry point, and improving GLP-1 outlook support the upside thesis.

Featured on The Call, where Keith McCullough and Tom Tobin highlighted WST's Bullish TREND signal and favored buying healthcare stocks amid broader sector weakness.

WST is trading near the low end of its daily risk range, offering a potentially attractive entry point despite losing Signal Strength on October 8.

The longer-term thesis remains supported by easing GLP-1 headwinds and increased drug utilization among Medicare patients, potentially driving demand for WST's pharmaceutical packaging and delivery products.

PM

Sector:

Consumer Staples

Sector Head:

Daniel Biolsi

THESIS SUMMARY:

PM remains a top Long Idea and Signal Strength Long, supported by strong pricing power, expanding smoke-free product adoption, and significant long-term growth opportunities in the U.S. nicotine market. Q3 earnings exceeded expectations, with revenue growing 5.5% year-over-year and operating margins expanding, while ZYN gained 140 basis points of market share as new flavors, nicotine strengths, and more competitive pricing supported demand. Although the transition to 20-pouch ZYN cans and increased marketing spending will pressure near-term U.S. profitability, continued ZYN expansion, favorable regulatory developments, and the anticipated U.S. launch of IQOS ILUMA reinforce the longer-term growth thesis.

WEEKEND UPDATE:

PM remains a top Long Idea and Signal Strength Long, supported by strong pricing power, expanding smoke-free product adoption, and significant long-term growth opportunities in the U.S. nicotine market.

PM reported Q3 EPS of $2.37, beating consensus by $0.07, with revenue growing 5.5% year-over-year and adjusted operating margins expanding to 44.7%. Strong combustible pricing and operating efficiencies helped offset slower international smoke-free growth and increased U.S. investment.

ZYN gained 140 basis points of U.S. nicotine pouch market share between June and September, supported by new flavors, higher nicotine strengths, and the ZYN Ultra rollout. The transition from 15 to 20 pouches per can effectively reduces pricing by 25% per pouch, pressuring near-term profitability but improving competitiveness and potentially supporting further market-share gains.

PM remains at the top of the Long list despite expectations for approximately breakeven or slightly negative U.S. operating income in Q4. A more favorable regulatory environment for nicotine pouches, continued international smoke-free expansion, and the anticipated U.S. launch of IQOS ILUMA reinforce the multiyear growth thesis.

DKS

Sector:

Retail

Sector Head:

Brian McGough

THESIS SUMMARY:

The business is still overearning while growth decelerates, with the Foot Locker acquisition viewed as structurally dilutive and a potential source of significant capital destruction. House of Sport adds another capital-allocation concern, while current guidance is not viewed as conservative enough to create an easy earnings reset. With growth investors avoiding the slowdown, GARP investors lacking a reacceleration catalyst, and value investors unlikely to step in near current levels, DKS remains Signal Strength Short with downside seen well below $100.

WEEKEND UPDATE:

DKS remains an Active Short and Signal Strength Short as declining seasonal hiring, shifting footwear preferences, and continued Foot Locker integration risks reinforce the downside thesis.

DKS is reducing seasonal hiring by 21% year-over-year, from approximately 14,000 workers in 2025 to just over 11,000 in 2026, signaling efforts to control costs amid weakening demand. Foot Locker hiring is down 39%, while core Dick's hiring is down 13%.

Consumer footwear preferences are shifting away from athletic sneakers toward loafers and flats, pressuring both Dick's and Foot Locker. With footwear driving much of DKS's recent growth outside trading cards, weakening trends could make future comparable-sales growth increasingly difficult.

DKS remains Signal Strength Short, with the company still viewed as over-earning despite last quarter's disappointing results. Foot Locker integration costs, House of Sport expansion, and additional capital requirements reinforce expectations for further earnings pressure and potential downside.

SAIA

Sector:

Industrials

Sector Head:

Jay Van Sciver

THESIS SUMMARY:

The LTL industry has excess capacity and no longer has a large pool of high-cost unionized freight to donate share, leaving non-union carriers like SAIA fighting harder for volume in an increasingly commoditized market. Recent data reinforce that pressure, with SAIA shipments up just 1.1% in August versus more than 5% growth at XPO, while Amazon's entry and FedEx Freight's willingness to chase volume on price add further competitive risk. With pricing beginning to roll over and growth still lagging peers, SAIA remains both a Signal Strength Short and an Active Best Idea Short.

Sector Head:

THESIS SUMMARY:

DraftKings (DKNG) remains a Short as growing legal uncertainty around prediction-market sports betting threatens a business the company has already committed nearly $1 billion of capital and P&L exposure to building. The widening split among federal appeals courts increases the likelihood of Supreme Court review, creating a major regulatory overhang while multiple states continue challenging prediction-market sports contracts as unlicensed gambling. DKNG remains Signal Strength Short and in a bearish trading trend after a recent failed attempt to turn bullish.

WEEKEND UPDATE:

DKNG remains a Short Bias and Signal Strength Short as slowing core business trends, mounting earnings revision risks, and significant prediction-market spending reinforce the downside thesis.

DKNG is expected to report a meaningful Q3 earnings miss, with EBITDA estimated to decline approximately $100 million and a substantial cut to 2026 guidance anticipated. The weaker outlook would also imply further pressure on Q4 profitability.

By the time #Quad4 becomes obvious across ALL Asset Classes on both our TRADE and TREND durations, you’ll be looking back at #MOAB and Cycle Highs that peaked like they did, cyclically, in 2021 (when all the “Crypto Guys” felt like a genius and nobody needed a risk mgt process).

What’s a cornerstone of a Diversified #Quad4 Portfolio that’s already working with the US Economy in its final QUARTERLY #Quad2? A: The US Dollar. And there are plenty of Shorts we already have on vs. USD like lots of Asian Equity Markets:

US Dollar Index was flat last week and remains Bullish on both out TRADE and TREND durations

EUR/USD was down another -0.4% last week and remains Bearish TRADE and TREND

Japanese Yen was +0.8% vs. USD last week, breaking out back to Bullish TRADE and TREND

Canadian Dollar popped +1.1% vs. USD last week, getting it back to Neutral TREND

Philippines Peso dropped another -1.0% vs. USD, taking its TRENDING 3-month decline to -2.9%

Pesos in the Philippines? When every Tech Bro wants to talk “neoclouds” and AI? Yep. We’re short Philippines Equities (EPHE), so we care more about their currency than what poor Zuck “feels” about where he lives and pays taxes:

Philippines (EPHE) was down another -0.9% last week, taking its TRENDING 3-month drawdown to -8.8%

South Korea (EWY) was down another -1.5% last week, taking its TRENDING 3-month drawdown to -23.6%

India (INDA) was down another -3.2% last week, taking its TRENDING 3-month loss to -6.7%

We’re short all 3 of those Asian Equity Exposures. We’re also Short Indonesia (IDX) and Malaysia (EWM), so they’ll help hedge our only Emerging Market Long position: Brazil (EWZ) which is going to get crushed this morning.

What was my edge on the Brazilian Election? Evidently zero. I have a MIN position SIZE (Equity MIN = 2%, MAX 6%) so I’ll either get stopped out of that today, or I will not. It’s a jailbreak so I won’t know until I get out in the prison yard on the open.

How about other Currencies like Gold or big Commodities like Oil? They weren’t in #Quad4 last week:

Oil (WTI) inflated another +4.3% last week, taking its TRENDING 3-month return to +28.5%

Gold was down another -4.1% last week to -6.8% in the last month alone (despite Bond Yields being down)

Since we’re long of Brent Oil (BNO) and not only out of Gold but short of Silver and Palladium, that was good for us last week:

Silver (SLV) was down another -5.9% last week to -17.1% in the last month alone

Palladium (PALL) was down another -6.0% last week to -17.2% in the last month alone

These Oil and Precious Metals moves continue to be #Quad2 moves. How about Bond Yields?

UST 2yr Yield was down -3 basis points last week to -21bps in the last month

UST 10yr Yield was down -8 basis points last week to -10bps in the last month

Bond Yields are signaling Bearish TRADE, Bullish TREND – that means the Cycle Highs for Inflation aren’t in but the Cycle Highs for Bond Yields may very well be. It also means that Bond Yields aren’t breaking down on a TRENDING basis yet.

We’re not short TLT anymore. Staying with a Yield Curve flattener and Short High Yield (HYG) with High Yield OAS Spread widening another +6 basis points last week to +63 basis points in the last month.

Will this developing Credit Event eventually slow US Growth from its Peak Cycle 2026? Yep. That’s what markets are signaling. That’s partly why Healthcare (XLV) Long was up another +1.5% last week vs. Short Industrials (XLI) down another -1.9%.

Sheridan said prison is mind-numbingly repetitive routine until the incident disrupts it. The Credit Event is the incident. The process is what tells you WHEN to put on your steel toe boots before it arrives. Not after. Before.

#Quad4 Prison Rules.

reports.titlePt: EARLY LOOK: Preparando-se Para o #Quad4
reports.quotePt: A prisão é uma mistura de rotina entorpecentemente repetitiva e lampejos repentinos de violência e caos.
takeawaysPt: Os mercados estão sinalizando cada vez mais uma transição em direção ao #Quad4 em 2027, com o Dólar americano mais forte, o enfraquecimento das ações asiáticas, a abertura dos spreads de crédito e a queda nos rendimentos dos títulos apontando para um crescimento mais lento à frente.

A Hedgeye permanece short em diversos mercados de ações asiáticos, metais preciosos como Prata e Paládio, e crédito High Yield, enquanto se mantém long em Petróleo Brent e Healthcare conforme a configuração atual de #Quad2 começa a apresentar mais características de #Quad4.

O Evento de Crédito em desenvolvimento é o principal risco a ser monitorado, com os spreads de High Yield abrindo e os setores sensíveis ao crescimento enfraquecendo, reforçando a necessidade de se posicionar antes que a desaceleração fique óbvia em todas as classes de ativos.
reports.bigPicturePt:
Você está se preparando para uma sequência de #Quad4s em 2027? Os mercados estão.

No momento em que o #Quad4 se tornar óbvio em TODAS as Classes de Ativos, tanto na nossa duração TRADE quanto na TREND, você estará olhando para trás, para a #MOAB e para as Máximas de Ciclo que atingiram o pico exatamente como fizeram, ciclicamente, em 2021 (quando todos os "Caras das Cripto" se sentiam gênios e ninguém precisava de um processo de gerenciamento de risco).

O que esperar de um dia no #Quad4? Bem, tivemos alguns na semana passada!

Enquanto estão se desenvolvendo, Bear Markets são muito parecidos com uma prisão de desempenho. Muitas pessoas, como Situational Unawareness (Leo alguma coisa?), simplesmente vão desaparecer. Sheridan explica o ritmo diário em How To Not Die In Prison: "Na maior parte do tempo, o seu dia se parece exatamente com o de ontem, com o de amanhã e com o dia seguinte a esse. Alguns dias, no entanto, um incidente interrompe a rotina."
reports.macroGrindPt:
Bem-vindos a mais uma bela Macro Monday @Hedgeye, onde praticamente qualquer pessoa da nossa comunidade pode lançar um hedge fund para lucrar tanto com o #Quad2 quanto depois com o #Quad4. Só não chame isso de Situational Leverage!

O que é a pedra angular de uma Carteira #Quad4 Diversificada que já está funcionando com a Economia dos EUA em seu #Quad2 TRIMESTRAL final? R: O Dólar americano. E há muitos Shorts que já temos contra o USD, como vários Mercados de Ações Asiáticos:

O Índice Dólar americano ficou estável na semana passada e permanece Bullish tanto na duração TRADE quanto TREND

EUR/USD caiu mais -0,4% na semana passada e permanece Bearish TRADE e TREND

Iene japonês subiu +0,8% vs. USD na semana passada, rompendo de volta para Bullish TRADE e TREND

Dólar canadense deu um salto de +1,1% vs. USD na semana passada, voltando para TREND Neutro

Peso filipino caiu mais -1,0% vs. USD, levando seu declínio em TREND de 3 meses para -2,9%

Pesos nas Filipinas? Quando todo Tech Bro quer falar sobre "neonuves" e IA? Sim. Estamos short em Ações das Filipinas (EPHE), então nos importamos mais com a moeda deles do que com o que o pobre Zuck "sente" sobre onde mora e paga impostos:

Filipinas (EPHE) caiu mais -0,9% na semana passada, levando seu drawdown em TREND de 3 meses para -8,8%

Coreia do Sul (EWY) caiu mais -1,5% na semana passada, levando seu drawdown em TREND de 3 meses para -23,6%

Índia (INDA) caiu mais -3,2% na semana passada, levando sua perda em TREND de 3 meses para -6,7%

Estamos short em todas essas 3 Exposições a Ações Asiáticas. Também estamos Short em Indonésia (IDX) e Malásia (EWM), então eles ajudarão a proteger nossa única posição Long em Mercados Emergentes: Brasil (EWZ), que vai ser esmagado nesta manhã.

Qual era a minha vantagem na Eleição Brasileira? Evidentemente zero. Tenho um TAMANHO de posição MÍNIMO (MÍNIMO de Ações = 2%, MÁXIMO 6%), então serei estopado disso hoje, ou não serei. É uma fuga da prisão, então não saberei até sair para o pátio da prisão na abertura.

E quanto a outras Moedas como o Ouro ou grandes Commodities como o Petróleo? Elas não estavam em #Quad4 na semana passada:

Petróleo (WTI) inflou mais +4,3% na semana passada, levando seu retorno em TREND de 3 meses para +28,5%

Ouro caiu mais -4,1% na semana passada para -6,8% apenas no último mês (apesar da queda nos Rendimentos dos Títulos)

Já que estamos long em Petróleo Brent (BNO) e não apenas fora do Ouro, mas short em Prata e Paládio, isso foi bom para nós na semana passada:

Prata (SLV) caiu mais -5,9% na semana passada para -17,1% apenas no último mês

Paládio (PALL) caiu mais -6,0% na semana passada para -17,2% apenas no último mês

Esses movimentos do Petróleo e de Metais Preciosos continuam sendo movimentos de #Quad2. E quanto aos Rendimentos dos Títulos?

Rendimento do UST de 2 anos caiu -3 pontos-base na semana passada para -21bps no último mês

Rendimento do UST de 10 anos caiu -8 pontos-base na semana passada para -10bps no último mês

Os Rendimentos dos Títulos estão sinalizando Bearish TRADE, Bullish TREND – isso significa que as Máximas de Ciclo para a Inflação ainda não ficaram para trás, mas as Máximas de Ciclo para os Rendimentos dos Títulos muito provavelmente sim. Isso também significa que os Rendimentos dos Títulos ainda não estão quebrando em uma base TREND.

Não estamos mais short em TLT. Mantendo uma posição de achatamento da Curva de Rendimentos e Short em High Yield (HYG), com o Spread OAS de High Yield alargando mais +6 pontos-base na semana passada para +63 pontos-base no último mês.

Esse Evento de Crédito em desenvolvimento eventualmente desacelerará o Crescimento dos EUA a partir do seu Pico de Ciclo em 2026? Sim. É isso o que os mercados estão sinalizando. É em parte por isso que a posição Long em Healthcare (XLV) subiu mais +1,5% na semana passada vs. Short em Industrials (XLI) caindo mais -1,9%.

Sheridan disse que a prisão é uma rotina entorpecentemente repetitiva até que o incidente a interrompa. O Evento de Crédito é o incidente. O processo é o que lhe diz QUANDO calçar suas botas de bico de aço antes que ele chegue. Não depois. Antes.

#Quad4 Prison Rules.
reports.synthesisPt: Os mercados começam a sinalizar uma transição gradual em direção ao regime de #Quad4 projetado para 2027, refletida no fortalecimento do Dólar americano, no enfraquecimento das ações asiáticas e no recuo dos rendimentos dos Treasuries. A Hedgeye mantém posições vendidas em bolsas emergentes da Ásia, além de Prata, Paládio e crédito High Yield, equilibrando o portfólio com posições compradas em Petróleo Brent e Healthcare. O foco central de atenção recai sobre a abertura dos spreads de crédito High Yield, desenhando um Evento de Crédito que tende a desacelerar o ciclo econômico norte-americano. Executar a gestão de risco e antecipar o posicionamento antes que essa desaceleração se torne consensual em todas as classes de ativos é a chave para preservar o capital.

Access The Macro Show Dashboard <https://model2.hedgeye.com/click/48070271.9612/aHR0cHM6Ly9hcHAuaGVkZ2V5ZS5jb20vbWFjcm9fZGFzaGJvYXJkL21hY3JvX3Nob3c/65561052a51cff3724ccb7dfC7075826d>



TL;DR - POSITIONS MENTIONED



BULLISH: Brent Crude Oil (BNO), Tanker Shipping (BWET), Healthcare (XLV), Healthcare Technology (HTEC), S&P 500 Equal Weight (RSP), Software (IGV), Cybersecurity (BUG), U.S. Dollar (USD), Bitcoin (BTC), Catastrophe Bond (ILS)



BEARISH: High Yield Corporate Bonds (HYG), European Equities including Germany (EWG), Silver (SLV), Palladium (PALL), Clean Energy (PBD), Qatar Equities (QAT), Memory Semiconductors (DRAM), Listed Private Equity (PSP).



The summary and positions listed here reflect commentary from The Macro Show and may not represent the full scope of Keith McCullough’s current portfolio positioning. Positions listed in order mentioned on the show, not of any strength



CLICK HERE <https://model2.hedgeye.com/click/48070271.9612/aHR0cHM6Ly9hcHAuaGVkZ2V5ZS5jb20vbXUvdG1zXzEwLTIzLTIwMjY_ZW5jb2RlZF9kYXRhPWZEb0shSi9sTjlWL3k0Y0lhaVF2aHQ1Y0ZTS1ZENHhzPSE/65561052a51cff3724ccb7dfC085756fa> to access today's slides.



MAIN SUMMARY



Equity Rotation: Out of QQQ and Into Equal Weight



Capital shifted out of QQQ and into RSP earlier in the week. The analysts highlighted the equal-weight S&P 500’s stronger performance relative to the capitalization-weighted index and reiterated their emphasis on inflation exposures and healthcare. A catastrophe-bond position was also added the previous day (ILS). (20:01)



Healthcare remained Keith’s largest U.S. equity sector allocation. XLV rose 1.3% the previous day, bringing its October gain to 7.7% and reaching an all-time high. The team also remained long healthcare technology through HTEC. (2:07) (18:41)



Rates and Credit: Long-End Yields Weaken Despite Persistent Inflation



Falling long-term yields were described as a flight toward safety and a response to credit and growth concerns, rather than evidence that inflation had subsided. High yield option-adjusted spreads widened another 11 basis points, and the stated position remained short HYG. (1:19)



The two-year Treasury yield remained bullish TREND, supported by an accelerating inflation nowcast. The 10-year yield was bearish TRADE but bullish TREND, with 5.10% resistance, 4.85% support, and a 5.29% upper Risk Range versus October’s 5.31% cycle high. (1:43) (3:40)



The team reduced long-end rate positioning as 30-year yields lost momentum. The 30-year yield remained bullish TREND but bearish TRADE, with a lower upper Risk Range. They were not adding PFIX exposure and identified the yield’s TREND line as the stop-loss reference. (5:20)



The macro outlook included a shallow quarterly Quad 4 in Q1 2027 and monthly Quad 4 readings in February, April, and May—three of the first six months. The analysts emphasized watching corporate guidance against that approaching backdrop. (26:13)



Inflation Positions: Brent and Tanker Shipping Remain Preferred



Brent remained the preferred oil exposure through BNO because its signal and price momentum were stronger than WTI’s. Both oils remained bullish TREND, while diesel continued making higher highs. The team said its inflation outlook and related positioning had not changed. (7:36)



The BWET tanker-shipping long remained in place despite its volatility. The U.S. dollar long also remained established, although the dollar was near the bottom of its Risk Range and losing some signal strength. No new dollar allocation was announced. (8:53)



AI Breakdown: New Memory Short, Continued Software Exposure



The DRAM short was added during the week. DRAM fell approximately 6% the previous day, with the analysts estimating a roughly 6–7% return on their short. They specifically identified semiconductor memory as their short exposure within the AI theme. (21:11)



Deterioration broadened across the AI tracker: only four of 36 names remained bullish TREND, while 32 were bearish TREND, versus 26 the prior week. High beta momentum fell 8.1% in a day and stood 43% below its cycle high; leveraged semiconductor ETF SOXL fell approximately 20% that day. (16:25)



Software remained a long exposure. Cybersecurity was identified as the strongest software subsector, with the analysts saying the AI-related breakdown had not yet affected that area in the same way. They continued monitoring it closely. (20:45)



Other Shorts: Metals, Europe, and Private Equity



Silver and palladium remained shorts. The analysts highlighted broad mining-stock weakness, including approximately 5–6% daily declines across several mining groups. They explicitly clarified that they were not short gold, despite its bearish TREND and new lows. (11:06)



European shorts remained in place, including Germany, with bounces viewed as opportunities to add short exposure. Higher inflation was cited as a problem for Europe. China was also bearish, but the team explicitly said it held no current China short. Clean energy and Qatar remained additional shorts. (9:52) (21:11)



The XLF short was closed as financial-sector signals became more bullish. The PSP private-equity short remained: the analysts distinguished improving financials outside private equity/private credit from continued bearish signals within those groups. (22:07)



Crypto: Bitcoin at Minimum Size; Ethereum Long Removed



Bitcoin remained long at minimum position size, near the bottom of its Risk Range and with weakening signal strength. The Ethereum long had been removed. Bitcoin and MSTR were identified as the only bullish TREND readings in their crypto coverage, but no MSTR position was announced. Weakness across the broader crypto market reduced their confidence in a sustained Bitcoin breakout. (12:54)



Volatility and Upcoming Catalysts



A volatility reading near 18 was explicitly described as insufficient to constitute a buy signal while QQQ was breaking down. Negative gamma could amplify moves in both directions, while demand for longer-term protection could keep volatility elevated. (23:17)



CTAs had already reduced exposure, while other systematic strategies were still buying. The team was watching whether one-month volatility crossed above three-month volatility, which could reverse that buying. They also highlighted the following week’s FOMC meeting and Microsoft, Alphabet, and Amazon earnings as key events. (24:47)



Prediction-Market Research



Ricci discussed analysis of 976 transcripts from 10 major podcasts. He reported that negative Trump discussion preceded moves in Democratic Senate-control odds. A recent decline in that measure reflected fewer political mentions rather than more favorable coverage. (27:39)

TL;DR - POSITIONS MENTIONED



BULLISH: Brent Crude Oil (BNO), Microsoft-linked Income ETF (MSFY), Technology Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLK; possible exit), Simplify Interest Rate Hedge ETF (PFIX), Philip Morris International (PM), Amazon (AMZN; moving to buy column), Bitcoin (BTC; minimum position), Healthcare (XLV).



BEARISH: South Korea (EWY), Memory Stocks (DRAM), Russell 2000 (IWM), Germany (EWG), France (EWQ), Blackstone (BX), Silver (SLV), Palladium (PALL), India (INDA)



The summary and positions listed here reflect commentary from The Macro Show and may not represent the full scope of Keith McCullough’s current portfolio positioning. Positions listed in order mentioned on the show, not of any strength



CLICK HERE <https://model2.hedgeye.com/click/48055277.7629/aHR0cHM6Ly9hcHAuaGVkZ2V5ZS5jb20vbXUvaGVfdG1zX2ttX3JyXzEwLTIyLTIwMjY_ZW5jb2RlZF9kYXRhPWZESUIhVlpuV2xreEhCL1kyeWl3OWV1M1FjSk54RWpFPSw/65561052a51cff3724ccb7dfC9ca9dc92> to access today's slides.



MAIN SUMMARY



U.S. Positioning: Selling the Rally and Rebuilding Shorts



McCullough shifted Real-Time Alerts to two longs and four shorts, describing the change as selling the three-day rally and adding shorts that had been squeezed. He characterized the S&P 500’s downside versus upside as approximately two to one. These counts referred to the alerts, rather than his broader macro book. (13:42)



Added back to the Russell 2000 short as the index approached the upper end of its bearish Risk Range. His approach remains covering shorts near the bottom of their ranges, generally toward minimum size, and rebuilding exposure on rebounds. The Russell’s upper range boundary remained approximately 0.9% above its latest price. (7:02)



Technology Rotation: QQQ Exit, Microsoft Exposure Added



Exited QQQ and rotated capital while maintaining healthcare exposure. McCullough cited Google’s confirmed bearish TREND breakdown and the possibility of Meta breaking TREND as evidence of weakening components within the index. He did not announce short positions in either company. (7:58)



Added MSFY, identifying Microsoft as the healthiest signal within QQQ. He preferred the Microsoft-linked income fund to adding more XLK and said XLK could be exited that day; that potential exit was not presented as a completed trade. (8:17)



Asia and Europe: Maintaining Regional Shorts



Added to the South Korea short through EWY on the previous day’s bounce. McCullough reiterated shorts in DRAM, semiconductors and India, describing the overall Asian exposure as net short. He cited the KOSPI’s 3.5% overnight decline and 39.3% drawdown from its cycle peak as reasons to continue shorting rebounds. (1:52)



The process had already taken him out of Japanese equities before their nearly 3% session decline. He also highlighted China reaching a six-month low and the yen breaking higher against the dollar, describing the regional macro deterioration as more consistent with Quad 3 conditions. (2:34)



Maintained shorts in Europe, Germany through EWG and France through EWQ. French equities were down approximately another 1.5% that morning. (19:18)



Commodities: Long Oil Against Precious-Metal Shorts



Maintained the long-oil/short-silver positioning. The accompanying slides identified BNO as the Brent oil long and SLV as the silver short, with oil rising approximately 3% while silver fell roughly 3.5%–4%. McCullough also maintained his palladium short. (3:26)



Gold and silver remained in bearish TRENDs. He explicitly said he was not short gold, preferring silver and palladium because their short-side performance had been stronger. He distinguished tactical positioning from his ownership of physical gold. (4:33)



Said inflation was broader than an energy story, pointing to food, education and household costs. He emphasized that rising inflation in some commodities could coexist with short opportunities in others. (5:33)



Copper had broken TREND support. He reiterated that he was not long copper or copper miners, including Teck and Freeport-McMoRan; he did not announce new shorts in those stocks. (19:56)



Volatility: VIX Breakout Level in Play



Identified 16.89 as the VIX’s medium-term TRADE breakout level, with the upper Risk Range boundary at 19.99. He said the setup had changed and that a move into the “Chop Bucket” was in play. This was a volatility signal discussion, rather than an announced VIX trade. (14:21)



Bonds: First Lower High, PFIX Position Maintained



Flagged the first lower high in the upper Risk Range boundary for the 10-year Treasury yield, one basis point below the prior 5.31% closing high. He had not committed to changing positioning and said the intraday signal could still change. (20:17)



Continued buying PFIX, describing it as one of his largest positions. MOVE remained in a bullish TREND, with approximately 91 identified as the level that would need to break; its cited Risk Range was 94–105. I can’t put down Sylvester Stallone’s new memoir The Steps. It’s a humbling reminder of how many steps it took to get to your inbox this morning.

Stallone was born to a mother who “never wanted to have kids.” At birth, doctors accidentally crushed a nerve that partially paralyzed the left side of his face. He says: “I was left with a crooked mouth and a permanent slur. So be it.”

How many books have you judged by their covers?

Is there a certain polished, non-slurring suit on Old Wall Street that impresses you more than the work? Does the amount of money someone has really impress you, or are you looking for substance with some contrarian style?

Stallone was offered $40,000, then $90,000, then finally $360,000 for the Rocky script on one condition - he couldn’t star in it. He had $1,200 to his name, had to sell his dog, and said no.

I got fired from Carlyle for being too bearish in November 2007. The bubble peaked in October 2007. I said screw this loser culture and yes to building something better.

reports.macroGrind:
It ain’t about how hard you can “believe” in a market position or “thesis.” It’s about how hard you can get hit and keep moving onto the next play.

If our new Big Theme product (The AI Bubble) wasn’t a bubble, I wouldn’t have been long of it on the way up. I’m old enough to remember when I was long Semis via DRAM. Now I’m short it.

Need a narrative on why Semis are imploding?  That’s what bubbles do AFTER they lose their PRICE Momentum.

While it’s what we call “Layer 4” of the AI Bubble (see our Themes deck), from a market perspective the Foundry & Memory layers in South Korea are really the tip of the market pricing spear:

South Korea’s KOSPI Crash continued, down another -3.5% overnight, taking its #Quad4 Crash to -39.3%

South Korea’s economy is already in #Quad4 and we are nowcasting back-to-back #Quad4s in 1H of 2027

How many suits that are financing this bubble know what #Quad4 is, never mind understand and respect its risks? They’re our Apollo Creed and we’re not backing down from them.

They’re in a layer of the AI Bubble that I’ll never have my name on – the Funding Layer. Remember, I worked there and now I’m short Carlyle (CG), Ares (ARES), etc. We’re short Private Equity (PSP) in the aggregate.

Will you ever read this script in a note from the “rich” suits at Citigroup or Bank of America (BAC)?

We’re short them too. When everyone knows that everyone knows they’re just doing this to get paid, that’s when truth-tellers like me become unpopular. I don’t do this to be popular. I do this because my life’s steps matter.

Stallone didn’t write Rocky to get rich. He wrote it because his life’s struggle was A) true and B) ultimately a blessing.

If you really want to give them ammo on how I’m the “bad guy” shorting their narratives and “Neo-Cloud” stocks (CRWV, NBIS, IREN, etc.), send them my Top 20 Macro Shorts that include:

DRAM

PSP

EWY

IWM

XLI

Don’t send them my Silver (SLV) or Palladium (PALL) Shorts. That’s a different crowd. Most of them won’t get it. You should see how happy our subscribers who identify as Gold Bugs are with me about Bearish Gold & Silver!

In terms of next steps, what happens on the margin of risk managing this AI Bubble is what matters most. Will META join GOOGL and break bad back to Bearish TREND? If both NVDA and META break, that will be incrementally bearish.

Will AAPL and MSFT continue to be our strongest Bullish TREND Signals of the MAGs? Will the Bull Market we’ve been riding in Software Stocks (BUG) since May continue or break down alongside QQQ?

I don’t know. Nobody but The Machine does.

But God willing, I’ll be on those Philly steps at 4:30 AM every morning doing the reps. Rain, snow, or whatever. The Old Wall hates that about me and I live for that.

Stallone said no to the money because the steps mattered more than the money. So be it. If you have a lot of money, I’m happy for you. Let’s make sure you don’t lose it alongside the crowd during crashes.

reports.bigPicturePt:
Não consigo largar a nova biografia de Sylvester Stallone, The Steps. É um lembrete que coloca os pés no chão sobre quantos passos foram necessários para chegar à sua caixa de entrada nesta manhã.

Stallone nasceu de uma mãe que “nunca quis ter filhos”. No parto, os médicos acidentalmente esmagaram um nervo que paralisou parcialmente o lado esquerdo de seu rosto. Ele diz: “Fiquei com a boca torta e uma fala arrastada permanente. Que assim seja.”

Quantos livros você já julgou pela capa?

Existe algum engravatado impecável e sem a fala arrastada na Velha Wall Street que impressiona você mais do que o trabalho em si? A quantidade de dinheiro que alguém tem realmente impressiona você, ou você busca substância com algum estilo contrário (contrarian)?

Ofereceram a Stallone US$ 40.000, depois US$ 90.000 e, finalmente, US$ 360.000 pelo roteiro de Rocky sob uma única condição — ele não poderia atuar como protagonista. Ele tinha US$ 1.200 em sua conta, teve que vender seu cachorro e disse não.

Fui demitido da Carlyle por ser bearish demais em novembro de 2007. A bolha atingiu o topo em outubro de 2007. Eu disse dane-se essa cultura de perdedores e disse sim para construir algo melhor.

Obrigado por tolerarem meu estilo. É quem eu sou. Os degraus nem sempre são bonitos. Eles só precisam continuar seguindo em frente.
reports.macroGrindPt:
Não se trata de quão forte você consegue “acreditar” em uma posição de mercado ou “tese”. Trata-se de quão forte você pode ser atingido e continuar seguindo em frente para a próxima jogada.

Se o nosso novo produto de Big Theme (A Bolha de IA) não fosse uma bolha, eu não teria ficado comprado (long) nela durante o caminho de alta. Tenho idade suficiente para lembrar de quando estava long em semicondutores via DRAM. Agora estou short.

Precisa de uma narrativa sobre por que os semicondutores estão implodindo? É isso que as bolhas fazem DEPOIS que perdem seu momentum de PREÇO.

Embora seja o que chamamos de “Camada 4” da Bolha de IA (veja nossa apresentação de Themes), sob uma perspectiva de mercado, as camadas de Foundry & Memória na Coreia do Sul são verdadeiramente a ponta da lança da precificação de mercado:

O Crash do KOSPI da Coreia do Sul continuou, caindo mais -3,5% durante a noite, levando seu Crash de #Quad4 a -39,3%

A economia da Coreia do Sul já está em #Quad4 e estamos fazendo o nowcasting de #Quad4s consecutivos no 1S de 2027

Quantos dos engravatados que estão financiando essa bolha sabem o que é #Quad4, quanto mais compreendem e respeitam seus riscos? Eles são o nosso Apollo Creed e não vamos recuar diante deles.

Eles estão em uma camada da Bolha de IA na qual meu nome jamais estará envolvido — a Camada de Financiamento. Lembre-se, eu trabalhei lá e agora estou short em Carlyle (CG), Ares (ARES), etc. Estamos short em Private Equity (PSP) no agregado.

Você já leu esse roteiro em alguma nota dos engravatados “ricos” do Citigroup ou do Bank of America (BAC)?

Estamos short neles também. Quando todo mundo sabe que todo mundo sabe que eles só fazem isso para receber bônus, é aí que quem fala a verdade, como eu, se torna impopular. Eu não faço isso para ser popular. Eu faço isso porque os passos da minha vida importam.

Stallone não escreveu Rocky para ficar rico. Ele escreveu porque a luta de sua vida era A) verdadeira e B) em última análise, uma bênção.

Se você realmente quer dar munição a eles sobre como sou o “vilão” dando short em suas narrativas e ações de “Neo-Cloud” (CRWV, NBIS, IREN, etc.), envie a eles meus 20 Principais Shorts Macro, que incluem:

DRAM

PSP

EWY

IWM

XLI

Não mande a eles meus shorts em Prata (SLV) ou Paládio (PALL). Essa é outra turma. A maioria deles não vai entender. Você deveria ver como nossos assinantes que se identificam como Gold Bugs estão felizes comigo por causa do viés Bearish em Ouro & Prata!

Em termos de próximos passos, o que acontece na margem da gestão de risco desta Bolha de IA é o que mais importa. META vai se juntar a GOOGL e quebrar de volta para um TREND Bearish? Se tanto NVDA quanto META quebrarem, isso será incrementalmente bearish.

AAPL e MSFT continuarão sendo nossos sinais de TREND Bullish mais fortes entre as MAGs? O Bull Market que estamos surfando em ações de Software (BUG) desde maio continuará ou vai quebrar junto com o QQQ?

Eu não sei. Ninguém além de A Máquina sabe.

Mas, se Deus quiser, estarei naqueles degraus da Filadélfia às 4h30 todas as manhãs fazendo as repetições. Chuva, neve ou o que for. A Velha Wall Street odeia isso em mim e eu vivo para isso.

Stallone disse não ao dinheiro porque os passos importavam mais do que o dinheiro. Que assim seja. Se você tem muito dinheiro, fico feliz por você. Vamos garantir que você não o perca junto com a multidão durante os crashes.
reports.synthesisPt: Keith McCallum aborda a transição crítica na dinâmica da Bolha de IA, destacando que a gestão de risco atual exige proteger capital em vez de perseguir o momentum que começa a se romper. O aprofundamento do crash no índice KOSPI da Coreia do Sul em meio ao regime de #Quad4 valida a postura bearish na ponta de semicondutores, memórias e no financiamento via Private Equity. Paralelamente, posições vendidas em DRAM, EWY, IWM e grandes bancos refletem o desmonte em andamento, enquanto o mercado aguarda sinais de confirmação bearish em nomes como NVDA e META. Por fim, apenas papéis seletos como AAPL e MSFT sustentam sinais robustos de Bullish TREND, reforçando a necessidade de disciplina quantitativa estrita em vez de apego a narrativas de Wall Street.

TL;DR - POSITIONS MENTIONED



BULLISH: S&P 500 Equal Weight (RSP), Hedged Dow (DJIA), Healthcare (XLV), Healthcare Technology (HTEC), Technology (XLK), Software (IGV), Cybersecurity (BUG), Microsoft (MSFT), Apple (AAPL), Amazon (AMZN), Illumina (ILMN), Eli Lilly (LLY), Collateralized Loan Obligations (CLOs).



BEARISH: Long-Term Treasuries (TLT), Zero-Coupon Treasuries (ZROZ), Silver (SLV), Global Clean Energy (PBD), Qatar Equities (QAT), Industrials (XLI), Palladium (PALL), India Equities (INDA), CoreWeave (CRWV), High-Yield Corporate Bonds (HYG), Investment-Grade Corporate Bonds (LQD).



The summary and positions listed here reflect commentary from The Macro Show and may not represent the full scope of Keith McCullough’s current portfolio positioning. Positions listed in order mentioned on the show, not of any strength



CLICK HERE <https://model2.hedgeye.com/click/48026428.8663/aHR0cHM6Ly9hcHAuaGVkZ2V5ZS5jb20vbXUvaGVfdG1zX2ttX21jXzEwLTIxLTIwMjY_ZW5jb2RlZF9kYXRhPWZESVghTVRBeldBZzVuelpkT3hIcFJsWGRLaTNJYTdjPSE/65561052a51cff3724ccb7dfCdadcef5b> to access today's slides.



MAIN SUMMARY



QQQ Exited; Capital Rotating Into Broader Equity Exposure



Keith sold the remainder of QQQ yesterday and bought DJIA, replacing Nasdaq exposure with the Dow strategy’s options feature. He reiterated his preference for RSP: QQQ remains bearish TRADE/bullish TREND, while equal weight is bullish on both measures. QQQ’s TRADE resistance is 737 and TREND support is 721. (4:28) (5:03)



Software exposure has been reduced to minimum positions: IGV and BUG are each approximately 2%, alongside a 2% XLK position, totaling 6% across those holdings. XLK remains owned but could be sold; Keith highlighted its substantial Nvidia exposure. Cash gives him room to add wherever signals improve. (4:28) (23:40)



Microsoft and Apple remain bullish TRADE and TREND; Amazon has also moved to bullish TRADE and TREND. Keith emphasized that the broadening signal itself prompted the purchases. (7:00) (23:40)



Healthcare Remains a Core Long Despite Historical Quad Relationships



Keith intends to stay long healthcare after XLV reached an all-time high. He rejected selling a working position simply because healthcare has historically been a weaker sector in Quad 1 or Quad 2. He also explicitly reaffirmed the HTEC long. (8:06) (14:29) (28:19)



He cited XLV’s approximately 2.4% advance and a 4.9% gain in the most-shorted healthcare basket. Illumina was bought on weakness yesterday; after the rebound, he discussed selling some positions into strength. Eli Lilly was added to Signal Strength stocks. (11:31) (14:12)



Treasury Shorts Remain; Any Exit Will Follow Market Signals



Keith maintained the TLT and zero-coupon Treasury shorts, citing continuing yield breakouts across Japan, France, Germany and the UK. He highlighted the U.S. 10-year’s 5.10% TRADE level, France’s approximately 5% yield and UK inflation reaching an 11-month high. The U.S. 10-year risk range remains 5.06%–5.33%. (1:44) (2:22) (22:42)



When reducing bond shorts, he plans to cover zero-coupon Treasuries before TLT because of their longer duration. This is an intended sequence, not a completed position change. He expects the bond market to signal the eventual transition toward Quad 4 before discretionary forecasts do. (2:40)



VIX Supports Broad Equity Exposure While Individual Shorts Remain



VIX failed to sustain its move into the “Chop Bucket,” with that failure confirmed yesterday. Keith highlighted approximately 17.5 as an important TRADE level; a break below would bring the lower end of the range into play. The broader S&P 500 remains in the investable volatility regime. (6:21)



Watch the SPX gamma flip line at 7,726. Keith said gamma could turn positive; negative gamma has accompanied sharper rallies and declines. He maintained that broad-index exposure can coexist with shorts in deteriorating AI and semiconductor names. If short-dated volatility falls from approximately 12 toward 8–9, he would revisit the short side. (6:43) (7:19) (13:57)



International Positions and Commodity Exits



Japan has been fully exited, and the Switzerland short has been covered because it was not working. Two European shorts remain; Keith is evaluating another candidate but did not announce a new position. India remains short after declining again when its market reopened. (17:56) (18:35)



Natural gas has been exited following another TREND breakdown. Keith emphasized accepting smaller losses rather than allowing repeated false breakouts to become larger drawdowns. Silver, palladium, clean energy, Qatar and industrials remain highlighted shorts; copper could also break TREND, but he did not announce a copper short. (3:18) (19:28) (21:26)



Credit: Retaining CLO Longs Against Corporate-Credit Shorts



Keith reaffirmed long CLO exposure alongside short high-yield and investment-grade credit. The signals have kept him invested in CLOs, which he described as paying substantial income. He emphasized that Quad 2 is generally a positive nominal-growth environment rather than a broad credit event. (28:45) (30:10)



CoreWeave was cited as an existing short with high-yield financing risk. Keith identified a return to shorting private equity near the upper end of its risk range as a potential trade today, without confirming execution. He distinguished those financing risks from the CLO positions that continue to work. (29:27) (31:12)



Regime Forecasts Guide the Process; Signals Determine Positions



The monthly sequence remains Quad 2 in October, Quad 1 in November and Quad 2 in December, followed by an expected Quad 4 transition. November’s Quad 1 forecast has limited conviction: Keith cited approximately 30% probability versus 25% for Quad 2, compared with approximately 83% Quad 2 probability for December. He is not rebuilding the portfolio around November’s forecast. (2:59) (26:05)



Keith and Matt reiterated that positioning follows price, volume and volatility signals within the probabilistic macro framework. Tesla’s return to bullish TREND prevented Keith from shorting it ahead of the news despite his criticism of the company’s narrative. (14:55) (27:51)
