TL;DR - POSITIONS MENTIONED



BULLISH: Brent Oil (BNO), Health Care, Talos Energy (TALO), PBF Energy (PBF), Petrobras (PBR), Marathon Petroleum (MPC), CVR Energy (CVI), Valero Energy (VLO), Range Resources (RRC), Antero Resources (AR), Simplify Interest Rate Hedge ETF (PFIX), Invesco S&P 500 Equal Weight ETF (RSP), Nasdaq-100 (QQQ; potential exit), Japan ((JPXN) remaining long; potential exit).



BEARISH: Nvidia (NVDA), Semiconductors, European Equities, Germany (EWG), India (INDA), Qatar (QAT), U.S. Treasuries, Gold.



The summary and positions listed here reflect commentary from The Macro Show and may not represent the full scope of Keith McCullough’s current portfolio positioning. Positions listed in order mentioned on the show, not of any strength



CLICK HERE <https://model2.hedgeye.com/click/48013766.467/aHR0cHM6Ly9hcHAuaGVkZ2V5ZS5jb20vbXUvaGVfdG1zX2ttX2V2XzEwLTIwLTIwMjY_ZW5jb2RlZF9kYXRhPWZESTIhY3A0L3lTdzVLK01ubnFjUXQ0U3RCRVQvUzZVPSE/65561052a51cff3724ccb7dfC568dd0b8> to access today's slides.



MAIN SUMMARY



AI and Semiconductors: The Breakdown Continues



South Korea’s KOSPI fell another 3.7%, bringing its decline to 39.1% from the 9,114 peak. Keith described the move as a continuing crash and highlighted its connection to semiconductor weakness spreading into the Nasdaq Composite and QQQ. Hedgeye remains out of semiconductor longs. (0:57)



Nvidia returned to bearish TREND, with analyst Felix Wang turning bearish on the signal. More than 80% of the 35 names in Hedgeye’s AI-bubble basket were signaling bearish TREND; Keith said they were long none and short many of those names. (1:58)



Keith and Daryl highlighted failed headline-driven rallies in AI-related power generation and cloud stocks. Constellation Energy surrendered much of its announcement-driven surge, while CoreWeave closed lower despite an early rally and more than 101 million shares traded. Their emphasis was on price behavior rather than the headline narrative. (12:10, 13:41)



QQQ and Broad Equities: Exits Depend on Signals



Keith said he would probably exit QQQ by the end of the day, but had not confirmed a sale. He reiterated that a TREND break would trigger an exit and said he would not remain long if Nasdaq volatility moved into the 30s. (4:33, 6:04)



VIX 19 remains the key threshold for the S&P 500 to enter the “Chop Bucket.” Its move below 19 supported the prior session’s rally, but Keith highlighted the market’s retreat from its highs into the close. Nasdaq volatility was already in the Chop Bucket. (4:33)



Key TREND levels were 7,601 for the S&P 500 and 26,119 for the Nasdaq Composite. Keith said equities could break TREND before the team’s first projected Quad 4 period in February; he would follow the signals without waiting for the macro forecast to arrive. (9:07, 10:10)



Negative gamma conditions were becoming more negative, while short-dated implied volatility had fallen back toward 12. Keith said it could return to the 20s. For equity exposure, he preferred equal weighting: RSP remained bullish TREND, although on a short leash. (16:15, 27:07)



Energy: New Calls and Continued Refining Strength



Brent remains a long, with the upper end of its risk range near $114. Keith also cited propane’s approximately 34% monthly increase as evidence of substantial energy inflation, particularly in Europe. (3:12)



Energy’s signals remained substantially stronger than the AI basket’s. Approximately 80% of the oil and gas names discussed were bullish, excluding AI-linked power-generation shorts. Range Resources and Antero Resources had turned bullish. Health care also remained a long and an area Keith viewed favorably. (8:44, 10:35, 11:31)



Daryl added Talos Energy (TALO) to Small Cap Pro. Keith confirmed its bullish signal and said it had also entered his list of potential purchases. They highlighted its roughly $3 billion market capitalization and Gulf production exposure. (22:20)



Hedgeye issued a fresh real-time buy signal for PBF Energy. Daryl’s rationale centered on diesel shortages, still-wide crack spreads, strong free cash flow, and earnings estimates that needed to rise to reflect refining conditions. He emphasized reasonable valuation combined with improving earnings, rather than valuation alone. (24:12)



Keith’s selected 20-stock Signal Strength list included five energy names: Petrobras, Marathon Petroleum, CVR Energy, PBF Energy, and Valero. He emphasized that benchmark sector weights did not determine his selections. (25:55)



International Positions: Japan Exit Under Consideration



Keith sold half his Japan exposure last week and said he would probably sell the remainder that day because it had broken TREND. The remaining position was still held during the discussion. India remained one of his largest shorts, leaving the broader Asian positioning net short. (16:53)



European equities and Germany remained shorts. Keith described Germany’s setup as Quad 3 stagflation, with weakening currency and rising inflation. Daryl cited September German PPI growth of 6.7%, energy inflation of 15%, and heating-oil inflation of approximately 90%. (3:34, 17:49, 19:50)



Qatar remained Macro Pro’s longest-standing short. Keith attributed the call to the signal and macro regime. (17:49)



Rates, Financials, Gold and Bitcoin



PFIX remained a long, and the broader bearish Treasury setup was unchanged. Keith partially covered Treasury shorts the prior day as Treasury prices fell, consistent with his practice of covering some shorts on down days. (19:05)



The two-year yield had returned to bullish TRADE and TREND. The 10-year/two-year spread narrowed to approximately 26 basis points, renewing discussion of a possible yield-curve inversion and a deteriorating growth and credit outlook. (3:34)



Keith walked back the improving financials setup. JPMorgan failed to break into bullish TREND, financials returned toward neutral, and he expected further deterioration that morning. He also highlighted the flattening curve as unfavorable for the sector. (16:34, 19:05)



Gold remained bearish TRADE and TREND, and Keith said it was not an asset he wanted to own. Bitcoin formed a lower high and broke TRADE; he advised keeping exposure at minimum size. (18:33, 19:50)

reports.title: EARLY LOOK: AI Bubble Prison
reports.bigPicture:
Same goes for bubbles. First, you hate getting squeezed by them. Then you buy the damn dips in them. Enough time passes, you better have a risk management plan to get out of them.

In Shawshank, Morgan Freeman played “Red.” His narration is one of the most celebrated in movie history - we’d love for him to deliver the numbers in our AI Bubble theme deck. Inflation keeps accelerating though. He’s too expensive.

Taylor Sheridan uses Red’s quote in How To Not Die In Prison - he calls the section “Don’t Be Institutionalized.” It’s the best market advice dressed as prison survival guidance you’ll ever read.

The Macro Tourist gets institutionalized by every bubble. First he hates it. Then he chases it. Then he depends on it. Then the walls close in. Andy Dufresne had a plan before that happened. So do we.
reports.macroGrind:
AI Bubble Update: close to 80% of the 35 AI stocks in our AI “Big Theme” deck are now signaling Bearish TREND.

So, especially if you’re levered long of the AI Bubble, that’s not good. The CNBC-type “Retail Investor” is down -27% from their AI highs back at the end of May and down -10.3% YTD (GS High Retail Sentiment basket).

How do you get out of that uniquely American jail? Move to South Korea?

Ever see Squid Games? At least Shawshank gives you 19 years to figure out the escape. Squid Games (in South Korea) kills you in the first round if you don’t have a process:

KOSPI (South Korean Stock Market) was down another -3.7% overnight and closing BELOW last week’s low

KOSPI’s crash is now -39.1% from its #MOAB (Mother of All Bubbles) Peak of 9114 in June of 2026

What’s endemic to the biggest bubbles I’ve ever had to risk manage is “Retail” participation. The difference between this one and all the others is that the “rich” guys look dumber, faster.

Leopold Aschenbrenner (former OpenAI “researcher”, Columbia valedictorian at 19, born in Germany, maybe 25 years old)? He built “Situational Awareness” into a $45 billion AI-focused hedge fund using leverage as high as 400%, then watched it shed roughly $35 billion in July 2026.

Leo himself said “obviously, not blowing up is task number one and two. You have to get the timing right.” Meanwhile chrome dome Cramer posted “HE’s back, he’s bigger than ever” on September 11, 2026.

He was back all right. The mid-Septermber Semis (DRAM) bounce to lower-highs was the last chance to get out.

I couldn’t make this up if I tried but yesterday the same clown show @CNBC was running the “story” that “neocloud stocks are recovering this morning.” Then one of our Top AI Bubble Shorts, Coreweave (CRWV) proceeded to:

CRWV ended up closing DOWN on the day

CRWV traded over 101 MILLION shares vs. 10-day bubble average of 31M shares

To me, that just means this bubble isn’t nearly done imploding. If “Retail” and panic/performance-stricken Hedge Funds are still buying something like CRWV or NBIS or IREN (we’re short all 3) because its green for an hour?

And that’s not the end of it. They keep buying Semis with Levered ETFs too:

SOXL (3x Semis Bull ETF) was +5% on over 96 MILLION shares yesterday

SOXL is down -41% since the 1st week of OCTOBER and -67% from its #MOAB Peak in June

Coreweave (CRWV) actually peaked back in the summer of 2025 at $183. Maybe not ironically, like SOXL, CRWV is down -67% from its #MOAB Peak. If you’re down -67%, you need to be up +203% (from here) to get back to break-even.

So who are the bad guys in this AI Bubble Prison story?

Keith McCullough

Key Takeaways



Nearly 80% of the 35 AI stocks in Hedgeye’s AI “Big Theme” deck are now in Bearish TREND, while the high retail sentiment basket is down 27% from its May peak and 10.3% YTD.



The unwind is accelerating across the AI complex, with South Korea’s KOSPI down 39.1% from its June peak and major AI and semiconductor names like CRWV and SOXL down roughly 67% from their respective highs.



Heavy retail participation, leverage, and continued dip buying suggest the AI Bubble unwind may have further to go, reinforcing the need for a disciplined risk management process instead of becoming institutionalized by the bubble.



The Big Picture



Same goes for bubbles. First, you hate getting squeezed by them. Then you buy the damn dips in them. Enough time passes, you better have a risk management plan to get out of them.



In Shawshank, Morgan Freeman played “Red.” His narration is one of the most celebrated in movie history - we’d love for him to deliver the numbers in our AI Bubble theme deck. Inflation keeps accelerating though. He’s too expensive.



Taylor Sheridan uses Red’s quote in How To Not Die In Prison - he calls the section “Don’t Be Institutionalized.” It’s the best market advice dressed as prison survival guidance you’ll ever read.



The Macro Tourist gets institutionalized by every bubble. First he hates it. Then he chases it. Then he depends on it. Then the walls close in. Andy Dufresne had a plan before that happened. So do we.



Macro Grind

How do you get out of that uniquely American jail? Move to South Korea?



Ever see Squid Games? At least Shawshank gives you 19 years to figure out the escape. Squid Games (in South Korea) kills you in the first round if you don’t have a process:



KOSPI (South Korean Stock Market) was down another -3.7% overnight and closing BELOW last week’s low



KOSPI’s crash is now -39.1% from its #MOAB (Mother of All Bubbles) Peak of 9114 in June of 2026



What’s endemic to the biggest bubbles I’ve ever had to risk manage is “Retail” participation. The difference between this one and all the others is that the “rich” guys look dumber, faster.



Leopold Aschenbrenner (former OpenAI “researcher”, Columbia valedictorian at 19, born in Germany, maybe 25 years old)? He built “Situational Awareness” into a $45 billion AI-focused hedge fund using leverage as high as 400%, then watched it shed roughly $35 billion in July 2026.



Leo himself said “obviously, not blowing up is task number one and two. You have to get the timing right.” Meanwhile chrome dome Cramer posted “HE’s back, he’s bigger than ever” on September 11, 2026.

CRWV ended up closing DOWN on the day



CRWV traded over 101 MILLION shares vs. 10-day bubble average of 31M shares

And that’s not the end of it. They keep buying Semis with Levered ETFs too:



SOXL (3x Semis Bull ETF) was +5% on over 96 MILLION shares yesterday



SOXL is down -41% since the 1st week of OCTOBER and -67% from its #MOAB Peak in June



Coreweave (CRWV) actually peaked back in the summer of 2025 at $183. Maybe not ironically, like SOXL, CRWV is down -67% from its #MOAB Peak. If you’re down -67%, you need to be up +203% (from here) to get back to break-even.

I’m not in jail - so it’s not me. My independent research team is crushing whatever “research” the super “smart” valedictorian from Columbia was doing on AI stocks with 400% leverage and no stop loss.

reports.quotePt: Estas paredes são engraçadas. Primeiro você as odeia. Depois você se acostuma com elas. Passa tempo suficiente, você passa a depender delas.
takeawaysPt: Quase 80% das 35 ações de IA no deck do “Big Theme” de IA da Hedgeye estão agora em Bearish TREND, enquanto a cesta de alto sentimento do varejo acumula queda de 27% em relação ao pico de maio e 10,3% no ano (YTD).

A desmontagem está se acelerando em todo o complexo de IA, com o KOSPI da Coreia do Sul caindo 39,1% em relação ao seu pico de junho e grandes nomes de IA e semicondutores como CRWV e SOXL despencando cerca de 67% de suas respectivas máximas.

A pesada participação do varejo, a alavancagem e a insistência em comprar nas quedas sugerem que a desmontagem da Bolha de IA ainda tem espaço para continuar, reforçando a necessidade de um processo disciplinado de gerenciamento de risco em vez de se deixar institucionalizar pela bolha.
reports.bigPicturePt:
O mesmo vale para bolhas. Primeiro, você odeia ser espremido por elas. Depois, você compra a droga das quedas nelas. Passa tempo suficiente, é melhor você ter um plano de gerenciamento de risco para conseguir sair delas.

Em Shawshank (Um Sonho de Liberdade), Morgan Freeman interpretou “Red”. Sua narração é uma das mais celebradas na história do cinema — adoraríamos que ele apresentasse os números em nosso deck temático da Bolha de IA. A inflação continua se acelerando, no entanto. Ele é caro demais.

Taylor Sheridan usa a citação de Red em How To Not Die In Prison — ele intitula a seção de “Não Fique Institucionalizado”. É o melhor conselho de mercado disfarçado de guia de sobrevivência na prisão que você lerá na vida.

O Turista Macro se torna institucionalizado por todas as bolhas. Primeiro ele a odeia. Depois corre atrás dela. Depois passa a depender dela. Então as paredes se fecham. Andy Dufresne tinha um plano antes que isso acontecesse. Nós também temos.
reports.macroGrindPt:
Atualização da Bolha de IA: perto de 80% das 35 ações de IA em nosso deck de “Big Theme” de IA estão agora sinalizando Bearish TREND.

Portanto, especialmente se você estiver comprado alavancado na Bolha de IA, isso não é bom. O “Investidor de Varejo” típico da CNBC está em queda de -27% em relação às máximas de IA vistas no final de maio e cai -10,3% no ano (YTD) (cesta GS High Retail Sentiment).

Como você escapa dessa prisão tipicamente americana? Mudando-se para a Coreia do Sul?

Já assistiu a Round 6 (Squid Game)? Pelo menos Shawshank lhe dá 19 anos para bolar a fuga. Round 6 (na Coreia do Sul) te mata logo na primeira rodada se você não tiver um processo:

O KOSPI (mercado de ações da Coreia do Sul) caiu mais -3,7% da noite para o dia e fechou ABAIXO da mínima da semana passada

O crash do KOSPI agora atinge -39,1% em relação ao seu pico da #MOAB (Mãe de Todas as Bolhas) de 9114 em junho de 2026

O que é endêmico nas maiores bolhas que já precisei gerenciar risco é a participação do “Varejo”. A diferença entre esta e todas as outras é que os caras “ricos” passam vergonha de forma mais rápida.

Leopold Aschenbrenner (ex-“pesquisador” da OpenAI, orador da turma em Columbia aos 19 anos, nascido na Alemanha, talvez com 25 anos de idade)? Ele transformou sua “Consciência Situacional” em um hedge fund focado em IA de US$ 45 bilhões utilizando alavancagem de até 400%, para então vê-lo perder cerca de US$ 35 bilhões em julho de 2026.

O próprio Leo disse: “obviamente, não explodir é a tarefa número um e dois. Você tem que acertar o timing”. Enquanto isso, o cabeça-raspada do Cramer postou “ELE está de volta, está maior do que nunca” em 11 de setembro de 2026.

Ele estava de volta, sem dúvida. O repique de meados de setembro dos semicondutores (DRAM) em direção a topos mais baixos foi a última chance para sair.

Eu não inventaria isso nem se tentasse, mas ontem o mesmo circo na @CNBC veiculava a “história” de que “ações de neocloud estão se recuperando esta manhã”. Em seguida, uma das nossas principais posições vendidas na Bolha de IA, Coreweave (CRWV), fez o seguinte:

CRWV acabou fechando em QUEDA no dia

CRWV negociou mais de 101 MILHÕES de ações contra uma média da bolha de 10 dias de 31 milhões de ações

Para mim, isso significa apenas que esta bolha está longe de terminar de implodir. Se o “Varejo” e hedge funds desesperados por performance ou tomados pelo pânico continuam comprando ativos como CRWV, NBIS ou IREN (estamos vendidos nas 3) só porque ficaram no verde por uma hora?

E não para por aí. Eles continuam comprando semicondutores através de ETFs alavancados também:

SOXL (ETF 3x Bull de Semicondutores) subiu +5% com mais de 96 MILHÕES de ações negociadas ontem

SOXL acumula queda de -41% desde a 1ª semana de OUTUBRO e -67% em relação ao seu pico da #MOAB em junho

A Coreweave (CRWV) atingiu seu pico real no verão de 2025 a US$ 183. E, talvez não por ironia, assim como o SOXL, CRWV cai -67% do seu pico da #MOAB. Se você está caindo -67%, precisa de uma alta de +203% (a partir daqui) apenas para voltar ao zero a zero (break-even).

Então, quem são os vilões nessa história de Prisão da Bolha de IA?

Eu não estou preso — então não sou eu. Minha equipe de pesquisa independente está massacrando qualquer que tenha sido a “pesquisa” que o orador super “inteligente” de Columbia estava fazendo com ações de IA a 400% de alavancagem e sem stop loss.

Talvez todos eles devessem fazer seus sistemas “inteligentes” de IA baixarem o Hedgeye Cockpit para Análise da Bolha de IA e aprenderem alguma coisa. Temos pesquisadores geniais (“wicked-smah-t”), vindos ou não da Ivy League, em nossa equipe!

Como ler o cockpit: 3 perguntas, seguidas pelas luzes de alerta. Leia de cima para baixo: quão frágil é a estrutura de IA, qual a probabilidade de uma ruptura em breve, qual seria o tamanho do estrago e se há algo se movendo?

Tudo está sempre se movendo. Você possui a leitura fractal sobre isso ou continua institucionalizado por Old Wall?
reports.synthesisPt: Cerca de 80% das ações temáticas do complexo de inteligência artificial monitoradas pela Hedgeye entraram formalmente em Bearish TREND, indicando um colapso em pleno andamento. O movimento de desalavancagem atinge proporções severas, exemplificado pela queda de quase 40% no KOSPI sul-coreano e baixas de 67% em ativos de alto beta como CRWV e SOXL. Fundos altamente alavancados e o varejo continuam insistindo na compra de repiques intradiários, postergando o processo de capitulação final da bolha. Keith reforça que a sobrevivência no mercado exige fugir das narrativas de Old Wall e aplicar uma disciplina quantitativa e fractal de gerenciamento de risco.

VIEW LINK



Hedgeye CEO Keith McCullough and Director of Research Daryl Jones walked through the small cap product and how the machine reads price momentum on The Macro Show this morning.



Small caps have been decimated, peaking around August 14th, with 80% down since.



They trade together, so the factor exposure is a certified disaster, negative across the board on a one-week, one-month, and three-month basis.



Even so, the small cap product validated the signal plus fundamentals, outperforming the Russell by 1,400 basis points in its first quarter.



The energy product Keith and Jonesy are building together is doing the same.



The coaching point is the discipline behind that outperformance. Read the numbers across the page the way the machine does, in ones and zeros, not through an analyst’s narrative.



As Keith put it, “stop buying the stocks that you or the analysts like, buy the stocks that the machine and therefore Mucker likes.”



It’s not about treating every idea equally, it’s about rewarding the ones with the best behavior, like Jakks Pacific (JAKK), which has been a huge winner and screens positive across durations.



The single most important column is price momentum at three weeks or less.



Most hedge fund risk platforms use one month as their duration, which is why Keith built his shorter. Positive TRADE but bearish TREND is a wait and watch, and a positive TREND that breaks TRADE gets cut to the minimum.



As he put it, “the causality between trade breaks and trends has never been more obvious to me.”

TL;DR - POSITIONS MENTIONED



BULLISH: U.S. Dollar (USD), Natural Gas (UNG), Brent Crude (BNO), Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ), Technology Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLK), Software (IGV), Health Care (XLV), Simplify Interest Rate Hedge ETF (PFIX), Microsoft (MSFT), Apple (AAPL), Meta Platforms (META), Japan, Bitcoin (BTC).



BEARISH: Long-Term U.S. Treasuries (TLT), High-Yield Credit, Russell 2000 (IWM), Industrials, CoreWeave (CRWV), IREN (IREN), Nebius (NBIS), South Korea (KOSPI), India (INDA), Europe.



The summary and positions listed here reflect commentary from The Macro Show and may not represent the full scope of Keith McCullough’s current portfolio positioning. Positions listed in order mentioned on the show, not of any strength



CLICK HERE <https://model2.hedgeye.com/click/47986424.7708/aHR0cHM6Ly9hcHAuaGVkZ2V5ZS5jb20vbXUvaGVfdG1zX2ttX2RqXzEwLTE5LTIwMjY_ZW5jb2RlZF9kYXRhPWZEZ0YhUTBYRmx2UHltbFRoUmpTUkFEMzdHN3JzNnFjPSw/65561052a51cff3724ccb7dfCc572b046> to access today's slides.



MAIN SUMMARY



Position Changes and Recent Trades



Covered the financials short after the sector moved to a bullish trend late last week. McCullough is now looking to buy dips in financials. (12:47)



Cut Japan exposure in half by selling one entire position. The Nikkei was testing trend support, prompting a reduction in exposure. (18:04)



Bought the dip in software late last week. McCullough expects earnings season to support selected software stocks and maintained the distinction between software longs and semiconductor weakness. (8:49) (9:10)



Added to the India short through real-time alerts near the upper end of its risk range. He described an expected 1%–3% decline toward the middle of the range following that entry. (18:46)



Bought the dollar following its approximately 0.4% weekly decline. (1:43)



QQQ and Technology: Minimum Positions, With Trend Support Decisive



QQQ and XLK remained at minimum allocations of 2% each, totaling 4% exposure. Their short-term weakness had not produced the trend breakdown required for an exit. McCullough said he would exit QQQ if the Nasdaq’s trend broke. (3:56) (4:13) (5:19)



Nasdaq Composite trend support was 26,119, with immediate-term trade resistance at 26,817. He described the Nasdaq’s roughly 4% decline from its high as a correction requiring disciplined sizing. (3:20) (5:42)



Microsoft, Apple, and Meta remained the preferred bullish trends. Google, Nvidia, Netflix, Amazon, and Tesla were bearish on both trade and trend; McCullough said their declines should not be treated as buying opportunities. (17:02)



Health care remained the longest-standing U.S. sector long, up nearly 5% month to date. Technology was a more recent position. (12:24)



Volatility and S&P 500 Levels



Watch VIX levels of 19 and 17.48. McCullough said a decline below both could support a return to all-time highs in the S&P 500. Nasdaq volatility had reached approximately 27, placing it in the “Chop Bucket.” (5:19) (6:19)



S&P 500 trade resistance was 7,725, with trend support at 7,601. The stated risk range was 7,611–7,852, leaving potential upside above the previous high of 7,818 if support held. (9:10) (10:11)



The negative-gamma setup could accelerate rallies as well as declines. The cited gamma flip level was 7,753. (15:50)



Inflation and Rates: Positioning Unchanged



Last week’s Treasury rally did not break the prevailing yield trends. McCullough maintained the bond shorts, citing another increase in the inflation nowcast. For the 10-year Treasury yield, he highlighted 5.10% as the immediate-term trade level and 4.84% as trend support. (1:43) (2:30)



The October CPI nowcast had increased another 14 basis points. Jonesy highlighted diesel prices rising approximately 127% year over year, while both speakers emphasized energy and food costs feeding into inflation. (21:55) (22:19) (22:44)



McCullough maintained the Quad 2 framework and expected a Quad 2 earnings season. He said rising inflation was inconsistent with a current Quad 4 designation, while retaining the expectation of Quad 4 in the first quarter. He also argued that postponing a pre-election rate hike could force a December hike just before inflation rolled over. (10:38) (23:28) (24:31)



Credit and AI Shorts Remain Central



Maintained shorts in high-yield credit and AI infrastructure names, including CoreWeave, IREN, and Nebius. High-yield spreads were approximately 331 basis points, while CoreWeave credit-default-swap spreads were approximately 1,000 basis points. (14:29)



McCullough described rebounds in CoreWeave and South Korea as short-selling opportunities. He said shorting the identified weak technology exposures was his preferred way to hedge technology longs. (15:23)



Twenty-six of 35 names in Hedgeye’s AI bubble presentation were signaling bearish trends. Across Signal Strength, shorts outnumbered longs approximately three to one; ETF Pro held approximately 20 macro shorts. (4:57) (9:53) (16:25)



Energy, Bond Volatility, and Bitcoin



Maintained Brent crude and natural gas longs. Brent had the stronger oil signal and was signaling potential cycle highs around $110–$111. Those energy signals also supported maintaining the bearish bond position. (11:48) (19:01)



Bond volatility remained bullish despite PFIX’s pullback. McCullough emphasized trimming near the upper end of the range and adding in increments of 50–100 basis points of portfolio exposure. (13:48)



Maintained the Bitcoin long. Bitcoin had regained its approximately $82,000 trade level and held roughly $77,000 trend support. McCullough highlighted its positive 15–30-day correlation with the dollar. (21:21)



Small Caps and the Risk-Management Process



Maintained shorts in industrials and the Russell 2000. Over three months, industrials had fallen nearly 7% and the Russell approximately 8.5%, versus a roughly 3.5% Nasdaq gain. Jonesy said approximately 80% of small caps had declined since their peak. (13:25) (25:19)



Jonesy reported approximately 1,400 basis points of Russell outperformance from the small-cap research selections over one quarter. McCullough emphasized buying names supported by the signals and excluding ideas on the bench. (25:19) (27:32)



McCullough reiterated the sizing rule: a bullish-trend position that breaks trade is reduced to its minimum. He highlighted one-month price momentum as a critical monitoring tool and defined his immediate-term trading horizon as three weeks or less. (29:58) (31:02) (31:50)

BULLISH: U.S. Dollar (USD), Natural Gas (UNG), Brent Crude (BNO), Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ), Technology Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLK), Software (IGV), Health Care (XLV), Simplify Interest Rate Hedge ETF (PFIX), Microsoft (MSFT), Apple (AAPL), Meta Platforms (META), Japan, Bitcoin (BTC).



BEARISH: Long-Term U.S. Treasuries (TLT), High-Yield Credit, Russell 2000 (IWM), Industrials, CoreWeave (CRWV), IREN (IREN), Nebius (NBIS), South Korea (KOSPI), India (INDA), Europe.



The summary and positions listed here reflect commentary from The Macro Show and may not represent the full scope of Keith McCullough’s current portfolio positioning. Positions listed in order mentioned on the show, not of any strength



CLICK HERE <https://model2.hedgeye.com/click/47986424.7708/aHR0cHM6Ly9hcHAuaGVkZ2V5ZS5jb20vbXUvaGVfdG1zX2ttX2RqXzEwLTE5LTIwMjY_ZW5jb2RlZF9kYXRhPWZEZ0YhUTBYRmx2UHltbFRoUmpTUkFEMzdHN3JzNnFjPSw/65561052a51cff3724ccb7dfCc572b046> to access today's slides.



MAIN SUMMARY



Position Changes and Recent Trades



Covered the financials short after the sector moved to a bullish trend late last week. McCullough is now looking to buy dips in financials. (12:47)



Cut Japan exposure in half by selling one entire position. The Nikkei was testing trend support, prompting a reduction in exposure. (18:04)



Bought the dip in software late last week. McCullough expects earnings season to support selected software stocks and maintained the distinction between software longs and semiconductor weakness. (8:49) (9:10)



Added to the India short through real-time alerts near the upper end of its risk range. He described an expected 1%–3% decline toward the middle of the range following that entry. (18:46)



Bought the dollar following its approximately 0.4% weekly decline. (1:43)



QQQ and Technology: Minimum Positions, With Trend Support Decisive



QQQ and XLK remained at minimum allocations of 2% each, totaling 4% exposure. Their short-term weakness had not produced the trend breakdown required for an exit. McCullough said he would exit QQQ if the Nasdaq’s trend broke. (3:56) (4:13) (5:19)



Nasdaq Composite trend support was 26,119, with immediate-term trade resistance at 26,817. He described the Nasdaq’s roughly 4% decline from its high as a correction requiring disciplined sizing. (3:20) (5:42)



Microsoft, Apple, and Meta remained the preferred bullish trends. Google, Nvidia, Netflix, Amazon, and Tesla were bearish on both trade and trend; McCullough said their declines should not be treated as buying opportunities. (17:02)



Health care remained the longest-standing U.S. sector long, up nearly 5% month to date. Technology was a more recent position. (12:24)



Volatility and S&P 500 Levels



Watch VIX levels of 19 and 17.48. McCullough said a decline below both could support a return to all-time highs in the S&P 500. Nasdaq volatility had reached approximately 27, placing it in the “Chop Bucket.” (5:19) (6:19)



S&P 500 trade resistance was 7,725, with trend support at 7,601. The stated risk range was 7,611–7,852, leaving potential upside above the previous high of 7,818 if support held. (9:10) (10:11)



The negative-gamma setup could accelerate rallies as well as declines. The cited gamma flip level was 7,753. (15:50)



Inflation and Rates: Positioning Unchanged



Last week’s Treasury rally did not break the prevailing yield trends. McCullough maintained the bond shorts, citing another increase in the inflation nowcast. For the 10-year Treasury yield, he highlighted 5.10% as the immediate-term trade level and 4.84% as trend support. (1:43) (2:30)



The October CPI nowcast had increased another 14 basis points. Jonesy highlighted diesel prices rising approximately 127% year over year, while both speakers emphasized energy and food costs feeding into inflation. (21:55) (22:19) (22:44)



McCullough maintained the Quad 2 framework and expected a Quad 2 earnings season. He said rising inflation was inconsistent with a current Quad 4 designation, while retaining the expectation of Quad 4 in the first quarter. He also argued that postponing a pre-election rate hike could force a December hike just before inflation rolled over. (10:38) (23:28) (24:31)



Credit and AI Shorts Remain Central



Maintained shorts in high-yield credit and AI infrastructure names, including CoreWeave, IREN, and Nebius. High-yield spreads were approximately 331 basis points, while CoreWeave credit-default-swap spreads were approximately 1,000 basis points. (14:29)



McCullough described rebounds in CoreWeave and South Korea as short-selling opportunities. He said shorting the identified weak technology exposures was his preferred way to hedge technology longs. (15:23)



Twenty-six of 35 names in Hedgeye’s AI bubble presentation were signaling bearish trends. Across Signal Strength, shorts outnumbered longs approximately three to one; ETF Pro held approximately 20 macro shorts. (4:57) (9:53) (16:25)



Energy, Bond Volatility, and Bitcoin



Maintained Brent crude and natural gas longs. Brent had the stronger oil signal and was signaling potential cycle highs around $110–$111. Those energy signals also supported maintaining the bearish bond position. (11:48) (19:01)



Bond volatility remained bullish despite PFIX’s pullback. McCullough emphasized trimming near the upper end of the range and adding in increments of 50–100 basis points of portfolio exposure. (13:48)



Maintained the Bitcoin long. Bitcoin had regained its approximately $82,000 trade level and held roughly $77,000 trend support. McCullough highlighted its positive 15–30-day correlation with the dollar. (21:21)



Small Caps and the Risk-Management Process



Maintained shorts in industrials and the Russell 2000. Over three months, industrials had fallen nearly 7% and the Russell approximately 8.5%, versus a roughly 3.5% Nasdaq gain. Jonesy said approximately 80% of small caps had declined since their peak. (13:25) (25:19)



Jonesy reported approximately 1,400 basis points of Russell outperformance from the small-cap research selections over one quarter. McCullough emphasized buying names supported by the signals and excluding ideas on the bench. (25:19) (27:32)



McCullough reiterated the sizing rule: a bullish-trend position that breaks trade is reduced to its minimum. He highlighted one-month price momentum as a critical monitoring tool and defined his immediate-term trading horizon as three weeks or less. (29:58) (31:02) (31:50)

New Range Charts: We've added visualizations to show where each ticker is trading within its Risk Range™ — highlighting proximity to the Top End (TRR) or Low End (LRR).



TXG



Sector: Healthcare

Sector Head: Tom Tobin



THESIS SUMMARY:



TXG remains a Long as stronger-than-expected Single Cell demand, accelerating Atera interest, and growing exposure to the AI application layer support a stronger multi-year growth outlook. Atera demand is already running well ahead of the initial 40-system 2026 target, with manufacturing capacity — not customer interest — now the primary constraint, while temporary Spatial softness reflects customers delaying purchases ahead of the new platform rollout. With 2027 estimates already above consensus and management seeing significant pull-through from Atera, the setup points to meaningful upside if adoption continues to outpace expectations.



WEEKEND UPDATE:



TXG has moved from Active Long to Long Bench after losing positive Signal Strength and seeing its Quad Factor Score deteriorate, despite continued strength in spatial genomics adoption and NIH funding.



Moved from Active Long to Long Bench on October 16 after losing positive Signal Strength and seeing its Quad Factor Score weaken, removing two key conditions for maintaining an active position.



FY26 NIH single-cell and spatial awards rose 6.5% to $3.25 billion, outperforming overall NIH funding, which declined 0.2%. Spatial-only awards grew 23.9% to $705 million, supporting the longer-term adoption thesis.



NIH funding growth slowed from 43.0% in June to 6.5%, while September awards declined 24.3%. Hedgeye still expects a Q3 revenue beat, but softer tracking data and weaker market signals warrant patience before reactivating the Long.



DT



Sector: Software

Sector Head: Andrew Freedman, CFA



THESIS SUMMARY:



DT is a Long as newly confirmed Signal Strength adds support to an observability name positioned in one of the infrastructure-software segments with the most upside. Its comparable exposure to DDOG gives Dynatrace leverage to rising observability demand as AI workloads and system complexity continue to expand.



WEEKEND UPDATE:



DT remains a Long as accelerating usage trends, durable recurring revenue growth, and expanding AI-related observability demand continue to strengthen the setup.



DT remains a Signal Strength Long on the bench, with the stock holding up well through the recent software drawdown and continuing to show relative strength versus weaker peers.



A shift toward consumption-based billing is driving accelerating usage trends that the desk views as more durable than what it is seeing at MongoDB, while the Arise acquisition is expected to add roughly 200 basis points to annual recurring revenue growth on top of DT’s stable mid-to-high-teens growth rate.



Additional upside optionality comes from observability becoming increasingly important for AI training and self-healing software, while Dynatrace’s history of activist involvement and ongoing M&A speculation provide potential additional catalysts.



MSFT



Sector: Global Technology

Sector Head: Felix Wang, CFA



THESIS SUMMARY:



MSFT remains a Long as accelerating Azure demand and strong secular AI spending support durable, economy-independent revenue growth. OpenAI’s July revenue accelerated roughly 20% month-over-month to a $40 billion-plus ARR run rate, reinforcing the improving AI demand trends that previously signaled an Azure inflection. MSFT’s exposure to accelerating Pod 1 revenue growth is particularly attractive in Quad 3, where companies delivering strong organic growth regardless of the macro environment have historically outperformed.



WEEKEND UPDATE:



MSFT remains a Long and Signal Strength Long, supported by bullish TRADE and TREND signals, continued leadership among S&P 500 mega-cap stocks, and expanding opportunities across AI infrastructure and consumer hardware.



MSFT continues to signal bullish TRADE and TREND alongside Apple (AAPL) and Meta (META), with its Signal Strength Long reinforcing the constructive technical setup. Large-cap technology stocks drove much of the S&P 500's performance last week, supporting the desk's decision to shift MSFT from its prior Short position to a Long.



Microsoft is expanding its competitive position in AI-powered hardware with the launch of its Surface Laptop Ultra, targeting Apple's MacBook Pro. Powered by NVIDIA's RTX Spark Superchip and offering up to 128GB of unified memory, the new device strengthens Microsoft's push into high-performance AI computing, with potential demand trends to be assessed through a Social Barometer.



The longer-term thesis remains centered on Microsoft's AI infrastructure and software ecosystem, though evolving visa policies introduce a potential labor-related risk. Recent H-1B and J-1 announcements and potential changes to the PERM employment-based immigration process could affect technology companies' access to skilled workers, with the impact to be monitored as labor data develops.



CRWD



Sector: Software

Sector Head: Andrew Freedman, CFA



THESIS SUMMARY:



CRWD remains a Long with Signal Strength as enterprise cybersecurity spending accelerates and AI expands the number of attack surfaces companies must protect. Broader security demand should support accelerating Pod 1 revenue and backlog growth into earnings. CRWD also reached the low end of its risk range, creating an attractive entry point as software continues to outperform semiconductors.



WEEKEND UPDATE:



CRWD remains a Signal Strength Long and a preferred cybersecurity name, supported by accelerating recurring revenue, strong Falcon Flex adoption, and rising AI-related security demand.



CRWD remains Signal Strength Long, added August 21, and is the desk’s favored fundamental cybersecurity name, supported by resilient enterprise security spending.



Always-on AI agents and greater system interoperability could increase cybersecurity vulnerabilities by as much as 100x, driving demand for CrowdStrike’s security solutions through year-end.



Net new ARR accelerated 51% year over year, while Falcon Flex ARR rose 101% to $2.29 billion. The upper end of CRWD’s risk range remains a potential point where upside momentum could stall.



PBR



Sector: Energy

Sector Head: Daryl Jones



THESIS SUMMARY:



PBR remains an Active Long as record production, improving refining profitability and a formulaic dividend support the thesis, while the stock still trades at a significant valuation discount to global oil peers. The potential suspension of Brazil’s 12% crude export tax would provide an additional free-cash-flow and dividend catalyst, although the tax remains in legal limbo and government intervention remains the key risk. Higher crude prices are also supporting the stock, while Petrobras is seeking a roughly 1 real-per-liter diesel price increase that could improve domestic pricing economics if approved.



WEEKEND UPDATE:



PBR remains an Active Long as strong production growth, attractive dividends, and the potential for reduced government intervention support the thesis, with Brazil’s presidential runoff providing an additional catalyst.



PBR is up nearly 30% since its August 24 addition as an Active Long, versus a 1.3% decline for XLE, as Flávio’s first-round election lead over Lula raises expectations for a more market-friendly government.



Liquids production grew 15.2% year over year to 2.689 million barrels per day in Q2, while PBR’s roughly 3.8x EV/EBITDA valuation remains well below Exxon and Chevron, supporting further upside potential.



Dividends and political upside remain key drivers, with $0.87 per ADR in declared distributions through Q2 and the October 25 runoff offering potential for a narrower valuation discount. Lower oil prices, higher capital spending, and continued state intervention remain risks.



WST



Sector: Healthcare

Sector Head: Tom Tobin



THESIS SUMMARY:



WST is a Signal Strength Long, added September 18, and recently moved to the Long Bench as easing GLP-1-related headwinds support an improving healthcare outlook. Increased early-stage patient monitoring and medical visits as Medicare patients begin using GLP-1 drugs could provide an additional demand catalyst. With the stock trading near the low end of its risk range, further weakness could present an attractive buying opportunity, supported by the desk’s broader bullish view on healthcare and biotechnology.



WEEKEND UPDATE:



WEEKEND UPDATE:



WST remains a Long Bias despite losing Signal Strength on October 8, as its Bullish TREND, attractive entry point, and improving GLP-1 outlook support the upside thesis.



Featured on The Call, where Keith McCullough and Tom Tobin highlighted WST's Bullish TREND signal and favored buying healthcare stocks amid broader sector weakness.



WST is trading near the low end of its daily risk range, offering a potentially attractive entry point despite losing Signal Strength on October 8.



The longer-term thesis remains supported by easing GLP-1 headwinds and increased drug utilization among Medicare patients, potentially driving demand for WST's pharmaceutical packaging and delivery products.



DKS



Sector: Retail

Sector Head: Brian McGough



THESIS SUMMARY:



The business is still overearning while growth decelerates, with the Foot Locker acquisition viewed as structurally dilutive and a potential source of significant capital destruction. House of Sport adds another capital-allocation concern, while current guidance is not viewed as conservative enough to create an easy earnings reset. With growth investors avoiding the slowdown, GARP investors lacking a reacceleration catalyst, and value investors unlikely to step in near current levels, DKS remains Signal Strength Short with downside seen well below $100.



WEEKEND UPDATE:



DKS remains an Active Short and Signal Strength Short as slowing core growth, Foot Locker integration risks, and a prolonged recovery in the athletic retail channel continue to pressure the outlook.



DKS remains Signal Strength Short and has not yet reached the low end of its risk range, suggesting additional downside potential as the athletic retail channel remains under pressure.



Nike’s recent earnings report presents additional read-through risk for DKS, with the athletic channel expected to remain at least 12 to 18 months away from a meaningful comparable-sales recovery.



Foot Locker integration and House of Sport expansion continue to create significant capital requirements, while additional debt financing and slowing core growth reinforce the Short thesis.



SAIA



Sector: Industrials

Sector Head: Jay Van Sciver



THESIS SUMMARY:



The LTL industry has excess capacity and no longer has a large pool of high-cost unionized freight to donate share, leaving non-union carriers like SAIA fighting harder for volume in an increasingly commoditized market. Recent data reinforce that pressure, with SAIA shipments up just 1.1% in August versus more than 5% growth at XPO, while Amazon's entry and FedEx Freight's willingness to chase volume on price add further competitive risk. With pricing beginning to roll over and growth still lagging peers, SAIA remains both a Signal Strength Short and an Active Best Idea Short.



WEEKEND UPDATE:



SAIA remains an Active Best Idea Short and Signal Strength Short as weak shipment growth, limited industry expansion, and elevated valuations reinforce the downside thesis across less-than-truckload (LTL) trucking.



SAIA remains a Signal Strength Short alongside ArcBest (ARCB) and Old Dominion (ODFL), with the desk viewing the broader LTL group as a once-in-a-decade Short opportunity in transports.



August shipments grew just 1.1% versus more than 5% for XPO, reinforcing continued share losses as the industry's historical growth advantage from displacing higher-cost unionized competitors has largely disappeared.



Industry growth has stalled despite valuations near 40x earnings, leaving significant downside risk as investors continue to favor these historically strong operators despite deteriorating fundamentals.



DKNG



Sector: Gaming Lodging & Leisure

Sector Head: Sean Jenkins



THESIS SUMMARY:



DraftKings (DKNG) remains a Short as growing legal uncertainty around prediction-market sports betting threatens a business the company has already committed nearly $1 billion of capital and P&L exposure to building. The widening split among federal appeals courts increases the likelihood of Supreme Court review, creating a major regulatory overhang while multiple states continue challenging prediction-market sports contracts as unlicensed gambling. DKNG remains Signal Strength Short and in a bearish trading trend after a recent failed attempt to turn bullish.



WEEKEND UPDATE:



DKNG remains a Short Bias and Signal Strength Short as weak NFL betting results, market share pressures, and rising prediction-market risks reinforce the downside thesis.



DKNG remains bearish on both TRADE and TREND, with flat to declining U.S. market share and greater exposure to weekly sports-betting volatility supporting further downside.



NFL Week 5 marked the third consecutive week of below-average sportsbook hold, with four of the first five weeks underperforming. Weak betting outcomes increase the risk of a Q3 earnings miss and downward revisions to 2026 guidance.



DKNG is investing nearly $1 billion cumulatively in prediction markets despite significant legal uncertainty. A potential Supreme Court or federal ruling within 12 months could reshape competition, adding risk to an already pressured business.

But they can “give” your kids some stock! Very cool. Eight seconds of clickbait well spent.

In

Grapes Of Wrath

, Steinbeck asked “who the bank” was in 1939. Reis resurfaces it in the new bestseller

Incorruptible

: tenant farmers evicted during the Dust Bowl couldn’t find who was making the decisions.

“A faceless system in which no individual can be held accountable, even though real people are losing their homes and livelihoods.”

Sound familiar?

The

AI Bubble

monster was made by humans, funded by humans, and promoted by humans. But now that the

AI Credit Event

is developing and the levered Neoclouds are imploding, nobody seems to know who’s in charge…

The bank isn’t like a man. But it’s made of men and women. And in 1939 and 2026, those people are unsurprisingly hard to find when the High Yield eviction notices arrive.

Welcome to another

Macro Monday @Hedgeye!

If we have any more weeks like last week, we’ll be transitioning our portfolios towards

#Quad4 instead of #Quad2!

While losing money in our Long Software (BUG) and Tech (XLK) positions for a week wasn’t enjoyable, consider the alternative – you could be losing money in Semis, Neoclouds, and AI Bubble Stocks since June!

One week, of course, defines most

Counter-TREND

moves. While one-week is indeed “three-weeks or less” (i.e., our immediate-term TRADE risk management duration), what happens in weeks 2 and 3 really matter, so we’ll see…

That’s all uniquely American US Stock Market stuff, obviously. What did the

Currency Market

think:

US Dollar Index only corrected -0.4% to +1.6% in the last month

We bought more USD via UUP because this was a Counter TREND correction in the USD Index

Since Bitcoin still has a positive correlation to USD, we stayed with both that and QQQ despite their -1.3% and -4.5% corrections last week. If you can’t withstand a -2-6% correction in something, you’re not long for

The Game.

As long-time subscribers to our process know:

In #Quad2 we’ve been paid to be long of Bitcoin and QQQ at the same time (remember 2021?)

Uma semana, evidentemente, define a maioria dos movimentos de Counter-TREND. Embora uma semana seja de fato "três semanas ou menos" (ou seja, nossa duração de gerenciamento de risco de TRADE de prazo imediato), o que acontece nas semanas 2 e 3 realmente importa, então veremos...

Isso tudo são questões exclusivamente do mercado de ações dos EUA, obviamente. O que o Mercado de Câmbio achou:

O US Dollar Index apenas corrigiu de -0,4% para +1,6% no último mês

Como o Bitcoin ainda mantém correlação positiva com o USD, continuamos posicionados tanto nele quanto no QQQ, apesar de suas correções de -1,3% e -4,5% na semana passada. Se você não consegue suportar uma correção de -2% a -6% em algo, você não vai durar muito no Jogo (The Game).

No #Quad2, somos pagos para ficar comprados em Bitcoin e QQQ ao mesmo tempo (lembra de 2021?)

No #Quad4, Bitcoin e QQQ são massacrados

A outra coisa que acontece no #Quad4 e que não acontece no #Quad2 é que os rendimentos dos títulos (Bond Yields) quebram o TRADE e o TREND:

O rendimento do UST 2yr caiu apenas -7 pontos-base na semana passada e permanece em Bullish TRADE e TREND ao lado do USD

O rendimento do UST 10yr caiu -16 pontos-base na semana passada, quebrando o TRADE de 5.10%, mas sustentando o TREND de 4.84%

Portanto, o rendimento de 10 anos mal quebrou o TRADE e pode facilmente recuperar esse patamar de 5.10% nesta semana. Por quê? A inflação nos EUA continua a acelerar.

Commodities NÃO fazem isso no #Quad4 (elas despencam nesse Quad):

O CRB Commodities Index inflacionou mais +1,2% na semana passada, levando seu retorno em TREND de 3 meses para +11,7%

Ações de Energia (XLE) subiram mais +4,9% na semana passada, atingindo +19,7% nos últimos 3 meses. Isso também não acontece no #Quad4.

A verdade é também que estar vendido tanto no Ciclo de Crédito (HYG, PSP, etc.) quanto em Cíclicos (nosso Short em XLI caiu -6,9% em 3 meses) coloca você em excelente posição sob a ótica do Ciclo Completo de Investimento (Full Investing Cycle).

Steinbeck disse que os homens criaram o monstro, mas não conseguem controlá-lo. O ciclo de financiamento do monstro já está no espelho retrovisor do ROC. A verdade sobre o que está na SUA conta não é sem rosto. Ela tem data e hora (timestamped).

Você terá que decidir onde ficar Long e Short nos estágios finais (meses) do #Quad2.

Nós já temos muitas posições vendidas montadas. Por quanto tempo permaneceremos Long em Software (IGV)? Vamos ver o que Os Sinais dirão, não é mesmo.
reports.synthesisPt: Apesar do selloff recente em tecnologia e software, os sinais macro mais amplos ainda apontam para o estágio final de #Quad2 em vez de uma transição para #Quad4. A firmeza do dólar, do Bitcoin e dos rendimentos dos Treasuries, somada à disparada das commodities e da energia, sinaliza aceleração contínua da inflação, comportamento incompatível com o Quad4. Ao mesmo tempo, a fraqueza no ciclo de crédito e nos ativos cíclicos confirma a eficácia das posições vendidas já adotadas. O foco da gestão de risco agora reside em monitorar os sinais de TRADE e TREND para determinar o momento exato de encerrar as posições compradas em tecnologia.

takeawaysPt: Os rendimentos dos títulos reverteram para baixo após o CPI à medida que os spreads de High Yield se alargaram, sinalizando estresse de crédito crescente mesmo com o Fed posicionado para aumentos adicionais de juros.

Os gastos com infraestrutura de IA e a alavancagem permanecem como riscos centrais, com a Hedgeye vendida (short) em CoreWeave, IREN, Nebius e Oracle diante do aperto nas condições de financiamento e queima de caixa elevada.

A Bolha de IA apresenta sinais mais amplos de estresse entre ações e crédito, destacados pelo recuo de 39% do KOSPI em relação ao pico da #MOAB e pelos spreads de High Yield abrindo 59 pontos-base no último mês.

Depois que minha equipe cravou o relatório do CPI no literal (e, portanto, matemático) ponto-base ontem, O Jogo avançou para o que sempre faz – a próxima jogada!

Revisando a fita do mercado de títulos:

Os rendimentos dos títulos dispararam em direção ao TRR (topo do sinal do Risk Range™) com a 'notícia' do CPI

Em seguida, os rendimentos dos títulos despencaram enquanto os spreads de High Yield explodiram junto com as ações de 'Crédito' de IA

Agora, 'por que' isso pode acontecer? Bem, deixe-me dar uma narrativa:

O CPI reforçou a ideia de que o Fed fará mais um aumento de juros

Subir juros em meio a um Evento de Crédito (4T de 2026) e a uma desaceleração do PIB (1S de 2027) não é bom

Então... agora temos a seguinte configuração no mercado de títulos:

O indicador antecedente do Fed (rendimento dos UST de 2 anos) se aproximando de seu LRR (piso do sinal do Risk Range™), mas ainda sinalizando altas

O spread OAS de High Yield abriu +11 pontos-base dia contra dia e +59 bps mês contra mês

Boas notícias, mãe: a Família está vendida (short) em High Yield (HYG)!

A sua mãe sabe quantos dos amigos aposentados dela estão sendo depenados pelo que meu amigo Dave Rasmussen, da Verdad Capital, chama de 'Fool’s Yield' (Rendimento dos Tolos)? Quantas contas de aposentadoria estão se afogando tanto no lado de Ações quanto no de Crédito da Bolha de IA?

Se o 'assessor' deles os colocou comprados em 'Private' Equity (estamos vendidos publicamente via PSP), vou rezar por eles.

Você pode assinar nosso novo produto Big Theme ou revisar o tema AI Bubble da nossa apresentação de Temas Macro do 4T, onde encontrará estes 3 shorts de Neocloud de IA alavancadas:

Coreweave (CRWV)

IREN

Nebius (NBIS)

Nebius soa como uma erupção cutânea que você pega por se alavancar demais em infraestrutura de IA nos topos de ciclo. E age como uma também.

Tem um Evento de Crédito pendente? Como destacamos em nossa apresentação de gestão de risco de IA, o financiamento é a gaveta mais fraca das três gavetas de gestão de risco que modelamos, e os planos de gastos estão perto do máximo em toda parte.

A Oracle (ORCL), na qual também estamos vendidos, agora gasta mais que o dobro de seu fluxo de caixa, e a CoreWeave (CRWV) mais de quatro vezes. A Oracle passou de 56% para 200% em dois anos. A CoreWeave esteve acima de 100% em todos os anos em que reportou.

O que poderia dar errado?

Bem, as coisas continuaram dando muito errado para aqueles que jogavam Round 6 na Coreia do Sul ontem à noite. O KOSPI caiu mais -7,6%, levando seu tombo para -39% a partir de seu pico da #MOAB.

Mãe, #MOAB significa 'Mother of All Bubbles' (A Mãe de Todas as Bolhas).

Pode parecer uma cotovelada afiada para algum garoto mimado em Fairfield, CT, cujo pai é um banqueiro de investimentos do Bank of America (e sim, estamos vendidos em BAC). Mas para este garoto de Thunder Bay, Ontário, ainda parece soprar um beijo para aquele cara a partir do ponto de faceoff.

Bird distribuía cotoveladas porque o momento exigia. Às vezes, eu também o faço porque Wall Street as merece. O Jogo continua. E como meu pai (bombeiro por 38 anos) sempre me ensinou: 'quando as coisas ficam difíceis, os fortes entram em ação'.
reports.synthesisPt: A reação do mercado ao CPI expôs o estresse latente no crédito, com o alargamento dos spreads de High Yield e a queda nos rendimentos dos títulos reforçando o risco de aperto monetário em meio à desaceleração macroeconômica. A tese central foca na fragilidade da Bolha de IA, cuja queima desmedida de caixa e alta alavancagem motivam posições vendidas em nomes como Oracle, CoreWeave, IREN e Nebius. Os sinais de fissura ultrapassam o mercado americano e já se manifestam no tombo de 39% do KOSPI desde sua máxima histórica. O cenário aponta para um ambiente adverso em que tanto o crédito privado quanto o equity inflado por narrativas de infraestrutura enfrentam riscos severos de reprecificação.

reports.title: EARLY LOOK: Babel Fish
reports.bigPicture:
In The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy, the Babel Fish is a small yellow creature you place in your ear. Feeding off brainwaves and absorbing mental impulses, it creates a telepathic matrix that allows anyone to speak and understand any language. The irony in the name is intentional: the Tower of Babel gave us the proliferation of miscommunication, not universal understanding. Douglas Adams liked that kind of joke.

The little fish parable at the top has made its way around the internet as a cartoon. I first encountered it in a 2005 commencement address by David Foster Wallace, the author of Infinite Jest, who was careful to make clear that the reader should not identify with the older fish. "The point of the fish story," he said, "is merely that the most obvious, important realities are often the ones that are hardest to see and talk about." The habits that surround us constantly shape not only our reality but our perception of it.

The parable has two components. First, the fish have no awareness of the medium in which they are swimming. Second, the older fish's question implies that the water might not always be pleasant. I think about both as we navigate Quad 2 through the remainder of this year before sailing into what the model currently projects as a string of Quad 4 months in 2027.

Why the Babel Fish? Because all market participants increasingly speak the same language. The same narratives, the same flows, the same reflexive responses to the same news. Everyone in the same water, no one asking what the water is. And yet, like the Biblical story, behavior grows more confounding, not less, as the vocabulary converges. The Machine has a way of doing that.
reports.macroGrind:
The composition of the water has changed materially, and most participants are swimming in it without noticing. As I wrote earlier this year, in the US, passive funds now represent 55% of total fund AUM, up from 34% a decade ago. Passive surpassed active for the first time in 2024. Within active, growth and momentum strategies dominate marginal decision-making. Valuation-sensitive strategies are becoming a rounding error of the remaining active component. Price discovery is increasingly a task assigned to a shrinking minority.

Nowhere is an aversion to price discovery more obvious than in private markets. Global private market assets have grown from roughly 2.5% of total AUM twenty years ago, to 6% a decade ago, to over 11% of the $135 trillion managed by global investment firms today.

Private credit alone has grown from under $1 trillion to $3.5 trillion in the last five years. Cracks are emerging. Nearly 12% of private credit loans now carry paid-in-kind (PIK) provisions at origination, and cash-to-PIK conversions are accelerating. You can’t pay the interest, so you dilute your equity in lieu of payment. That's a sign of strain that doesn't show up in reported default rates, which are mid-single digits depending on the methodology used. The real issue here is opacity. Something is lurking in the water, and the marks don't reflect it.

High Yield spreads are rising. CCC rated credit spread to treasury is over 1000 basis points. Everything is duration now. 40% of the companies in the Russell 2000 are losing money. At the other end, the biggest companies are generally outspending their cash flow and taking on more and more cap ex obligations.

All of this is fine in a low-rate environment. But we are not in low-rate waters anymore. Hedgeye has been bullish rates for months now. The 10 year still sits near levels last seen over 20 years ago. CPI later today is likely to show further acceleration. Quad 2. Growth and inflation accelerating. Brent remains over $100.

Consider the back testing problem. A 40-year lookback period for most strategies is almost entirely a falling-rate environment. In January 1986, the 10-year Treasury yield opened at 9% and the 30-year fixed mortgage rate was 10%. We bottomed out at a sub-1% 10-year and mortgages briefly dipped below 3%. Now we are over 5% and 7% respectively. Every model built on that history is calibrated to a world of secular rate decline. The parameters are estimated in one pool of water. We appear to now be swimming in another.

# EARLY LOOK: Babel Fish
**Data:** Wed, 14 Oct 2026 08:20:32 -0400 (EDT)
**Remetente:** Hedgeye <info@hedgeye.com>
**ID:** 111899

---

This research was prepared exclusively for jpaulo82@gmail.com as a subscriber of Hedgeye Risk Management and may not be forwarded or otherwise provided to any unauthorized party. If you have received this transmission in error, please notify Hedgeye Risk Management <mailto:support@hedgeye.com>.

10/14/2026 08:19 AM EDT Babel Fish

There are these two young fish swimming along and they happen to meet an older fish swimming the other way, who nods at them and says "Morning, boys. How's the water?" And the two young fish swim on for a bit, and then eventually one of them looks over at the other and goes "What the hell is water?" -David Foster Wallace's famous 2005 commencement speech Access Early Look Dashboard <https://model2.hedgeye.com/click/47920687.460/aHR0cHM6Ly9hcHAuaGVkZ2V5ZS5jb20vbWFjcm9fZGFzaGJvYXJkL2Vhcmx5X2xvb2s/65561052a51cff3724ccb7dfCf5066f3c>



 



R. Patrick Kent



@RPKent



Key Takeaways



Passive investing, momentum strategies, and private markets are increasingly dominating capital allocation, reducing price discovery and masking risks beneath the surface.



Private credit stress, widening high yield spreads, unprofitable small caps, and rising corporate spending are becoming more vulnerable as rates remain structurally higher.



Most investment models were built during decades of falling interest rates, but today’s Quad 2 environment of accelerating growth, inflation, and higher rates requires recognizing that the market is swimming in very different water.



The Big Picture



In The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy, the Babel Fish is a small yellow creature you place in your ear. Feeding off brainwaves and absorbing mental impulses, it creates a telepathic matrix that allows anyone to speak and understand any language. The irony in the name is intentional: the Tower of Babel gave us the proliferation of miscommunication, not universal understanding. Douglas Adams liked that kind of joke.



The little fish parable at the top has made its way around the internet as a cartoon. I first encountered it in a 2005 commencement address by David Foster Wallace, the author of Infinite Jest, who was careful to make clear that the reader should not identify with the older fish. "The point of the fish story," he said, "is merely that the most obvious, important realities are often the ones that are hardest to see and talk about." The habits that surround us constantly shape not only our reality but our perception of it.



The parable has two components. First, the fish have no awareness of the medium in which they are swimming. Second, the older fish's question implies that the water might not always be pleasant. I think about both as we navigate Quad 2 through the remainder of this year before sailing into what the model currently projects as a string of Quad 4 months in 2027.



Why the Babel Fish? Because all market participants increasingly speak the same language. The same narratives, the same flows, the same reflexive responses to the same news. Everyone in the same water, no one asking what the water is. And yet, like the Biblical story, behavior grows more confounding, not less, as the vocabulary converges. The Machine has a way of doing that.



Macro Grind



(VIEW LARGER IMAGE <https://model2.hedgeye.com/click/47920687.460/aHR0cHM6Ly9kMXloaWxzNml3aDVsNS5jbG91ZGZyb250Lm5ldC9jaGFydHMvcmVzaXplZC8xNjE0MDgvb3JpZ2luYWwvMTAuMjUuMjAyMl9yYXRlc19jYXJ0b29uLnBuZz9zcmM9ZW1haWwmZW1haWw9anBhdWxvODJAZ21haWwuY29t/65561052a51cff3724ccb7dfCde166eb0>)



The composition of the water has changed materially, and most participants are swimming in it without noticing. As I wrote earlier this year, in the US, passive funds now represent 55% of total fund AUM, up from 34% a decade ago. Passive surpassed active for the first time in 2024. Within active, growth and momentum strategies dominate marginal decision-making. Valuation-sensitive strategies are becoming a rounding error of the remaining active component. Price discovery is increasingly a task assigned to a shrinking minority.



Nowhere is an aversion to price discovery more obvious than in private markets. Global private market assets have grown from roughly 2.5% of total AUM twenty years ago, to 6% a decade ago, to over 11% of the $135 trillion managed by global investment firms today.



Private credit alone has grown from under $1 trillion to $3.5 trillion in the last five years. Cracks are emerging. Nearly 12% of private credit loans now carry paid-in-kind (PIK) provisions at origination, and cash-to-PIK conversions are accelerating. You can’t pay the interest, so you dilute your equity in lieu of payment. That's a sign of strain that doesn't show up in reported default rates, which are mid-single digits depending on the methodology used. The real issue here is opacity. Something is lurking in the water, and the marks don't reflect it.



High Yield spreads are rising. CCC rated credit spread to treasury is over 1000 basis points. Everything is duration now. 40% of the companies in the Russell 2000 are losing money. At the other end, the biggest companies are generally outspending their cash flow and taking on more and more cap ex obligations.



All of this is fine in a low-rate environment. But we are not in low-rate waters anymore. Hedgeye has been bullish rates for months now. The 10 year still sits near levels last seen over 20 years ago. CPI later today is likely to show further acceleration. Quad 2. Growth and inflation accelerating. Brent remains over $100.



Consider the back testing problem. A 40-year lookback period for most strategies is almost entirely a falling-rate environment. In January 1986, the 10-year Treasury yield opened at 9% and the 30-year fixed mortgage rate was 10%. We bottomed out at a sub-1% 10-year and mortgages briefly dipped below 3%. Now we are over 5% and 7% respectively. Every model built on that history is calibrated to a world of secular rate decline. The parameters are estimated in one pool of water. We appear to now be swimming in another.



The activity fostered by low rates is eventually slowed by the higher rates. The accelerations will become decelerations as the lagged effects of higher rates take hold and the base effects get steeper. Just keep swimming but take note of the conditions of the water.

reports.titlePt: EARLY LOOK: Peixe-Babel
reports.quotePt: "Bom dia, rapazes. Como está a água?" E os dois peixes jovens continuam nadando por um tempo, até que um deles finalmente olha para o outro e diz: "Que diabos é água?"
takeawaysPt: O investimento passivo, as estratégias de momentum e os mercados privados estão dominando cada vez mais a alocação de capital, reduzindo a descoberta de preços e mascarando riscos sob a superfície.

O estresse no crédito privado, a abertura dos spreads de high yield, small caps não lucrativas e a elevação dos gastos corporativos estão se tornando mais vulneráveis à medida que as taxas de juros permanecem estruturalmente mais altas.

A maioria dos modelos de investimento foi construída durante décadas de queda nas taxas de juros, mas o ambiente atual de #Quad2, com aceleração do crescimento, da inflação e taxas mais altas, exige reconhecer que o mercado está nadando em águas muito diferentes.
reports.bigPicturePt:
Em O Guia do Mochileiro das Galáxias, o Peixe-Babel é uma pequena criatura amarela que você coloca no ouvido. Alimentando-se de ondas cerebrais e absorvendo impulsos mentais, ele cria uma matriz telepática que permite a qualquer pessoa falar e entender qualquer idioma. A ironia no nome é intencional: a Torre de Babel nos trouxe a proliferação da falha de comunicação, não a compreensão universal. Douglas Adams gostava desse tipo de piada.

A pequena parábola dos peixes citada acima circulou pela internet em formato de tirinha. Eu a encontrei pela primeira vez em um discurso de formatura de 2005 feito por David Foster Wallace, autor de Graça Infinita, que teve o cuidado de deixar claro que o leitor não deveria se identificar com o peixe mais velho. "O objetivo da história dos peixes", disse ele, "é meramente mostrar que as realidades mais óbvias e importantes costumam ser aquelas mais difíceis de enxergar e discutir." Os hábitos que nos cercam moldam constantemente não apenas a nossa realidade, mas também a nossa percepção sobre ela.

A parábola possui dois componentes. Primeiro, os peixes não têm consciência do meio no qual estão nadando. Segundo, a pergunta do peixe mais velho dá a entender que a água pode nem sempre ser agradável. Eu penso em ambos enquanto navegamos no #Quad2 pelo restante deste ano, antes de navegarmos para o que o modelo projeta atualmente como uma sequência de meses em #Quad4 em 2027.

Por que o Peixe-Babel? Porque todos os participantes do mercado estão falando cada vez mais a mesma língua. As mesmas narrativas, os mesmos fluxos, as mesmas respostas reflexivas às mesmas notícias. Todo mundo na mesma água, ninguém perguntando o que é a água. E, no entanto, assim como na história bíblica, o comportamento torna-se mais desconcertante, e não menos, à medida que o vocabulário converge. A Máquina tem uma forma peculiar de fazer isso.
reports.macroGrindPt:
A composição da água mudou materialmente, e a maioria dos participantes está nadando nela sem perceber. Como escrevi no início deste ano, nos EUA, os fundos passivos agora representam 55% do total de AUM dos fundos, acima dos 34% registrados há uma década. O passivo ultrapassou o ativo pela primeira vez em 2024. Dentro da gestão ativa, estratégias de crescimento e momentum dominam a tomada de decisão marginal. Estratégias sensíveis a valuation estão se tornando um mero erro de arredondamento da parcela ativa restante. A descoberta de preços é cada vez mais uma tarefa delegada a uma minoria minguante.

Em nenhum lugar a aversão à descoberta de preços é mais evidente do que nos mercados privados. Os ativos globais em mercados privados cresceram de cerca de 2,5% do AUM total há vinte anos para 6% há uma década, superando hoje 11% dos $135 trilhões administrados por gestoras globais de investimento.

O crédito privado, isoladamente, saltou de menos de $1 trilhão para $3,5 trilhões nos últimos cinco anos. Rachaduras estão surgindo. Quase 12% dos empréstimos de crédito privado agora contam com cláusulas de pagamento em espécie (PIK) na originação, e as conversões de pagamento em dinheiro para PIK estão se acelerando. Você não consegue pagar os juros, então dilui o seu equity como forma de pagamento. Esse é um sinal de estresse que não aparece nas taxas de inadimplência reportadas, que giram no meio de um dígito dependendo da metodologia utilizada. O verdadeiro problema aqui é a opacidade. Algo está à espreita na água, e as marcações a mercado não refletem isso.

Os spreads de High Yield estão subindo. O spread do crédito classificado como CCC em relação ao Treasury está acima de 1000 basis points. Tudo virou duration agora. 40% das empresas do Russell 2000 estão perdendo dinheiro. Na outra ponta, as maiores companhias estão, no geral, gastando além do fluxo de caixa e assumindo cada vez mais obrigações de cap ex.

Tudo isso funciona perfeitamente em um ambiente de juros baixos. Mas não estamos mais em águas de juros baixos. A Hedgeye tem mantido uma postura bullish em juros há meses. O título de 10 anos ainda se sustenta perto de níveis vistos pela última vez há mais de 20 anos. O CPI a ser divulgado hoje mais tarde provavelmente mostrará nova aceleração. #Quad2. Crescimento e inflação acelerando. O Brent segue acima de $100.

Considere o problema do backtesting. Um período de análise retrospectiva de 40 anos para a maioria das estratégias cobre quase que exclusivamente um cenário de queda nas taxas. Em janeiro de 1986, o rendimento do Treasury de 10 anos abriu em 9% e a taxa hipotecária fixa de 30 anos estava em 10%. Atingimos o fundo com o papel de 10 anos abaixo de 1% e as hipotecas brevemente perfuraram os 3%. Agora estamos acima de 5% e 7%, respectivamente. Todos os modelos construídos com base nesse histórico foram calibrados para um mundo de declínio secular dos juros. Os parâmetros foram estimados em uma determinada piscina de água. Ao que tudo indica, agora estamos nadando em outra.

A atividade fomentada por juros baixos é, em última análise, freada pelos juros mais altos. As acelerações se transformarão em desacelerações à medida que os efeitos defasados das taxas mais elevadas se consolidarem e os efeitos de base ficarem mais exigentes. Continue nadando, mas preste atenção nas condições da água.
reports.synthesisPt: A ascensão desenfreada do investimento passivo e a opacidade dos mercados privados reduziram a descoberta de preços e mascaram fragilidades crescentes sob a superfície. O avanço do estresse no crédito privado, a abertura dos spreads de high yield e o grande contingente de small caps deficitárias tornam o mercado altamente vulnerável a taxas de juros estruturalmente elevadas. A maior armadilha reside no fato de que os modelos convencionais foram calibrados em quatro décadas de queda secular nos juros, sendo ineficazes para a água em que nadamos hoje. Atualmente em regime de #Quad2 com inflação e crescimento acelerando, os investidores precisam reconhecer a nova realidade antes que os efeitos defasados do aperto monetário conduzam o ciclo a uma desaceleração profunda.

August and September both printed monthly #Quad2s, and October is tracking a third. August was revised from #Quad3 after CPI printed 3.40%, up from July's 3.36%, alongside accelerating consumption. The forward count reads #Quad1 in November and #Quad2 in December before the cycle turns, #Quad3 in January and #Quad4 in February. The market started trading it the way this particular #Quad2 trades, Dollar Up, Rates Up, Gold Down. The US Dollar Index broke out to new #Quad2 Cycle Highs, up 3.4% in the last month. The UST 10yr crossed 5.30% for the first time since 2002. Large Cap Tech (XLK) and the Nasdaq 100 (QQQ) printed all-time highs in early October, while Small Caps, Financials, Consumer Discretionary, and Utilities kept falling.



So we rotated back toward the #Quad2 playbook while keeping the shorts that the Signal said were working. We added US Large Cap Growth (XLK, QQQ, TOPT, CRTC), Cybersecurity (BUG), Healthcare Technology (HTEC), Japan (JPXN, FJP), and the inflationary energy-logistics complex (Brent via BNO, Refiners via CRAK, Tanker Shipping via BWET). The result, 43 total positions, 22 longs and 21 shorts, and the book is back to net long after one month net short. The long book is anchored in US Large Cap Tech and Secular Growth, the energy-logistics complex, crypto, and the carry sleeve, plus a PFIX rate hedge. The short book is concentrated in Duration and Credit, rate-sensitive and cyclical US sectors, Small Caps, Precious Metals, and the countries in #Quad3 Stagflation.



KEY TAKEAWAYS Quad Path: The monthly count reads #Quad2 in August (revised from #Quad3), September, and October, three straight #Quad2s. Then #Quad1 in November, #Quad2 in December, #Quad3 in January 2027, and #Quad4 in February. The Quads are global and they are diverging. The USA and Japan are in #Quad2 in Q4. Canada, Germany, and India are in #Quad3 Stagflation. South Korea slows into back-to-back #Quad4s in Q1 and Q2 of 2027, and India heads to #Quad4 in Q1 2027. Last month the Signal disagreed with the Quad. This month it agrees.



Growth / Inflation: August CPI printed +3.40% y/y, up from July's +3.36%. Our September CPI Nowcast is +3.74% y/y (range +3.63% to +3.85%) against a consensus of +3.6%, with the print due Wednesday, October 14, and October's Nowcast is +3.80% (range +3.69% to +3.91%). On the quarter, Headline CPI runs 3.50% in 3Q26E and returns to 3.86% in 4Q26E, matching the 2Q26 peak, while Real GDP re-accelerates from 2.10% to 2.35% YoY. The inflation is broad. The CRB Commodities Index is up 12.5% over three months, WTI is up 29.1%, Copper is up 6.8%, Natural Gas is up 14.1% in the last month after breaking out to Bullish TREND, and Rice is up 21.5% over three months. The Fed hiked 25bps on September 16 to a 3.75% to 4.00% target range, and fed funds futures price roughly 71% odds of another hike by December. The bond market agrees with the Nowcast. The UST 10yr Risk Range is 5.20% to 5.35%, the 2yr is 4.75% to 4.94%, the 30yr is 5.51% to 5.70%, and the curve has started to steepen.



Playbook: The back-tested #Quad2 playbook says Commodities are the best asset class, Fixed Income the worst, Tech the best sector, Utilities the worst, Secular Growth the best style factor, and Low Beta the worst. We are positioned for all six, long US Large Cap Tech and Secular Growth (XLK, QQQ, TOPT, CRTC, IGV, BUG, HTEC), long the energy-logistics complex (BNO, CRAK, BWET) and crypto (IBIT), long Japan (JPXN, FJP), and short Duration and Credit (TLT, ZROZ, LQD, HYG, JOJO) and Utilities (XLU). Where the back-test and the tape disagree, we follow the tape. Financials usually work in #Quad2 and are not working in this one, so we are short XLF. This #Quad2 is Dollar Up, so we are short Gold's cousins (SLV, PALL) and out of Gold itself.

Added Longs: BNO, CRAK, BWET, BUG, CRTC, XLK, TOPT, HTEC, JPXN, QQQ, FJP
