Removed: AAAU, FXH, COLO, LVHI, MSOS, CORN, EWZ, XLE, JETS, PRN, JOET, SMH, UFO



MACRO THEMES CONTEXT

Theme 1: The Signal Confirms #Quad2 — Three Straight #Quad2s



The Quads give us our priors. The Signal confirms or rejects them in real time. In September the two disagreed, the Quad math said #Quad2 and the tape went risk-off, so we de-risked and ran the book net short. In October the Signal came around. Large Cap Tech printed all-time highs, the Dollar broke out, Bond Yields made new Cycle Highs, and commodity inflation kept accelerating. When the market confirms a prior, we press, and that is why the book is net long again.



Confirmation does not mean every #Quad2 rule applies. Financials are the clearest example. In #Quad2 the sector has averaged a 4.3% quarterly return with a positive return frequency of 78%, and Regional Banks have averaged 9% per quarter, their best regime. In September XLF fell 6.6% while the S&P 500 slipped 0.5%, and KRE fell roughly 6% over the past month. Three reasons explain the gap. The Fed hike flattened the curve and compressed bank net interest margins. The 10yr crossing 5.30% eroded the value of banks' fixed-rate securities. And AI agents that move idle balances toward the best available rate threaten the cheap deposit base that bank profitability depends on. Usually is a probability, always is a promise, and markets do not make promises. We are short XLF.



The same discipline applies to Healthcare. XLV protected the book through the June and July drawdown in Tech, and it remains a full-cycle long, but it has lagged in this #Quad2. We reduced the expression to a single position in XLV and moved the incremental Healthcare exposure into Healthcare Technology (HTEC), where the Healthcare AI factor basket has been leading.



U.S. Growth & Inflation Outlook



Q3 2026 GDP: 2.10% YoY — growth decelerating from 2Q26's 2.19%



Q3 2026 CPI: 3.50% YoY — off the 2Q26 peak of 3.86%, but re-accelerating month-over-month from July's 3.36% to September's 3.74% Nowcast



Q4 2026 GDP: 2.35% YoY — sequential re-acceleration, with capital goods orders up 14% on AI infrastructure spending



Q4 2026 CPI: 3.86% YoY — resumed acceleration, back to the 2Q26 peak



QoQ SAAR growth path: 2.20% → 3.46% → 1.19% into 4Q26E — the quarterly YoY reads #Quad4 in 3Q26E even as the monthly count runs #Quad2



After August's +3.40% print, our Forecast framework now expects CPI to:



September: Accelerate (base case +3.74% y/y; upside +3.85%, downside +3.63%; consensus +3.6%, report October 14)



October: Accelerate (base case +3.80% y/y; upside +3.91%, downside +3.69%)



November: Disinflate (#Quad1)



December: Accelerate (#Quad2)



January 2027: Accelerate (#Quad3, growth slows as inflation keeps rising)



February–May 2027: Disinflate — sharper leg as Oil comps roll over, with Q1 2027 turning #Quad4 and 2Q27E Headline CPI falling to 1.94%

Theme 2: Dollar Up, Rates Up, Gold Down



Not every #Quad2 is Dollar Up. This one is. The US Dollar Index rose 1.0% in the week ending October 2 and is up 3.4% in the last month, signaling Bullish TRADE and TREND at new #Quad2 Cycle Highs. EUR/USD is down 2.7% in a month and Bearish TRADE and TREND. The Canadian Dollar is down 3.4% in a month against a Canadian economy that grew less than 1% in the first half of 2026. The Mexican Peso is down 8.1% in a month, which is why we are short Mexican stocks (EWW).



Rates moved with the Dollar. The Fed hiked 25bps on September 16, fed funds futures price roughly 71% odds of another hike by December, and the modal path implies a 4.50% to 4.75% range by mid-2027. The 2yr rose roughly 50bps over the past month to 4.84%. The 10yr crossed 5.30%, its highest level since 2002, and printed a 5.33% Cycle High. After flattening through September, the curve has started to steepen, so we are no longer positioned for a flattener. We remain short Treasuries (TLT, ZROZ), IG Credit (LQD), High Yield (HYG), and the Credit Rotation basket (JOJO), and long the BUXX, CLOX, and CLOZ carry sleeve and the PFIX rate hedge in their place.



Dollar Up and Rates Up is rarely good for Gold. Gold fell 3.5% in the week ending October 2 and is Bearish TREND. We sold AAAU, which we had held since February 2025, and we are short Silver (SLV) and Palladium (PALL), which fell 6.8% and 8.1% respectively that week. Gold and Gold Miners are next on the short list if they bounce to lower highs.



Theme 3: The Flows & Market Structure



This #Quad2 favors Large over Small. QQQ is up 4.2% in the last month and IWM is down 3.9%. The Russell 2000 is down 9.0% from its Cycle Peak and remains Bearish TREND. US Large Cap Tech (XLK) rose 5.0% in September and returned to the all-time highs it had not seen since the end of May. Short positions in Consumer Discretionary (XLY), Utilities (XLU), and Industrials (XLI) fell 6.7%, 6.6%, and 4.7% respectively in September.



Consensus did not position for it. Goldman prime brokerage data shows Hedge Funds cut exposure through the move into #Quad2 that started in August, and consensus fundamental US Long/Short funds hit their lowest Net Long Exposure of 2026 while the market made new highs. The "High Retail Sentiment" basket is down 1.8% for 2026 YTD after peaking at +21.6% on May 28.



The AI trade is separating the funded from the financed. Over the last 60 days the "Cash Funded Four" hyperscalers are up 17% and the "Neoclouds" are down 7%. By our Fractal Score Card, 15 of the 35 AI names we track are Bearish TREND, including every Power Grid name. AI infrastructure spending is driving a 14% increase in capital goods orders, accelerating both growth and inflation, and it is financed with debt that competes with Treasury issuance from a government running 6% deficits. That is #Quad2 now. It is also the setup for a deep #Quad4 when those comps arrive. We are long the cash-funded growth exposures (XLK, QQQ, TOPT, IGV, BUG) and avoid the levered infrastructure complex.

Asset Class Positioning

COMMODITIES



Longs: BNO, CRAK, BWET



Shorts: PALL, SLV



Commodities are the best-performing asset class in a #Quad2 back-test, and the CRB is up 12.5% over three months. We moved the energy exposure out of stocks and closer to the barrel. We sold Energy stocks (XLE) on October 2 when they signaled lower highs. BNO (Brent Oil) replaces it, because Brent has held its $99 TRADE level while WTI broke $92, and the Signal has favored Brent through that divergence. CRAK (Oil Refiners) is back in the book, Bullish TRADE and TREND. BWET (Tanker Shipping) is the most inflationary position we own and the most volatile, so it is risk managed strictly inside its Trend Range, with sales at the top end. On the short side, SLV (Silver) and PALL (Palladium) are the cleanest expression of Dollar Up, Rates Up, Gold Down, and both are better shorts than Gold itself.



DOMESTIC EQUITIES



Longs: XLV, IGV, CRTC, XLK, TOPT, QQQ



Shorts: XLU, XLI, IWM, XLY, XLF



Tech is the best sector in #Quad2 and Secular Growth the best style factor, and this is where the long book now lives. XLK (Technology) returned to all-time highs, QQQ (Nasdaq 100) is up 4.2% in the last month, TOPT (Top 20 US Stocks) concentrates the book in the cash-funded large-cap leaders, and CRTC (US Critical Tech) adds the strategic-technology sleeve. IGV (Software) is up 8.0% since the September update and remains the core Expensive Software long. XLV (Healthcare) stays as the full-cycle defensive long. We removed FXH and MSOS.



The short book targets the sectors this #Quad2 punishes. IWM (US Small-Cap) is down 9.0% from its Cycle Peak and is the cleanest Large-over-Small expression. XLF (Financials) is the sector where the back-test and the tape disagree, and we follow the tape. XLY (Consumer Discretionary), XLU (Utilities), and XLI (Industrials) fell 6.7%, 6.6%, and 4.7% in September. We covered the factor-basket shorts (PRN, JOET) and Semiconductors (SMH) as the high-beta growth complex turned higher.



DOMESTIC FIXED INCOME



Longs: BUXX, CLOX, CLOZ, PFIX



Shorts: LQD, TLT, ZROZ, JOJO, HYG



Fixed Income is the worst asset class in #Quad2, and US Treasuries remain the largest Major Market Drawdown on the board. TLT is down 4.0% and ZROZ down 7.5% since the September update, and LQD down 2.2%. New this month, HYG (High Yield) completes the short across Treasuries, IG, and High Yield, the three bond exposures most 60/40 accounts own. On the long side, PFIX (Interest Rate Hedge) is up 15.9% since the September update and pays as the curve rises and steepens. The carry sleeve, BUXX, CLOX, and CLOZ, remains our core fixed-income allocation.



International EQUITIES



Longs: JPXN, FJP



Shorts: QAT, INDA, EWA, EWL, EWG, EWW



The country-by-country Quad divergence drives this sleeve. Japan is in #Quad2 in Q4, moved from Bearish TREND back to Bullish TREND, and is up 6.0% in the last month, so we are long it two ways, JPXN and FJP. On the short side, INDA (India) is in #Quad3 heading to #Quad4 in Q1 2027 and is down 6.2% in a month. EWG (Germany) and EWL (Switzerland) are short on European #Quad3 Stagflation, with a Bearish TREND Euro and Bullish TREND European Bond Yields. EWW (Mexico) is short on an 8.1% decline in the Peso over the past month. EWA (Australia) and QAT (Qatar) remain short. We removed the Colombia (COLO), Brazil (EWZ), and International High Dividend (LVHI) longs as the Dollar broke out, and we will look to buy EWZ on a pullback within its new Bullish TREND.



FOREIGN EXCHANGE



Longs: DBMF



Shorts: None



The most consequential change in the book is the exit from AAAU (Physical Gold), which we had held since February 2025. Gold is Bearish TREND in a Dollar Up, Rates Up #Quad2, and the long Dollar position is now expressed through what the Dollar is positively correlated with (crypto) and what it hurts (precious metals, EM currencies, European equities) rather than through a direct UUP position. DBMF (Managed Futures) is up 2.9% since the September update, the trend-following overlay that benefits when cross-asset trends persist.



GLOBAL EQUITIES



Longs: BUG, HTEC



Shorts: PBD, PSP, IPAY



BUG (Cybersecurity) is a Secular Growth software long. HTEC (Healthcare Technology) captures the Healthcare AI factor basket. On the short side, PBD (Clean Energy) and PSP (Global Private Equity) remain short into higher rates, and IPAY (Digital Payments) is new, short the payments fee pools exposed to the same AI-agent disintermediation weighing on the Financials. We covered JETS and UFO.



Digital Assets



Longs: IBIT



Shorts: None



Bitcoin is one of the US Dollar's most positive correlations in this #Quad2, and the crypto complex is working for the same #Quad2 reasons it worked in 2021. IBIT (Bitcoin) remains Bullish TREND,



The Signaling Process did what it is built to do. In September it kept us out of trouble when the Quad and the tape disagreed. In October it confirmed the Quad, and we pressed. The book reflects a Dollar Up, Rates Up #Quad2, long US Large Cap Tech, Secular Growth, the energy-logistics complex, Japan, and crypto, and short Duration, Credit, Financials, Small Caps, Precious Metals, and the #Quad3 countries. The discipline is the same in every Quad, hold multiple ideas in your head at once, take profits when the Signal calls the change, and rotate when the fractal tells you to.



As always, please reach out with any questions.



Best,

Your Macro Team



APPENDIX



We find two factors to be most consequential for forecasting future financial market returns: economic growth and inflation. We track both on a year-over-year rate of change basis to better understand the big picture, then ask the fundamental question: Are growth and inflation heating up or cooling down?



From there, we get four possible outcomes, each of which is assigned a “quadrant” in our Growth, Inflation, Policy (GIP) model and the typical government response as a result (neutral, hawkish, in-a-box or dovish): Growth accelerating, Inflation slowing (QUAD 1); Growth accelerating, Inflation accelerating (QUAD 2); Growth slowing, Inflation accelerating (QUAD 3); Growth slowing, Inflation slowing (QUAD 4).

reports.macroGrind:
The number 1 place to start today is Tier1 alpha data. There are two general rules that we use when looking at the Short Dated Calendar Volatility.

Implied volatility does not stay in single digits for more than a couple days

The market buys protection between 1-3 days before major events

What’s great about this game is just because something has happened in the past does not mean it will continue. But, something that has been working ever since we started implementing Tier 1 into our process is important.

On point 1 above, super short dated implied vol (1-2 days out) has now remained in the single digits for 2 days. Currently sitting at 8.33. That is about as low as we have seen it go. That to us signals the broad market is overbought. A sell some signal.

On point 2, we have inflation tomorrow and we currently have implied volatility at 10.5 going into the event. Typically, we see that number go to at least 12-15. That means the market has not done its last-minute hedging yet. Maybe the last-minute hedging didn’t happen yet because of the bank holiday yesterday, as we saw volume -22% MoM. But I don’t know…

Why is this important? Fed rate hike expectations for October went from a 27% chance to 68% chance after the inflation report and then followed by the Fed Rate hike on 9/16. Now the chances of a hike in October went from 68% to 18%. What changed this trajectory? Well, it was two fed heads making dovish comments. Then we had a jobs report for the last stretch of the move.

So, where we are sitting right now, has nothing to do with data (the reality) and mostly to do with two fed heads.

Before we get to the next play we have to look at the broad market impact. SPY’s current move to all-time highs started two days after October rate hike expectations peaked. The last inflation report on 9/11 brought the S&P and Nasdaq to Neutral trend.

Why am I spending so much time on this? Because even though the last inflation print had expectations for an acceleration the market still reacted the way it did. For tomorrow’s inflation, expectations are for 3.6% an acceleration from 3.4%. We have our nowcast which we have been publishing for over a month now! Which points to an even larger acceleration. The point though is that it is an acceleration and the current market has not bought its protection for this acceleration.

So how do we prepare? Well look at the chart of the day which is from our new dashboards (under the hamburger menu click ‘User Dashboards’)! We have gone to 1 long and 4 shorts with the 1 long being bond market volatility.

We follow the signals and the ranges so let’s look at what those are telling us today.

At the low end of the risk range within bullish trends: UST 2yr Yield, UST 30yr Yield. Approaching the top end of the range within bearish trends: High Yield HYG, Germany DAX, Gold. At the top end of the range within a bullish trend: Brent Oil. Continuing its crash to now -2.8% YTD: High retail sentiment. Reversed towards bearish trend: Kospi, High beta Momentum.

So, what do you do with all of this? Very simple. Increase rate sensitive shorts. sell some of your pure inflation plays (Brent BNO, BWET). Stay away from the Kospi for now.

But it is not all negative! You see, we are long of large cap tech. 6 of the 7 Mag 7 are bullish trend, we bought some Nasdaq QQQ. We are also in a positive gamma environment.

You shouldn’t be reading this note as “The Next Stock Market Crash Is Upon Us” NO. We do risk management. This note is, we can see buying opportunities in the areas that we like! But, nothing in life is guaranteed.

It is always about the next play. Because after this inflation report and the next one, we will be looking forward to Q1.

As expectativas de alta de juros despencaram diante de comentários dovish do Fed e dados de emprego mais fracos, mas um dado de inflação mais forte pode reverter rapidamente esse movimento e pressionar ativos sensíveis a juros.

A Hedgeye está aumentando posições short sensíveis a juros enquanto se mantém long em techs selecionadas de grande capitalização, com o objetivo de gerenciar o risco em torno da inflação e usar qualquer volatilidade para encontrar melhores oportunidades de compra.

reports.macroGrindPt:
O lugar número 1 para começar hoje são os dados da Tier1 alpha. Há duas regras gerais que usamos ao analisar a Short Dated Calendar Volatility.

A volatilidade implícita não fica em um dígito por mais de dois dias

O mercado compra proteção entre 1-3 dias antes de grandes eventos

O que é fantástico neste jogo é que só porque algo aconteceu no passado não significa que continuará acontecendo. Mas algo que vem funcionando desde que começamos a implementar a Tier 1 em nosso processo é importante.

Sobre o ponto 1 acima, a vol implícita de curtíssimo prazo (1-2 dias) permaneceu agora em um dígito por 2 dias. Atualmente situada em 8.33. Isso é praticamente o nível mais baixo que já vimos chegar. Para nós, isso sinaliza que o mercado amplo está sobrecomprado. Um sinal para vender um pouco.

Sobre o ponto 2, temos inflação amanhã e atualmente temos a volatilidade implícita em 10.5 entrando no evento. Normalmente, vemos esse número ir para pelo menos 12-15. Isso significa que o mercado ainda não fez seu hedge de última hora. Talvez o hedge de última hora ainda não tenha acontecido por causa do feriado bancário de ontem, já que vimos o volume em -22% MoM. Mas não sei…

Por que isso é importante? As expectativas de alta de juros do Fed para outubro foram de uma probabilidade de 27% para 68% após o relatório de inflação, seguidas pela alta de juros do Fed em 9/16. Agora, as chances de uma alta em outubro foram de 68% para 18%. O que mudou essa trajetória? Bem, foram dois dirigentes do Fed fazendo comentários dovish. Depois tivemos um relatório de empregos para o trecho final do movimento.

Portanto, onde estamos posicionados agora não tem nada a ver com dados (a realidade) e quase tudo a ver com dois dirigentes do Fed.

Antes de irmos para a próxima jogada, temos que olhar para o impacto no mercado amplo. O movimento atual do SPY rumo às máximas históricas começou dois dias após as expectativas de alta de juros de outubro atingirem o pico. O último relatório de inflação em 9/11 levou o S&P e a Nasdaq para TREND Neutro.

Por que estou dedicando tanto tempo a isso? Porque, embora o último dado de inflação tivesse expectativas de aceleração, o mercado ainda assim reagiu da forma que reagiu. Para a inflação de amanhã, as expectativas são de 3.6%, uma aceleração em relação a 3.4%. Temos nosso nowcast, que já estamos publicando há mais de um mês! O qual aponta para uma aceleração ainda maior. O ponto, porém, é que se trata de uma aceleração e o mercado atual não comprou sua proteção para essa aceleração.

Então, como nos preparamos? Bem, olhe para o gráfico do dia, que vem dos nossos novos dashboards (no menu hambúrguer, clique em ‘User Dashboards’)! Passamos para 1 long e 4 shorts, sendo o 1 long a volatilidade do mercado de títulos.

Nós seguimos os sinais e os ranges, então vamos olhar para o que eles estão nos dizendo hoje.

Na extremidade inferior do Risk Range dentro de bullish trends: UST 2yr Yield, UST 30yr Yield. Aproximando-se da extremidade superior do range dentro de bearish trends: High Yield HYG, Germany DAX, Gold. Na extremidade superior do range dentro de uma bullish trend: Brent Oil. Continuando sua queda para agora -2.8% YTD: High retail sentiment. Reverteu em direção à bearish trend: Kospi, High beta Momentum.

Então, o que fazer com tudo isso? Muito simples. Aumente os shorts sensíveis a juros. Venda um pouco de suas apostas puras de inflação (Brent BNO, BWET). Fique longe do Kospi por enquanto.

Mas nem tudo é negativo! Veja bem, estamos long em techs de grande capitalização. 6 das 7 Mag 7 estão em bullish trend, compramos um pouco de Nasdaq QQQ. Também estamos em um ambiente de gamma positivo.

Você não deve ler esta nota como “O Próximo Crash do Mercado de Ações Está Chegando”. NÃO. Nós fazemos gestão de risco. Esta nota significa: podemos ver oportunidades de compra nas áreas que gostamos! Mas nada na vida é garantido.

É sempre sobre a próxima jogada. Porque após este relatório de inflação e o próximo, estaremos olhando para o Q1.
reports.synthesisPt: A volatilidade implícita de curtíssimo prazo atingiu patamares excepcionalmente comprimidos, indicando complacência e sobrecompra no mercado acionário antes do relatório de inflação. Enquanto as expectativas de alta de juros caíram drasticamente devido a declarações dovish do Fed, o nowcast da Hedgeye aponta para uma aceleração da inflação que ainda não conta com proteção montada pelos investidores. Diante desse cenário, a recomendação tática é ampliar posições short sensíveis a taxas e realizar lucros parciais em ativos atrelados à inflação. Ao mesmo tempo, a carteira mantém posições long em techs de grande capitalização (Mag 7 e QQQ), utilizando qualquer volatilidade gerada pelo evento para capturar melhores oportunidades de compra.

Quando estiver no Canadá, faça o que fizer, não fale sobre o quão objetivamente ruim a economia deles ficou. O PIB do Canadá foi inferior a 1% no primeiro semestre de 2026, e sua moeda está despencando em chamas (CAD/USD caiu -3,4% apenas no último mês).

Não, não preciso ter uma opinião política sobre isso. Sem sentimentos. São apenas números. E eles são ruins.

O Mercado Global de Moedas votou a favor disso. O que mais aconteceu no FX na semana passada?

O US Dollar Index continuou construindo Momentum de #Quad2, subindo mais +0,3%, atingindo +3,4% no último mês

Por que nos importamos com Reais e Pesos? Porque estamos vendidos em ações mexicanas (EWW) e aguardando para comprar na queda no recente rompimento para Bullish TREND nas ações brasileiras (EWZ).

Estamos vendidos em Alemanha (EWG), que caiu mais -0,6% na semana passada, somando -1,9% no último mês

O Rendimento da UST de 10 anos caiu -4 pontos-base, ficando em +41 pontos-base no último mês

O que O Fractal enxerga no mercado de Moedas, Commodities e Títulos?

Nenhuma mudança. Mais alto por mais tempo tanto no Crescimento quanto na Inflação dos EUA. Dependendo do seu país, isso é bom (EUA e Japão em #Quad2 no 4T) ou ruim (Canadá, Alemanha e Índia na Estagflação de #Quad3).

Peck disse que sem disciplina não podemos resolver nada. O Fractal não tem sentimentos sobre em qual país você está e/ou o que você acha do Donald Pump. Ele apenas lê o sinal e relata o que é.

Disciplina total. Não apenas alguma. Total.

No mercado acionário americano, o sinal favorece claramente as large caps (comprado em QQQ) contra as small caps (vendido em IWM). Em termos globais, a alocação prioriza a compra de ações no Japão e a venda na Alemanha, enquanto economias como Canadá e Índia permanecem presas no #Quad3 de estagflação. Na América Latina, a preferência tática recai sobre o Brasil e Petrobras (PBR) em detrimento do México (EWW). Por fim, o modelo fractal reforça a importância da disciplina estrita na execução diária, ignorando opiniões políticas e narrativas de mercado.

Welcome to Weekend Reading—your weekly roundup of actionable market insights and top Hedgeye highlights. Each edition offers a taste of the investing process our subscribers rely on to protect and grow their capital.

 Key Economic Data This Week 



All sessions from the Fall 2026 Hedgeye Investing Summit are now available to watch on demand. 🔥 



October 6-8, Hedgeye CEO Keith McCullough hosted many of the sharpest minds in finance — Fidelity’s Jurrien Timmer, QI Research’s Danielle DiMartino Booth, Bianco Research’s Jim Bianco, bestselling author Jim Rickards, and several others. 



They covered everything from the AI Bubble and what happens when it pops to bonds, gold, and the Federal Reserve. 



If you want to position ahead of the market moves that matter, you don’t want to miss this. 



						SEE THE FULL LINEUP AND WATCH HERE  → https://info.hedgeye.com/e/764243/026-your-access-links-to-watch/2svdvjq/2562853173/h/errG2uZqy5MoghkkFMmSmhqyuIjzclwH70OBVUhYvI0



Jim Bianco: Bond Traders Can Stop Panicking When the Fed Starts Panicking 



https://info.hedgeye.com/e/764243/eye-investing-summit-fall-2026/2svdvjt/2562853173/h/errG2uZqy5MoghkkFMmSmhqyuIjzclwH70OBVUhYvI0



On Day 1 of the Hedgeye Investing Summit, Macro Strategist Jim Bianco said the period from September 2024 through the present is the first time in more than 50 years a rate-cutting cycle produced higher long-term yields. 



“Bond traders can stop panicking when the Fed starts panicking.” 



He warned that skipping a hike the market wants could push the 10-year yield to 5.50% from about 5.25%. He also rejected the idea that 5% yields are a threat to stocks. 



“Why is the stock market ignoring higher interest rates? Because they’re not high. They were too low.” 



						WATCH THE FULL CONVERSATION  → https://info.hedgeye.com/e/764243/eye-investing-summit-fall-2026/2svdvjt/2562853173/h/errG2uZqy5MoghkkFMmSmhqyuIjzclwH70OBVUhYvI0



 



DiMartino Booth: The Fed Is Hiking Into a Slowdown 



https://info.hedgeye.com/e/764243/eye-investing-summit-fall-2026/2svdvjx/2562853173/h/errG2uZqy5MoghkkFMmSmhqyuIjzclwH70OBVUhYvI0



On Thursday, Danielle DiMartino Booth said small business bankruptcies are up 63% year over year, larger corporate bankruptcies are running at a 15-year high, and CCC spreads widened to 1,000 basis points last week, her proxy for private credit. 



She said the Federal Reserve’s recent rate hike mostly rewarded the people sitting in cash. 



“For the top 1%, this rate hike was a home run.” 



She expects the Fed to cut rates once credit breaks, and warned against the Street’s base case that the Fed will eventually step in and buy stocks. 



“You’ll kiss capitalism goodbye that day.” 



						WATCH THE FULL CONVERSATION  → https://info.hedgeye.com/e/764243/eye-investing-summit-fall-2026/2svdvjx/2562853173/h/errG2uZqy5MoghkkFMmSmhqyuIjzclwH70OBVUhYvI0



 



McAlvany: “The Mother of the Mother of All Bubbles Is Government Debt.” 



https://info.hedgeye.com/e/764243/eye-investing-summit-fall-2026/2svdvk1/2562853173/h/errG2uZqy5MoghkkFMmSmhqyuIjzclwH70OBVUhYvI0



Tuesday, David McAlvany joined Keith McCullough at the Hedgeye Investing Summit to discuss gold and the debt behind the AI buildout. 



McAlvany said the buildout needs $3.7 trillion in revenue by 2032 to work, and pointed to Oracle’s $165 billion New Mexico data center as an early crack. 



“Equity capital can be patient, but debt has to be paid.” 



He sees support for gold near $4,000, recommends buying incrementally, and called $8,000 gold over the next two to three years a reasonable target. The bigger risk, he said, sits in Washington. 



“The mother of the mother of all bubbles is government debt.” 



						WATCH THE FULL CONVERSATION  → https://info.hedgeye.com/e/764243/eye-investing-summit-fall-2026/2svdvk1/2562853173/h/errG2uZqy5MoghkkFMmSmhqyuIjzclwH70OBVUhYvI0

McCullough: Stop Measuring Yourself Against Warren Buffett 



https://info.hedgeye.com/e/764243/tt-type-macro2Cmarket-insights/2svdvk4/2562853173/h/errG2uZqy5MoghkkFMmSmhqyuIjzclwH70OBVUhYvI0



Hedgeye CEO Keith McCullough: https://info.hedgeye.com/e/764243/KeithMcCullough/2svdvkb/2562853173/h/errG2uZqy5MoghkkFMmSmhqyuIjzclwH70OBVUhYvI0



 said most investors should stop measuring themselves against Warren Buffett. 



"You are not Warren Buffett, and you actually want to have risk management at the core, quantitative strategies at the core," McCullough said at the Hedgeye Investing Summit: https://info.hedgeye.com/e/764243/026-your-access-links-to-watch/2svdvjq/2562853173/h/errG2uZqy5MoghkkFMmSmhqyuIjzclwH70OBVUhYvI0



HGRO Portfolio Manager Sam Rahman: https://info.hedgeye.com/e/764243/Hedgeye-HGRO/2svdvkf/2562853173/h/errG2uZqy5MoghkkFMmSmhqyuIjzclwH70OBVUhYvI0



 says very few investors can hold positions the way Buffett has. 



"Very, very few people have the luxury to have that kind of duration of the capital," Rahman says. "Buffett owns his duration because he owned the capital." 



Rahman says his own long-term view runs one to three years, with many short-term moves to manage along the way. 



"That doesn't mean you buy and hold and you sit there for three years and pray that it's going to work out." 



McCullough describes the alternative as a top-down macro view like Stan Druckenmiller’s combined with stock picking. 



"One bear market will convince you."

Eu sou o Dusty? Não. Eu sou o Mucker.

E não importa o quão bem eu jogue, alguns assinantes pagantes ainda encontram algo do que reclamar. Um cara disse ontem que está "cansado do meu teatrinho de hóquei".

Fiquei levemente ofendido. Comprei exatamente um taco de hóquei novo nos últimos cinco anos e ele é muito bom. Minha mãe concorda. Coloque isso no seu cachimbo anti-hóquei e fume, amigão.

Eu me identifico como jogador de hóquei. Tenho um orgulho danado disso.

Como Baker bem sabe por razões muito mais sérias que as minhas, é mais fácil odiar o homem do que o processo. Tenho 51 anos. Não tenho tempo sobrando no relógio para ser outra pessoa.

Eu entendo isso

Isso não muda minha performance nem a forma como falo e tuíto sobre ela

Como qualquer grande marca, vou divulgar tanto meu processo quanto minha performance. Se eu não fizer isso, você acha que a Carlyle ou a CNBC farão?

Fundos hedge US Long/Short "fundamentais" de consenso atingiram sua menor Net Long Exposure de 2026

Reúna toda essa multidão de amadores e profissionais que precisam se juntar à Hedgeye ou competir conosco, e você terá uma bola de demolição de ódio bastante potente.

O jogador de hóquei dentro de mim simplesmente adora isso!

"Mas, mas... alguns dos seus ETFs não estão batendo novas máximas históricas, então você é horrível..."

Beleza, amigo.

Em primeiro lugar, a maioria dos nossos ETFs iniciais é o que o público de varejo da arquibancada não reconheceria mesmo que uma rebatida em linha de Dusty Baker acertasse a cara deles: Produtos de Gestão de Risco.

Apenas espere até eu lançar de 50 a 100 ETFs.

Baker dava dois passos à frente e alguém estava sempre esperando que ele desse um passo atrás. Estive nessa situação durante toda a minha carreira em Wall Street. A diferença é que sou um jogador de hóquei.

Nós não damos passos para trás. Nós bloqueamos e chutamos a gol.
reports.synthesisPt: Keith McCulloch compara sua trajetória profissional à resiliência de Dusty Baker no beisebol, lembrando que o ceticismo e o ressentimento alheios sempre acompanham quem mantém a disciplina contra o consenso. Enquanto investidores de varejo e fundos hedge long/short tradicionais amargam perdas ou reduzem drasticamente sua exposição, as carteiras da Hedgeye atingiram recordes históricos consecutivos. Respondendo a críticas sobre o rendimento de certos ETFs da casa, ele enfatiza que esses veículos foram desenhados com matemática fractal especificamente para gestão de risco e hedge, não para perseguição irresponsável de upside. Com a mentalidade implacável de um jogador de hóquei, Keith reitera que permanecerá intransigente na execução e na divulgação do seu processo proprietário.

takeawaysPt: Os mercados asiáticos e europeus estão emitindo amplos sinais de baixa, com Coreia do Sul, Índia, China, Alemanha e Suíça enfraquecendo à medida que os mapas de Quad apontam para um crescimento mais lento e risco persistente de estagflação ou desinflação.

Os sinais macroeconômicos dos EUA também estão apertando, com nowcasts de inflação em alta, rendimentos de títulos permanecendo mais altos por mais tempo, o dólar renovando máximas de ciclo em #Quad2 e o Russell 2000 já acumulando queda de 9% em relação ao seu pico.

A mensagem central é ignorar o ruído e prestar atenção ao que os mercados estão realmente sinalizando por meio do preço, exposição a fatores, fluxos e tendências de Quad, posicionando o capital em conformidade.
reports.bigPicturePt:
Duas palavras = todo o processo da Hedgeye.

Sou pago para escrever e desabafar sobre o posicionamento do meu capital suado todas as manhãs. O que a maioria das pessoas não sabe é que, após as 9h30, sento-me em quase completo silêncio pelo restante do dia.

"Mantenha seus olhos e ouvidos abertos... Esteja ciente de qualquer coisa que pareça fora do comum. Substitua "o pátio" por "o mercado". Substitua "roupas" por "Exposições a Fatores". Substitua "reunir" por "concentrações de Fluxo". Esse é o Processo de Sinalização. Não o que alguém está dizendo. Trata-se puramente do que A Máquina está vendo.
reports.macroGrindPt:
O que estamos vendo em certos Grandes Sinais do Mercado Macro já não é tão sutil assim.

Vamos começar observando “o pátio” na Ásia:

O KOSPI da Coreia do Sul caiu mais -2,6% durante a noite, levando seu Crash de #Quad4 a -27,3% desde junho

O mercado de ações da Índia (estamos vendidos em INDA) caiu mais -1,7%, levando seu momentum de preço de 1 mês para -6,2%

O Shanghai Comp da China reabriu com uma baixa de -0,8% no dia, levando seu momentum de preço de 1 mês para -3,3%

Conclusão: Não fique comprado em nenhum desses grandes mercados — venda-os a descoberto nos repiques para topos descendentes de ciclo.

Você pode fazer o que eu faço todas as manhãs (sentar em silêncio das 4h30 às 7h45, quando entro no The Call @HedgeyeTV) e apenas prestar atenção às 2 coisas que importam mais do que qualquer outra:

Os Sinais multifatoriais e multiduração

Os Mapas de Quad para muitos países

O que esses 3 Sinais de mercados de ações (todos Bearish TRADE e TREND) na Ásia estão antecipando?

A contagem de Quads da Coreia do Sul inclui desaceleração em direção a #Quad4s consecutivos no 1T e 2T de 2027

A economia da Índia permanece em Estagflação de #Quad3 e caminha para Desinflação de #Quad4 no 1T de 2027

A China está tentando sair de um longo período de #Quad3 e #Quad4, mas evidentemente simplesmente não consegue

E quanto aos Sinais e Quads europeus? Eles se parecem mais com os EUA ou com a Ásia? Nenhum dos dois — eles se parecem mais com a Europa!

O mercado de ações da Alemanha caiu mais -0,8% esta manhã, acumulando -4,3% no último mês

O mercado de ações da Suíça caiu mais -1,0% esta manhã, acumulando -2,4% no último mês

EUR/USD permanece Bearish TREND, enquanto os rendimentos dos títulos europeus, ao longo de toda a curva, permanecem Bullish TREND

Como venho vendendo a descoberto cada repique para topos descendentes na Alemanha (EWG) e na Suíça (EWL) no último mês, isso é ótimo. Em casa, a família chama isso de alpha. Esse é o verdadeiro pão que coloco na mesa e com o qual alimento os patos.

O que esses 3 Sinais europeus estão sinalizando?

Boas-vindas a Carney, do Canadá, que quer se juntar ao clube de golfe europeu como um “Membro Associado”?

Estagflação de #Quad3 no estilo europeu?

Alex, eu escolho tanto A) quanto B) por $500.

Alex Trebek era o meu conterrâneo do “Sul” (de Thunder Bay) em Sudbury, Ontário. Sobre se apresentar ao vivo, ele disse: "Faço isso há 35 anos. As pessoas dizem que é muito tempo. Eu digo que passa rápido quando você ama o que faz."

Eu amo o que faço. Amo saber o que a multidão do consenso de Hedge Funds e/ou “Investidores de Varejo” do tipo CNBC vai A) nunca saber e B) que sempre podemos antecipar. Nunca quis fazer parte do establishment e/ou de seus clubes.

Quais são alguns dos outros Grandes Sinais Macro vindos do pátio esta manhã?

Nosso Nowcast de Inflação dos EUA, o melhor do mercado, continua apontando para cima nas leituras de SET e OUT

Nossos Sinais de rendimentos de títulos continuam confirmando o mesmo — mais altos por mais tempo, com topos de ciclo mais elevados em jogo

Nosso Sinal para o Dólar Americano continua avançando para novas máximas de ciclo em #Quad2

O Russell 2000 já caiu -9,0% em relação ao seu pico de ciclo. A cesta de fatores de “Investidor de Varejo” (ações com maior concentração de investidores individuais) atingiu o pico no final de maio e acumula queda de -0,8% no último mês.

Sheridan disse para prestar atenção às mudanças sutis no pátio, onde os grupos se reúnem, o que estão vestindo.

Será que seus antigos amigos de Washington e/ou de Old Wall a caminho da prisão sabem o que significa quando uma gangue decide usar botas no pátio? Provavelmente não. Isso importa?

Não estamos vivendo a vida atrás das grades. Nosso capital suado vai para onde quer que O Sinal e os Quads mandem ir.

ICYMI — "Fools Yield", the Bond Market’s New Normal, and the House Your Kids Can’t Afford



Day 2 of the Hedgeye Investing Summit is in the books, and all three webcasts are now available on-demand.



									"Investors often mistake yield for return."



Verdad Founder & Portfolio Manager Dan Rasmussen has a name for the trap he sees in private credit: fool’s yield.



A higher yield almost always means higher default risk. Investors see a 15% yield and think they’ll earn 15%. Rasmussen warns they may find out they earned far less, and at the worst possible time, when enough loans go bad at once.



He also shared where he’s finding opportunity instead: overlooked small caps in Japan.



Watch Rasmussen + McCullough Here: https://info.hedgeye.com/e/764243/eye-investing-summit-fall-2026/2svdmwz/2560937309/h/5S2c6HgQMQaiv3ZCvDZRx8GtE9uADRW--jxkwsuhG4M





									"Three is the new two in terms of inflation."



Jurrien Timmer, Director of Global Macro at Fidelity Investments, broke down why bond yields are rising around the world, and what it could mean for stocks.



By his math, if yields reach 6%, stock valuations could take roughly a 20% haircut. The only thing standing in the way is how fast earnings keep growing.



Watch Timmer + McCullough Here: https://info.hedgeye.com/e/764243/eye-investing-summit-fall-2026/2svdmx3/2560937309/h/5S2c6HgQMQaiv3ZCvDZRx8GtE9uADRW--jxkwsuhG4M

Chemistry Professor David Collum of Cornell University says the boomer generation is sitting on a problem it hasn’t faced yet: how to hand its wealth to the next generation.



									His hunch is that it can’t happen without prices coming down. Many boomer homes are too expensive for younger buyers to purchase, maintain, or even pay the taxes on, and he says many young people don’t want them anyway.



									He points to his own home overlooking Cayuga Lake, where the property taxes alone run about $30,000 a year.

reports.title: EARLY LOOK: Usually ≠ Always
reports.bigPicture:
September and October have historically marked the heart of the Atlantic hurricane season. The climatological peak falls on September 10, and just over half of a typical season's tropical activity occurs after September 9, with roughly 90% of that remainder realized by the end of October. This year has been a notable exception.

The 2026 season entered October without producing a single hurricane, a first in the satellite era dating back to 1966, with all eight named storms to date topping out at tropical storm strength. Going back to 1851, only 1907 and 1914 completed a full season without a recorded hurricane, and the record for the latest first hurricane of a season, October 8 (set in 1905), is now just a day away. Most of the credit goes to a very strong El Niño in the Pacific, which has amplified wind shear across the Atlantic basin and kept storms from organizing. That said, the Hurricane Center is tracking a disturbance in the Bay of Campeche with high odds of becoming a tropical depression later this week, so we'll stop short of declaring victory.

Few seasonal patterns are as dependable as the autumn surge in Atlantic hurricane activity, yet this year has landed squarely in the tail of the distribution, a reminder that a strong central tendency narrows the range of outcomes without ever closing it.
reports.macroGrind:
Our Quad framework classifies the macro environment into one of four regimes based on the rate of change in growth and inflation. Its utility lies in its simplicity. By reducing a complex macro backdrop to a finite set of states, each with a historically consistent market signature, the framework provides a reliable map of how absolute and relative returns vary across asset classes, sectors, styles, and factors. We exploit that conditional return dispersion by tactically positioning a multi-asset, multi-duration portfolio for the Quads we expect to prevail over the coming months and quarters.

The Quads, however, are guidelines, not rules. The Quads give us our priors, whereas the Signal, feeding on price, volume, and volatility data across asset classes, is how we risk-manage those priors in real time. When the market confirms a prior, we press, and when the market rejects it, we listen.

Even the strongest central tendencies, like Atlantic hurricane activity in September and October, carry no guarantees. In today's market, financials are a prime example of "usually" falling short of "always." In Quad 2, when growth and inflation are both accelerating, the sector has averaged a 4.3% quarterly return with a positive return frequency of 78%. Nearly four out of five times, financials go up in Quad 2. That reads like a sure thing until you look at the last month.

XLF fell -6.6% in September while the S&P 500 slipped just -0.5%, a -610 bps spread. It helps to know what XLF actually owns. The fund is cap weighted and top heavy. Berkshire Hathaway, JPMorgan, Visa, and Mastercard alone account for roughly 38% of the fund. Commercial banks make up about 28%, and adding Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, and the custody banks lifts bank-like exposure to roughly 37%. That exposure sits overwhelmingly with the money centers. PNC, the largest regional lender in the fund, carries a weight of only about 1.2%. The big names did most of the damage. Bank of America, Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, and BNY each fell between -12% and -14% over the past month.

An even more robust Quad 2 tendency belongs to regional banks. On average, Quad 2 is the single best regime for regionals, with an average quarterly return of 9% and a 78% positive return frequency. Yet KRE is down roughly -6% over the past month, lagging the S&P 500 alongside the rest of the sector.

While we prefer to be right on the "when" rather than the "why," here is the fundamental logic behind the underperformance:

First, the market repriced the Fed's path higher. Following the FOMC's 25 bps hike to a 3.75% to 4.00% target range on September 16, fed funds futures now assign roughly 71% odds to another hike by the December meeting and a further 16% to two, with the modal path implying a 4.50% to 4.75% range by mid-2027, or three additional hikes. That repricing hit the front end hardest. The 2-year Treasury yield rose roughly 50 bps over the past month to 4.84%, outpacing the long end for much of September and compressing the 2s10s spread to roughly 40 bps by month end. Banks borrow short and lend long, so a flatter curve means a thinner spread between what they pay on deposits and what they earn on loans.

Second, the long end moved to levels not seen in more than two decades. The 10-year Treasury yield crossed 5.30%, its highest level since 2002. Rising long rates erode the value of banks' fixed-rate securities. For available-for-sale holdings, those unrealized losses flow through AOCI and reduce tangible book value immediately. For held-to-maturity holdings, the losses sit off the balance sheet but still weigh on investors' assessment of economic capital. Meanwhile, the benefit of reinvesting at higher yields accrues only gradually, as fixed-rate assets mature and roll over. Higher long rates also raise the cost of capital, which tends to dampen loan demand and revive concerns about credit quality as borrowers face higher debt service costs.

Third, the market found a new disintermediation worry. Meta's new AI agent, Muse, can help consumers cancel subscriptions and hunt for better deals with very little effort. Recall, the bread-and-butter of banking is a cheap and docile depositor base, and the last hiking cycle showed how quickly that docility fades once rates become worth chasing. At JPMorgan, the nation's largest deposit franchise, noninterest-bearing deposits fell -8.1% y/y in 2Q23, -3.3% in 2Q24, and -5.7% in 2Q25, taking their share of total deposits from a peak of 30.0% in 2Q22 to 24.2% three years later. Even after a +7.5% y/y rebound in 2Q26, that share sits at just 24.6%. Notably, the outflows persisted well after the Fed's final hike in July 2023, which suggests that once depositors learn to shop for yield, the habit sticks. That migration played out with depositors moving money on their own initiative. An AI agent that automatically moves idle balances toward the best available rate could compress that learning curve considerably, and with the Fed hiking again, the cheap deposit franchises and fee pools that underpin bank profitability look less sticky than they did a month ago.

Getting back to the point, positioning on what should work rather than what is working is a reliable path to disaster. The Quad 2 playbook says financials and regional banks should be working, and over a long sample they usually have. Over the last month, the tape has said otherwise.

The Quads give us our priors. The Signal confirms or rejects them, even the strongest among them.

After all, "usually" is a probability, "always" is a promise, and markets don't make promises.

The 2-year Treasury yield rose roughly 50 bps over the past month to 4.84%, outpacing the long end for much of September and compressing the 2s10s spread to roughly 40 bps by month end. Banks borrow short and lend long, so a flatter curve means a thinner spread between what they pay on deposits and what they earn on loans.



Second, the long end moved to levels not seen in more than two decades. The 10-year Treasury yield crossed 5.30%, its highest level since 2002. Rising long rates erode the value of banks' fixed-rate securities. For available-for-sale holdings, those unrealized losses flow through AOCI and reduce tangible book value immediately. For held-to-maturity holdings, the losses sit off the balance sheet but still weigh on investors' assessment of economic capital. Meanwhile, the benefit of reinvesting at higher yields accrues only gradually, as fixed-rate assets mature and roll over. Higher long rates also raise the cost of capital, which tends to dampen loan demand and revive concerns about credit quality as borrowers face higher debt service costs.



Third, the market found a new disintermediation worry. Meta's new AI agent, Muse, can help consumers cancel subscriptions and hunt for better deals with very little effort. Recall, the bread-and-butter of banking is a cheap and docile depositor base, and the last hiking cycle showed how quickly that docility fades once rates become worth chasing. At JPMorgan, the nation's largest deposit franchise, noninterest-bearing deposits fell -8.1% y/y in 2Q23, -3.3% in 2Q24, and -5.7% in 2Q25, taking their share of total deposits from a peak of 30.0% in 2Q22 to 24.2% three years later. Even after a +7.5% y/y rebound in 2Q26, that share sits at just 24.6%. Notably, the outflows persisted well after the Fed's final hike in July 2023, which suggests that once depositors learn to shop for yield, the habit sticks. That migration played out with depositors moving money on their own initiative. An AI agent that automatically moves idle balances toward the best available rate could compress that learning curve considerably, and with the Fed hiking again, the cheap deposit franchises and fee pools that underpin bank profitability look less sticky than they did a month ago.



Getting back to the point, positioning on what should work rather than what is working is a reliable path to disaster. The Quad 2 playbook says financials and regional banks should be working, and over a long sample they usually have. Over the last month, the tape has said otherwise.



The Quads give us our priors. The Signal confirms or rejects them, even the strongest among them.



After all, "usually" is a probability, "always" is a promise, and markets don't make promises.

Day 1 of the Hedgeye Investing Summit is in the books, and all three webcasts are now available on-demand.



									"You can see a bubble a mile away... What's hard is knowing when it will pop."



Bestselling author Jim Rickards joined Keith McCullough to break down the expanding AI bubble.



Drawing on his time as General Counsel for the Long-Term Capital Management hedge fund, Rickards warned that AI could make the next market panic faster and worse than previous crashes, and that the trigger will likely be something no one sees coming.



															Watch Rickards + McCullough Here: https://info.hedgeye.com/e/764243/eye-investing-summit-fall-2026/2svdhnl/2559055577/h/4pdRhyz-wV4r2pz7Hst5dxxr7o9ayhNI2jTmMuh4zr8

Macro strategist Jim Bianco, founder of Bianco Research, answered a question that's got investors uneasy:



Why do interest rates on U.S. government bonds keep rising, even though the Fed is supposed to be pushing them down?



Bianco's take:



Rates aren't too high — they're finally normal. He argues the economy is running hot enough to justify them, and that the bond market has spent two years signaling the Fed is making a mistake.



His warning for stock investors: every major new technology ends its first boom in a bubble — and AI won't be the exception.

									"Equity capital can be patient, but debt has to be paid."



David McAlvany, CEO of McAlvany Financial Group, explained why he believes gold is headed sharply higher once the AI bubble bursts.



McAlvany's argument is simple: the companies building AI are borrowing enormous sums to do it — and borrowed money has to be paid back whether or not the profits show up.



He thinks they won't, at least not fast enough. As that reality sets in, he sees investors pouring into gold, pushing it to $8,000 over the next two to three years — with so many buyers that there won't be enough to go around.

reports.title: EARLY LOOK: Who's The Bank In #Quad2?
reports.bigPicture:
Eric Reis has a chapter in his new book

Incorruptible

that asks one of the most important questions in financial services:

“Who Is The Bank?”

Reis, who wrote

The Lean Startup,

uses Steinbeck's

Grapes of Wrath

(1939) to answer it:

"The bank - the monster has to have profits all the time. It can't wait. It'll die. The bank isn't like a man."

The bank isn't like a man. But it's made of men and women. They need bonuses. They need quarterly earnings.  They need the fee structure to survive. They will do what the monster requires, irrespective of what

The People

need.

Evidently, you don't want to be a bank stock in this edition of

#Quad2.

They're perpetuating

man-made risks

at a scale Steinbeck would recognize immediately. We reviewed the financing risks in our

Q4 Macro Themes

presentation through what we're calling our

Big Theme: The AI Bubble.

(

VIEW LARGER IMAGE

)

Welcome to another

Macro Monday @Hedgeye

where the coffee is being consumed and the measuring and mapping of markets and their cycles has been done.

Let’s jump right into our weekly

Macro Market

review with the

Global Currency Market:

US Dollar Index was up another +1.0% last week and continues to signal Bullish TRADE and TREND

EUR/USD was down another -1.1% last week to -2.7% in the last month = Bearish TRADE and TREND

Japanese Yen was -0.3% vs. USD and continues to signal Bearish TRADE, Bullish TREND

GBP/USD was flat last week but also remains Bearish on both our TRADE and TREND durations

Canadian Dollar was down another -0.7% vs. USD last week and continues to signal Bearish TREND

Why do we care about Canadian Dollars getting smoked? If you're paid in USD you probably don't (unless you're planning a ski trip to Banff with The Fam, in which case great news: it just got cheaper).

I am Canadian. I'm also aware that many very nice Canadians don't do Macro or math. Carney's "popular" government had GDP running under 1% in the first half of 2026 and the national currency is a disaster.

Europe’s currency and economy is turning into a #Quad3 Stagflation

mess too. We’re short European Equities via:

Germany (EWG) which was down another -0.7% last week to -2.4% in the last month

Switzerland (EWL) which was down another -2.0% last week to -4.9% in the last month

Maybe that’s why Carney wants Canada to be an “Associate Member” of the Euro Golf Club?

Moving along. A big reason why European Equities have been breaking down is where I started this morning’s rant: they have a lot of Bank Stocks in their Major Indexes. In the US, here’s how

Financials did vs. Tech

last week:

US Financials (XLF) were down another -2.5% last week, taking their drawdown to -7.2% in the last month

US Mega Cap Tech (XLK) was UP another +1.8% last week to +8.8% in the last month alone

We’re long XLK and Short XLF. I was Captain of the Yale Hockey team. Carney was Harvard’s 3

rd

string goalie.

This pervasive US Dollar strength is impressive given the mouth pieces of big US Banks (Fed Heads) did their best to “tone down rate hike expectations last week.”

Global Currency Volatility

has broken out alongside

Bond Market Volatility.

So now

The Machine

must deal with the following:

USD breaking out to new #Quad2 Cycle Highs this morning

UST 2yr, which the Fed tried to tone down, was only down 1 basis point last week to 4.84%

What's next? The thing that always gets Old Wall Bankers and Levered Long investors: gravity.

The headline Jobs report looked "dovish" to someone with no Quad Models and/or Fractal TRADE and TREND Signals. We know the pending CPI is going to be hawkish. Precious Metals know it too.

Dollar Up. Rates Up. Rarely good for Gold

. Down -3.5% last week. Our Palladium (PALL) and Silver (SLV) Shorts were down -8.1% and -6.8% respectively.

So who is the bank? Steinbeck said it's only made of men. I hope you've become your own person. Use banks for commodity services like paying you interest. Use your own process to risk manage your hard-earned capital.

The monster needs its profits. Make sure yours aren't funding them.

reports.bigPicture:
In the Lord of the Rings, Sauron's Ring was not merely a weapon; it was a platform strategy. Total control, no competitors, every user bound to the ecosystem. The companies racing to dominate AI -- sorry, "superintelligence" because that's what we are doing this week -- have read the same playbook. The winner-take-all platform mindset that produced Google in search, Amazon in e-commerce, Meta in social media, and Microsoft in productivity is now being applied with maximum aggression to "superintelligence."  The only problem is the Ring has a habit of destroying the bearer.

After playing with Muse for a few days, it is clear that the agent layer needs cooperation to be truly useful. In many cases technology created the most value when the underlying infrastructure was standardized and shared. The Machine.

Macro Monday @Hedgeye

where those who aren’t rocking the 60/40 portfolios are going to be quite happy to have sidestepped this

Dollar Up, Rates Up, Gold Down

. Another #Quad2 week, it was.

Let’s do the

US Dollar

part of the fractal pattern first:

US Dollar Index was up another +0.8% last week to +2.1% in the last month = Bullish TRADE and TREND

EUR/USD was down another -0.5% last week to -2.3% in the last month = Bearish TRADE and TREND

We’re also looking to short Mexican Stocks (EWW) on bounces alongside EM Equity (Country) Exposures if #Quad2 continues to manifest into a stronger US Dollar.

You know what really doesn’t like a Strong Dollar and #Quad2 Rates Ripping? A:

Gold.

It was down another -2.1% last week after breaking TRADE Signal Support. And it’s down another -3.1% this morning after breaking TREND.

What up with those #Quad2 Rates Ripping?

UST 2yr Yield was up another +9 basis points last week to +67 basis points in the last month

UST 10yr Yield was up another +15 basis points last week to +53 basis points in the last month

UST 30yr Yield was up another +16 basis points last week to +33 basis points in the last month

No one in our growing community should be surprised.

Why did the long-end finally go up more (week-over-week) than the short-end? A: ROC (rate of change) Data for PMI was that good! How much longer can #Quad2 in SEP US economic data be printed? A: well into October.

The TREND is, therefore, for the US economic GROWTH Cycle Data to peak in Q326, then start slowing more obviously in 1H of 2027 from that Cycle Peak. In the meantime,

LARGE CAP GROWTH

continues to perform.

rising Cost of Capital into a Revenue slowdown

 Key Economic Data This Week 



EVENT | Q4 2026 Macro Themes Presentation 



Growth and inflation are both accelerating. That’s what we call #Quad2, a bullish setup for tech, growth, and momentum stocks, to name just a few asset classes that have historically outperformed in this environment. 



Hedgeye expects that to continue through Q4, before a more challenging Macro setup in 2027. 



Want to see how to position now and front-run the shift? 



On Thursday, October 1 at 11 AM ET, Hedgeye CEO Keith McCullough and the Macro team present our Q4 2026 Macro Themes, a deep-dive on the three major Themes we believe will drive market returns in the months ahead. 



1. #QUAD2 IN Q4, THEN…



Stimulus, AI spending, record profits and a $21 trillion jump in household wealth drove growth this year. In 2027, all of that becomes the comparison. The team will cover when market risk is most likely to rise. 



2. THE AI BUBBLE



Bubble or not a bubble is the wrong question. Hedgeye's new framework measures how stretched AI stocks are, how likely a break is and how much damage one would do. 



The right question is WHEN the bubble will pop and to prepare for it. 



3. DOLLAR UP, RATES UP



The 2-year Treasury yield is making new cycle highs as the market prices a Fed that keeps tightening. A flattening yield curve has weighed on Financials, Gold, and Silver; and the dollar is rising with rates. 



60 minutes. ~150 slides. Live and on-demand. 



This institutional-grade presentation is available exclusively in Macro Pro and Pro Risk Manager. 



SEE EVERYTHING INSIDE MACRO PRO  → https://info.hedgeye.com/e/764243/omo-3-monthsp-a-macro-pro-1417/2svc584/2552645094/h/uv3Q7KxAy3ci2Y8X9lnLH5k7Su4KspVB7NbyhKoIz2I

Hedgeye CEO Keith McCullough joined The David Lin Report to discuss surging bond yields, inflation, market positioning, the U.S. dollar, gold, Bitcoin, and the potential transition from today’s Quad 2 environment into a much more dangerous Quad 4 in 2027. 



“2027 is 2022, but potentially a lot worse because we have a lot more bubbles.” 



He also explains why he remains bullish on software, energy, and Bitcoin today, while warning that those positions could change quickly as growth slows and market signals turn. 



“Q2 of next year is going to be nasty.” 



WATCH THE FULL CONVERSATION  → https://info.hedgeye.com/e/764243/at-type-macro2Cmarket-insights/2svc587/2552645094/h/uv3Q7KxAy3ci2Y8X9lnLH5k7Su4KspVB7NbyhKoIz2I



McCullough: The Yield Curve Is The Biggest Problem Since 2022: https://info.hedgeye.com/e/764243/22-type-macro2Cmarket-insights/2svc58b/2552645094/h/uv3Q7KxAy3ci2Y8X9lnLH5k7Su4KspVB7NbyhKoIz2I

The sequence is the same: first Quad 2, then Quad 4, and the curve is now diving toward 19 basis points. 



It draws attention only after it turns negative, and by then the damage is done. On the way there, while stocks push higher, almost no one flags the risk — except for Hedgeye.

#Quad2 is where you get plenty of Short Squeezes in High Beta Factor Exposures

Ahead of the Fed Meeting last week, short-dated US Equity Calendar Vol got bid straight up to 20

As of yesterday’s close, that same super-short-term duration of Volatility got smoked down to 9!

If you're not measuring and mapping all these fundamental and behavioral feedback loops simultaneously, that's ok. We are. The Machine is.

Structure emerges from repetition. Impact scales through aggregation. The Old Wall built its business on static vines like “valuation” and Gaussian “risk model” assumptions. Fractals don't grow on static vines.

In addition to Long MU vs. Short JPM, there have been some amazing #Quad2 Breakouts that we’re on the right side of. How many Hedge Funds are Long Cannabis (MSOS). The ETF was +7.9% for The Fam yesterday.

How many are Long Bitcoin (IBIT), ETHA, and Bitcoin Equities (BLOK)? They’re all vertical alongside Bond Yields.

Does it all “make sense” to our linear econ brains? Does it have to?

The Old Wall dude who's pumped about his AI Muse and META (we're bullish on both) but still doesn't "get" how AI is dominating The Flows and Market Structure isn't observing an adaptive system. He's observing a static one.

Brennan said it plainly: markets are shaped by the impact of every participant. AI is now the largest participant. The feedback loops it creates aren't random. They're fractal. They aggregate. They repeat. They produce structure.

The Fractal Gods don't care if it makes sense. They just keep flowing.

This month’s update is a little later than usual given the shift from #Quad1 to #Quad2 and the position changes that came with it; moving forward, we’ll return to publishing in the first week of each month.



Dear ETF Pro Plus Subscriber,



Welcome back!



The current lineup of ETFs is as follows:



Long: BUXX, AAAU, CLOX, CLOZ, FXH, XLV, COLO, IGV, LVHI, MSOS, IBIT, DBMF, CORN, EWZ, XLE, ETHA, PFIX



Short: QAT, LQD, TLT, PBD, XLU, ZROZ, JOJO, JETS, PRN, JOET, XLI, INDA, IWM, EWA, EWL, PSP, SMH, UFO, QTUM, EWG

The Quad math for September and Q4 is still #Quad2. The Signal is telling a different story, and that divergence is the whole update.



The Quad is the central tendency, what the growth and inflation data say should happen. The Signal is the risk overlay, what the market is actually doing through flows and rotation, and it tends to sniff out phase transitions early. Right now the two disagree. The math still reads #Quad2 for September and Q4 — Growth Accelerating as Inflation Accelerates — with the monthly count running August #Quad3 to September #Quad2 to October #Quad2. The Signal is going risk-off underneath it. We rebuilt the book around the Signal, not the page.



What that looks like in the tape is a broadening breakdown. Consumer Discretionary first, then parts of Tech, now Financials. Rates have spiked across the curve, which is what #Quad2 tends to produce. A risk-off tape is not what #Quad2 is supposed to produce, and that tension is the information. So we cut the cyclical commodity and EM-beta longs we were adding in early September, kept the energy, hard-asset, and defensive-compounder longs that still work, added an outright rate hedge, and widened the short book across the small-cap, semiconductor, momentum, international, and private-equity complexes that a risk-off #Quad2 punishes first.



The result, 37 total positions, 17 longs and 20 shorts, and the book is now net short for the first time this cycle. The long book is anchored in Healthcare, Software, Energy, Gold, and the crypto and carry sleeves, plus a PFIX rate hedge. The short book is concentrated in Duration, rate-sensitive Utilities, and the cyclical, small-cap, and momentum factor exposures that keep breaking TREND.



KEY TAKEAWAYS Quad Path: The monthly count reads August #Quad3, September #Quad2, October #Quad2, with Q4 still #Quad2 and Q1 2027 turning #Quad4 on our map. On the quarterly YoY rate of change the path is 2Q26 #Quad3, 3Q26E #Quad4, 4Q26E #Quad2, 1Q27E #Quad4. Globally, the G20 aggregate is #Quad3 in Q3 heading to #Quad2 in Q4. The Quad math is #Quad2, but the Signal is rotating risk-off inside it, and that divergence is the reason the book de-risked.



Growth / Inflation: The engine is Oil. WTI is up roughly $20 since late August and the futures curve has moved into severe backwardation, a rare pairing of an acute price spike with a steeply inverted curve. Backwardation concentrates the shock in prompt barrels, so it hits headline inflation immediately, and our September CPI Nowcast came in +27bps above August. On the quarter, Q4 2026 CPI is re-accelerating toward 3.76% y/y. That is forcing the Fed's hand, one hike last week and three more expected by April 2027, tightening straight into a Q1 2027 #Quad4 slowdown. The bond market agrees, the UST 10yr is pressing 5% with the TRR up at 5.12% and the 2yr TRR at 4.84%, the VIX has moved to Bullish TREND, and the US Dollar has firmed back to Bullish/Neutral as risk comes off.



Playbook: #Quad2 on the page is not a reason to ignore a Signal rotating defensive, this is the setup where the Signal keeps you out of trouble. We express it by paring the cyclical commodity and EM-beta longs, keeping the inflation and hard-asset longs that still lead (Energy via XLE, Gold, Bitcoin, Ethereum, Corn), keeping the Defensive Compounders (Healthcare) and secular-growth Software, adding an outright interest-rate hedge (PFIX) and holding Managed Futures (DBMF), and widening the short book across Duration and rate-sensitives (TLT, ZROZ, LQD, JOJO, XLU) and the cyclical, small-cap, semiconductor, momentum, and international complexes (IWM, SMH, QTUM, UFO, PSP, INDA, EWA, EWL, EWG, JETS, PRN, JOET, XLI) that lead lower when breadth breaks.

Added Shorts: XLU, ZROZ, JOJO, JETS, PRN, JOET, XLI, INDA, IWM, EWA, EWL, PSP, SMH, UFO, QTUM, EWG



Flipped Short → Long: IBIT

MACRO THEMES CONTEXT

Theme 1: The Signal vs. The Quad — Why #Quad2 Is Tilting Toward Risk-Off



The Quad math for September and Q4 is still #Quad2. The Signal is not confirming it. When the central tendency and the risk overlay diverge, the divergence is the trade, and the Signal is the one that front-runs the phase transition.



The tell is a broadening breakdown in the tape, Consumer Discretionary first, then parts of Tech, now Financials. Rates have spiked across the curve, which is exactly what #Quad2 produces. What #Quad2 is not supposed to produce is a risk-off tape, and we are getting one anyway. The market is discounting a consumer already under strain and a central bank adding to the pressure, so the breadth deterioration in cyclically sensitive sectors is signal, not noise. Worse before better. We do not dismiss a Signal that is rotating defensive because the page still says #Quad2, we position for both, and that is why the book is now net short.



U.S. Growth & Inflation Outlook



Q3 2026 GDP: 2.03% YoY — growth decelerating from 2Q26's 2.10%



Q3 2026 CPI: 3.44% YoY — off the 2Q26 peak of 3.86%, and rising again on the September re-acceleration



Q4 2026 GDP: 2.28% YoY — sequential re-acceleration; the #Quad4 slowdown re-emerges in Q1 2027



Q4 2026 CPI: 3.76% YoY — resumed acceleration, revised up on the Oil shock



QoQ SAAR growth path: 1.50% → 4.02% → 1.46% into 4Q26E — the quarterly YoY reads #Quad4 in 3Q26E even as the near-term monthly texture runs #Quad2



After August's re-acceleration, our Forecast framework now expects CPI to:



August: Accelerate (base case +3.50% y/y)



September: Accelerate (Nowcast +27bps above August — the disinflation the model penciled for September did not show)



October: Accelerate



November: Disinflate



December: Accelerate



January 2027: Disinflate — Q1 2027 turns #Quad4 as the Oil comps roll over



February–May 2027: Disinflate — sharper leg

Theme 2: The Flows & Market Structure



The mechanical bid works in both directions, and Q3 proved it. High-Beta Momentum was +69% YTD on June 22 and negative on the year five weeks later; High Retail Sentiment round-tripped from +21% to -8% over the same window — the same passive, levered, price-insensitive flow that manufactured the melt-up unwound with the same indifference on the way down, all while the S&P held up (~+11.5% YTD). Into a rising-yield tape the two factor exposures that matter most are cyclicality and size, and both cut against consensus: Small-Cap factor exposure was −1.7% last week vs. Large Cap +0.3%, and the Russell is down ~2.0% in a month while the tape inflates. This is why the short book is built around the specific momentum, quality, and industrials factor baskets that keep breaking (PTF, JOET, PRN, XLI, JETS) rather than a blanket beta short, and why the surviving longs skew to secular-growth software (IGV) and idiosyncratic movers (XBI, MSOS) — the AI-Software-over-Semis pair is +17.9% in a month — instead of the crowded factor trades.



Theme 3: Short USD, Long EM — Long Commodities, Short Duration



Short USD, Long EM is a play on engineered dollar weakness, not a Fed-easing trade. Treasury and Japan already ran a coordinated intervention to pull the Yen off its lows, and the push to lean on the FIMA facility lets Japan keep defending the Yen without dumping Treasuries — so the Dollar weakens on direct intervention even with Warsh's Fed holding a hawkish bias and a hike still on the table. A softer Dollar lowers funding costs and improves carry across EM, which is the natural expression. In the ETF book that shows up as long the commodity complex and long the weaker-Dollar / EM winners, against short Duration and the rate-sensitives that a rising-yield tape punishes.



This is also the complete inversion of the July book. July was "Long Duration, Short Commodities." September is the exact reverse. The CRB is at new cycle highs (+11.5% in a month), WTI is +23% in a month, Copper is at all-time highs, Nat Gas is +10.9%, and the ags are inflating — so we're long the complex broadly (OIH, ICOP, UNG, WEAT, CORN, SRUUF), plus the anti-fiat expression through GDX, AAAU, and IBIT while the Dollar burns. Against that, Duration is the wrong side and so are the rate-sensitives that trade off it: short TLT, ZROZ, LQD, JOJO, and XLU, with the Bond Yield Signals (2yr TRR 4.50%, 10yr TRR 4.86%) saying these have room to keep working into and possibly through Friday's CPI.



Below is the current ETF Pro Plus lineup, followed by an asset-class walk-through of the book and what we added and removed since the last update. New users should review the Appendix for a primer on the Macro process and how we select (and remove) these exposures.

CURRENT ETF LINEUP



(VIEW LARGER IMAGE <https://model2.hedgeye.com/click/47603925.511/aHR0cHM6Ly9kMXloaWxzNml3aDVsNS5jbG91ZGZyb250Lm5ldC9jaGFydHMvcmVzaXplZC8xNjAwNTkvb3JpZ2luYWwvU2NyZWVuc2hvdF8yMDI2XzA5XzIyXzEwMzM1NC5wbmc_c3JjPWVtYWlsJmVtYWlsPWpwYXVsbzgyQGdtYWlsLmNvbQ/65561052a51cff3724ccb7dfC7d6c4274>)



Asset Class Positioning

COMMODITIES



Longs: XLE, CORN, IBIT, ETHA



Shorts: None



Oil is the whole macro story, so we keep the direct energy exposure. XLE (Energy) expresses the WTI breakout and the backwardated curve, the one place a risk-off #Quad2 still rewards being long. CORN is the surviving ag long. On the anti-fiat side, IBIT (Bitcoin) re-entered on a reclaim of Bullish TREND and ETHA (Ethereum) was added alongside it, the expression of devalued money looking for somewhere to go. The broader cyclical commodity sleeve we ran in early September (Oil Services, Copper Miners, Nat Gas, Uranium, Gold Miners) was taken back down as the Signal turned risk-off and broad commodity beta stopped confirming.



DOMESTIC EQUITIES



Longs: FXH, XLV, IGV, MSOS, XLE



Shorts: XLU, PRN, JOET, XLI, IWM, SMH



The long book keeps the Defensive Compounders that lead across regimes, XLV (Healthcare) and FXH (Healthcare Equity), long the same theme two ways. IGV (Software) is the secular-growth hold we bought on red as SPY tested TREND, and MSOS (US Cannabis) is the idiosyncratic long. XLE sits here on the energy breakout.



The short book is where the risk-off Signal lives. IWM (US Small-Cap) broke TRADE and TREND first and is the cleanest read on breadth breaking, and SMH (Semiconductors) shorts the complex that led the momentum unwind, with the levered version of that trade down double digits in single sessions. XLU (Utilities) is the rate-sensitive short into a curve making new highs, and PRN (Industrials Momentum), JOET (Quality Momentum), and XLI (Industrials) target the cyclical and momentum factor baskets that lead lower when Financials and Discretionary roll.



DOMESTIC FIXED INCOME



Longs: BUXX, CLOX, CLOZ, PFIX



Shorts: TLT, ZROZ, LQD, JOJO



The cleanest expression of the regime. We are short long Duration via TLT and the convex ZROZ (25yr+ Zero Coupon), short Investment Grade credit via LQD, and short the JOJO (Credit Rotation) basket, with US Treasuries the biggest Major Market Drawdown on the board as yields press new Inflation Cycle Highs and the Fed hikes into it. New this month on the long side, PFIX (Interest Rate Hedge) is an outright long-rates/rate-volatility hedge, the position that pays as the curve rises and the Fed tightens into a slowdown. The carry sleeve stays intact, CLOX (AAA CLO), CLOZ (BBB-B CLO), and the BUXX 5%+ cash sleeve, the place to be instead of bag-holding long-term Treasuries.



International EQUITIES



Longs: COLO, EWZ, LVHI



Shorts: QAT, INDA, EWA, EWL, EWG



On the long side the book is narrow, COLO (Colombia), held since July though off its all-time high as EM beta came in, EWZ (Brazil), retained from the August flip and re-loaded in September, and LVHI (International High Dividend) as the defensive high-carry sleeve. On the short side the risk-off rotation widened the international book, QAT (Qatar) and INDA (India) on the EM side, and EWA (Australia), EWL (Switzerland), and EWG (Germany) as the developed-market cyclicals that follow US beta lower and sit inside deteriorating local Quad setups.



FOREIGN EXCHANGE



Longs: AAAU, DBMF



Shorts: None



AAAU (Physical Gold) remains the structural store-of-value with no counterparty risk, held through the Dollar's round trip, from fresh 3-month lows earlier in September back to Bullish/Neutral TREND as risk came off. DBMF (Managed Futures) is the diversifying, trend-following overlay that does its work when cross-asset trends persist, a useful ballast into a risk-off tape.



GLOBAL EQUITIES



Longs:  None



Shorts: PBD, JETS, PSP, UFO, QTUM



The global short book is built around the highest-beta, most-speculative, and most rate-sensitive thematics. PBD (Clean Energy) runs through higher rates and tightening subsidy math, and JETS (Global Airlines) is short the oil-cost-exposed cyclical, long Oil against the airlines that have to buy it. New this month, PSP (Global Private Equity) shorts the leverage-and-marks complex directly into a rising-rate risk-off, and UFO (Space) and QTUM (Quantum Tech) short the long-duration, story-stock thematics that unwind first when momentum breaks.



Digital Assets



Longs: IBIT, ETHA



Shorts: None



We covered the summer crypto short. IBIT (Bitcoin) re-entered long on a reclaim of Bullish TREND, and ETHA (Ethereum) was added alongside it. In a burning-Dollar, inflation-accelerating tape the anti-fiat trade earns a long, and we size it as a hard-asset expression rather than a beta chase.



The Signaling Process is as sharp as it's ever been, and it is doing exactly what it is built to do. The Quad math says #Quad2. The Signal says risk-off, and the two work together, #Quad2 on the page is not a reason to dismiss a Signal that is rotating defensive. The book reflects it, long the Energy, hard-asset, and Defensive-Compounder exposures that still lead, long an outright rate hedge, and short the Duration, rate-sensitive, small-cap, semiconductor, momentum, and international complexes that lead lower when breadth breaks. Worse before better. The discipline is the same in every Quad, hold multiple ideas in your head at once, take profits when the Signal calls the change, and rotate when the fractal tells you to.



As always, please reach out with any questions.



Best,

Your Macro Team



APPENDIX



We find two factors to be most consequential for forecasting future financial market returns: economic growth and inflation. We track both on a year-over-year rate of change basis to better understand the big picture, then ask the fundamental question: Are growth and inflation heating up or cooling down?



From there, we get four possible outcomes, each of which is assigned a “quadrant” in our Growth, Inflation, Policy (GIP) model and the typical government response as a result (neutral, hawkish, in-a-box or dovish): Growth accelerating, Inflation slowing (QUAD 1); Growth accelerating, Inflation accelerating (QUAD 2); Growth slowing, Inflation accelerating (QUAD 3); Growth slowing, Inflation slowing (QUAD 4).

I cracked Sheridan's How To Not Die In Prison on a flight to Toronto last week. The already uptight guy sitting next to me started looking even more uncomfortable. Lol.

Rule Number One before you start trying to hedge your hard-earned capital and/or short stocks: have rules. The fish doesn't survive prison without them. The CNBC-type “Retail Investor” doesn't survive #Quad4 without them either.

Can't help you with your emotions if they're getting in the way of your risk management rules, bud. Read Sheridan's book. Chapter one. Rules first. Feelings later, preferably never.

If the #MOAB (Mother of All Bubbles) wasn't a thing, you wouldn't have had that kind of #Quad2 Short Squeeze yesterday. The bubble going back up is the point. That's why it's called a bubble and not a ceiling.

Bitcoin Sensitive Equity basket +5.1%

High Retail Sentiment basket +4.9%

Most (Hedge Fund Consensus) Short basket +2.3%

Since we’re long both Bitcoin (IBIT) and Ethereum (ETHA), we had a monster day being long the #1 Factor Exposure. What do our recent additions of Long Software (IGV) stocks (in May) and Crypto have to do with the #MOAB in AI?

On the HRS Basket (what “Retail Investors” own the most of), don’t forget that most of them were chasing AI “Muse” memes yesterday via META which had its best day in 17 months at +11.4%!

Guess who went from Bearish to Bullish on META right on Signal Time? A Thunder Bay guy who didn’t go to prison.

In addition to the Fractal Gods delivering me Bullish TREND Breakout Signals in META and MSFT (after being accurately Bearish on both earlier this year), your daily Risk Range™ Signal sheet continues to signal Bullish TREND on the following:

Did I say META and MSFT?

AAPL, GOOGL, NVDA, SPCX, TXG

What’s most interesting about these Bullish TRADE and TREND Signals is how much they’re diverging vs. Small/Mid Cap Stock Signals and certain Sector Styles (we’re short Industrials and Utes):

Russell 2000 (IWM) barely bounced yesterday and is still in -6.3% drawdown

Our #1 Sector Style Short, Utilities (XLU) was down another -1.1% yesterday to -10.3% for Q3 alone!

Why? Don’t tell the fish too much about The Flows of the Macro Waters but…

Maybe both Oil and Bond Yields are done with their short-term correction, eh?

Maybe when you walk out into the prison yard tomorrow, they’re heading higher again?

Did you know that the Fractal Gods just told me to buy some Brent Oil (BNO) on sale this morning? They’re telling me to buy some Large Cap Energy (XLE) exposure too.

What else would Macro Aware “Shot Callers” in the prison-yard have noticed this morning?

Yield Curve just got smashed to new #Quad2 Cycle Lows at +19bps wide on 10s minus 2s

Both USD and UST 2yr Yield Signals are signaling higher-lows and higher-highs for #Quad2

Send me one young USA-only Captain Stock Picker fish who's feeling sweet about our Bullish TREND Signal on NVDA today… and can also explain Yield Curve to Currency Signals within a Quad Shift… and I might hire them.
